name: Classic Buttermilk Biscuits
description: Tall and flaky hand-cut biscuits made with cold butter and tangy buttermilk for perfect layers.
ingredients: 9 tbsp cold unsalted butter cut into small chunks
instructions: Heat oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar together in a large bowl.
Work cold butter into dry ingredients with fingertips or pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse meal with pea-sized chunks.
Add buttermilk and stir until large craggy clumps form; knead briefly until dough just holds together.
Transfer dough to floured counter and pat to 3/4-inch thickness.
Cut rounds with a 2-inch cutter pressing straight down without twisting; re-roll scraps once.
Place biscuits 2 inches apart on prepared sheet and bake 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown on top.
Cool slightly and serve warm.

name: Classic Scones
description: Tender wedge-shaped scones with a crisp exterior and soft crumb ready in under an hour.
ingredients: 8 tbsp cold unsalted butter cut into pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F with rack in upper third; line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Work butter into dry ingredients with fingertips until mixture is unevenly crumbly with some pea-sized pieces remaining.
Whisk sour cream, egg, and vanilla together; add to flour mixture and stir until dough comes together.
Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface and press gently into a 1-inch-thick round.
Cut into 6 wedges with a bench scraper; place on prepared sheet with space between them.
Brush tops with milk and sprinkle with coarse sugar; freeze pan 15 minutes.
Bake 18 to 23 minutes until light golden brown; cool briefly and serve warm.

name: Ham and Cheddar Savory Scones
description: Savory scones loaded with sharp cheddar and ham with a hint of garlic and fresh chive.
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl; stir in chives and cheddar.
Grate frozen butter with a box grater into flour mixture; toss to coat.
Whisk 2/3 cup buttermilk and egg yolk together; pour over flour mixture and add ham then mix until dough clumps together.
Turn onto a floured surface and press into an 8-inch disc; cut into 8 wedges.
Whisk egg white with 1 tbsp buttermilk; brush tops of scones.
Refrigerate scones on a lined baking sheet for at least 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F; bake scones 22 to 25 minutes until golden brown around edges.
Cool for a few minutes on baking sheet before serving warm.

name: Big and Bubbly Focaccia
description: Crispy-edged oven focaccia with an open crumb dimpled with olive oil and flaky salt.
instructions: Whisk together flour, salt, sugar, and yeast in a large bowl; add water and 2 tbsp olive oil and stir until no dry patches remain.
Cover bowl and set aside for 15 minutes; perform a bowl fold by lifting and pressing dough inward around the bowl then flip dough smooth side up.
Repeat bowl fold 3 more times at 15-minute intervals; cover and let dough rise at room temperature 1 hour until nearly doubled.
Spray a 9-inch square pan with nonstick spray; add 1 tbsp olive oil and tilt to coat.
Transfer dough to pan flipping it to coat in oil; cover and let rise at warm room temperature 1 to 1.5 hours until marshmallowy.
Preheat oven to 475°F with racks in upper and lower thirds.
Oil fingers and dimple dough thoroughly from edge to edge; drizzle remaining olive oil over surface and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Bake on lower rack 15 to 18 minutes until golden; lift out with parchment and return to oven directly on rack 5 to 7 more minutes to crisp sides.

name: Overnight Cinnamon Rolls
description: Pillowy enriched dough rolls with cinnamon sugar filling and cream cheese frosting made ahead overnight.
ingredients: 6 tbsp unsalted butter very soft for filling
2/3 cup light brown sugar for filling
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, brown sugar, and salt in stand mixer bowl; pour in warm milk and add eggs.
Mix with dough hook until dough forms then add softened butter gradually and knead 8 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky.
Cover bowl and let rest 15 minutes; punch down and roll dough into a 14x18-inch rectangle.
Spread very soft butter over dough leaving a 1/2-inch border; mix brown sugar and cinnamon then sprinkle evenly over butter.
Roll up tightly from the long side; cut into 12 equal rolls and place in a greased 9x13-inch or round pan.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight 8 to 12 hours.
Remove from fridge and let rolls come to room temperature and proof for 1 to 1.5 hours until puffed.
Preheat oven to 350°F; bake 22 to 25 minutes until golden.
Beat cream cheese with powdered sugar and milk until smooth; spread over warm rolls.

name: Homemade Soft Pretzels
description: Chewy hand-shaped pretzels with a deeply golden crust from a baking soda bath.
instructions: Whisk yeast and sugar into warm water; cover and let sit 1 minute until foamy.
Whisk in melted butter and salt; add 3 cups flour and mix with a wooden spoon or dough hook until combined.
Add remaining 3/4 cup flour until dough is slightly tacky and pulls away from sides; knead 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let dough rest 10 to 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F; line 2 baking sheets with parchment.
Divide dough into 8 pieces about 75g each; roll each into a 20-to-22-inch rope and form into pretzel shape.
Bring baking soda and 9 cups water to a boil; drop pretzels in one at a time for 20 to 30 seconds then lift out and place on baking sheet.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with coarse salt; bake 12 to 15 minutes until deep golden brown.

name: Blueberry Muffins
description: Domed bakery-style blueberry muffins with a crunchy turbinado sugar top and yogurt-enriched crumb.
instructions: Heat oven to 375°F; line a muffin tin with 9 paper liners and spray with nonstick spray.
Melt butter in a large bowl; whisk in granulated sugar, lemon zest, yogurt, and egg until smooth.
Whisk in baking powder, baking soda, and salt until fully combined.
Fold in flour and blueberries gently; batter will be very thick like cookie dough.
Divide batter between prepared cups filling nearly to top.
Sprinkle each muffin with 1 tsp turbinado sugar.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until tops are golden and a tester inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes then transfer to a rack.

name: Morning Glory Muffins
description: Hearty muffins packed with carrots and apple and coconut for a nourishing portable breakfast.
ingredients: 1/2 cup raisins soaked in hot water
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F; line a 12-cup muffin tin with papers and grease insides.
Cover raisins with hot water in a small bowl and set aside to soak.
Whisk together flour, brown sugar, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, and salt in a large bowl.
Stir in carrots, apple, coconut, and walnuts.
Beat eggs, oil, vanilla, and orange juice together in a separate bowl.
Add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and stir until evenly moistened.
Drain raisins and fold in; divide batter among muffin cups filling nearly to the top.
Bake 25 to 28 minutes until nicely domed and a tester comes out clean; cool 5 minutes in pan then transfer to a rack.

name: Maple Corn Muffins
description: Lightly sweet corn muffins made with real maple syrup and a tender golden crumb.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F; lightly grease a 12-cup standard muffin pan or line with papers.
Whisk together flour, cornmeal, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl.
Whisk together milk, maple syrup, maple extract, and egg in another bowl.
Pour liquid all at once into flour mixture and stir quickly and gently until just combined.
Once barely combined, stir in melted butter.
Scoop batter into prepared pan filling cups about 2/3 full.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes until a toothpick in a center muffin comes out clean and tops spring back lightly.
Remove from oven and transfer to a rack; serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Classic Banana Bread
description: Classic one-bowl banana bread with walnuts and warm spice that bakes up moist and tender.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups mashed very ripe bananas about 3 large
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F; lightly grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl stir together butter, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, baking soda, baking powder, and salt vigorously for 2 to 3 minutes until smooth.
Add mashed bananas, honey, and eggs and stir until combined; some lumps are fine.
Add flour and walnuts and stir just until smooth.
Spoon batter into prepared pan and smooth top; let rest at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Bake for 45 minutes then loosely tent with foil to prevent over-browning.
Bake an additional 25 minutes until a toothpick inserted in center comes out with just a few moist crumbs.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes then turn out onto a rack to cool completely before slicing.

name: Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Bread
description: Deeply spiced pumpkin loaf studded with chocolate chips and baked to a moist dense crumb.
instructions: Position oven rack in lower third and preheat to 350°F; grease a 9x5-inch metal loaf pan.
Whisk flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, ginger, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk eggs, granulated sugar, and brown sugar together in a medium bowl until combined.
Whisk in pumpkin, oil, and orange juice.
Pour wet ingredients into dry and mix gently with a rubber spatula until just combined with a few lumps.
Fold in chocolate chips then pour into prepared pan.
Bake 60 to 65 minutes covering loosely with foil halfway through; bread is done when a toothpick in center comes out clean.
Cool completely in pan on a wire rack before slicing and serving.

name: Simple Zucchini Bread
description: Warmly spiced zucchini loaf with a crunchy brown sugar top and consistently moist tender crumb.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; lightly grease an 8.5x4.5-inch loaf pan.
Beat together brown sugar, apple juice, oil, eggs, and vanilla in a medium bowl until smooth.
Whisk baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon into flour then add to wet ingredients stirring gently until smooth.
Gently pat shredded zucchini dry with paper towels then stir in zucchini and walnuts.
Scoop batter into prepared pan smoothing top; sprinkle with 1 tbsp brown sugar.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes until a toothpick in center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes then turn out onto a rack.
For best results do not slice until completely cool; store wrapped at room temperature.

name: Honey Butter Cheddar Biscuits
description: Flaky layered cheddar biscuits baked in a skillet and finished with a warm honey garlic butter glaze.
ingredients: 4 tbsp salted butter for honey butter
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F; rub a 10-inch cast iron skillet with butter.
Combine flour, baking powder, garlic powder, and salt in a bowl; mix in grated butter and cheddar with hands until combined.
Pour in milk and honey and mix until just combined.
Turn dough onto a floured surface and pat into a 1-inch-thick rectangle; fold one side in like a letter then fold other side over; repeat fold once more.
Cut into 3-inch rounds with a biscuit cutter; re-roll scraps and cut more.
Arrange biscuits in prepared skillet and brush tops with milk.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes until golden brown.
Melt 4 tbsp butter with honey and parsley; spoon over warm biscuits and sprinkle with sea salt.

name: Fruit Galette
description: Rustic free-form tart with a buttery yogurt pastry crust and a jammy seasonal fruit filling.
ingredients: 8 tbsp cold unsalted butter cut into pieces
1/4 cup plain yogurt or sour cream
3 1/2 cups seasonal fruit berries or stone fruit sliced
1 large egg beaten with 1 tsp water
instructions: Combine flour, salt, and sugar in a large bowl; cut in cold butter with a pastry blender until pieces resemble small peas.
Stir in yogurt and 3 tbsp cold water until large clumps form; add last tbsp water if needed.
Bring dough together into a flat disc on parchment; wrap and chill in fridge 1 to 2 hours until firm.
Combine fruit, sugar, tapioca starch, salt, and lemon juice in a bowl and toss.
Heat oven to 400°F; roll dough on floured counter into a 14-inch round and transfer on parchment to a baking sheet.
Spoon filling into center leaving a 2 to 3 inch border; fold border over fruit pleating as needed.
Brush crust with egg wash and sprinkle turbinado sugar over crust and fruit.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden all over and fruit is bubbling; cool at least 20 minutes before serving.

name: Zucchini Ricotta Galette
description: Savory free-form tart with a creamy ricotta base topped with thinly sliced zucchini and fresh basil.
ingredients: 8 tbsp cold unsalted butter cut into cubes
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Whisk flour and salt in a large bowl; cut in cold butter until mixture resembles coarse meal.
Whisk sour cream, lemon juice, and water together; stir into flour mixture until large lumps form.
Gather into a disc wrap in parchment and chill 1 to 2 hours.
Spread zucchini slices on paper towels; salt and let drain 30 minutes then blot dry.
Whisk olive oil and garlic; mix ricotta, Parmesan, mozzarella, and 1 tsp garlic oil; season with salt and pepper.
Heat oven to 400°F; roll dough on floured surface into a 12-inch round and transfer to parchment-lined baking sheet.
Spread ricotta mixture over dough leaving a 2-inch border; shingle zucchini in concentric circles; drizzle remaining garlic oil over top.
Fold border over filling pleating edges; brush crust with egg yolk glaze; bake 30 to 40 minutes until golden.
Sprinkle with basil; let stand 5 minutes then slide onto serving plate.

name: Homemade Croissants
description: Buttery laminated pastry croissants with dozens of flaky layers shaped and baked golden over two days.
ingredients: 2 cups unsalted butter cold for lamination
2 tbsp all-purpose flour for butter layer
1 tbsp whole milk for egg wash
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, salt, and yeast in stand mixer bowl with dough hook; add softened butter then slowly pour in warm milk and knead on medium 3 minutes until smooth.
Shape dough into a rectangle; wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour or overnight.
Beat cold butter with 2 tbsp flour until smooth; flatten into an 8x5-inch rectangle between parchment; chill 30 minutes.
Roll dough into a 10x20-inch rectangle; place butter block in center and fold dough over enclosing it completely.
Roll into a large rectangle; fold into thirds like a letter (1st turn); wrap and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Repeat rolling and folding 2 more times with 30-minute rests between; refrigerate 4 hours or overnight.
Roll dough into an 8x20-inch rectangle; cut into 16 triangles and roll each from wide end to point; curve ends inward.
Place on lined baking sheets; let proof at room temperature 1 hour then refrigerate 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 400°F; brush croissants with egg wash; bake 20 minutes until deep golden brown.

name: Homemade Bagels
description: Dense chewy New York-style bagels boiled in a honey water bath and baked until dark golden.
ingredients: 1 tbsp barley malt syrup or sugar
1 tbsp barley malt syrup or honey for water bath
1 large egg beaten for egg wash
2 tbsp sesame seeds or poppy seeds for topping
instructions: Whisk warm water, yeast, and barley malt syrup together in stand mixer bowl; let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Add flour and salt; beat with dough hook on medium speed 2 minutes until stiff dough forms; knead 6 to 7 minutes.
Place dough in a greased bowl; cover and let rise 1.5 to 2 hours until doubled.
Punch down dough and divide into 8 equal pieces; shape each into a ball then poke a hole through center and stretch to 1.5-to-2-inch diameter.
Let shaped bagels rest 5 to 10 minutes; preheat oven to 425°F and line 2 baking sheets.
Bring 2 quarts water with barley malt syrup to a boil; drop 2 to 3 bagels at a time and boil 1 minute per side.
Lift out with a slotted spatula; brush with egg wash and dip tops in seeds.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes rotating pans halfway until bagels are dark golden brown; cool on sheets 20 minutes.

name: English Muffins
description: Griddle-cooked yeasted muffins with signature nooks and crannies perfect for toasting.
instructions: Make preferment by whisking together bread flour, yeast, milk, and water until smooth; cover and rest at room temperature 1 to 4 hours until bubbly.
Add flour, salt, sugar, and butter to preferment and mix by hand into a soft sticky dough.
Perform bowl folds reaching under dough and stretching up and over; flip smooth side up and round; cover and rest 1 hour.
Perform another bowl fold; cover and rest 1 more hour until very puffy.
Turn dough onto a cornmeal-dusted surface; gently deflate and pat into a 1/2-inch-thick circle.
Cut into 3.5-inch rounds with a cutter; gather scraps and cut again to yield 6 muffins; dust tops with cornmeal and let rest 20 to 30 minutes until puffy.
Heat a cast iron skillet over medium-low; cook muffins undisturbed 10 to 15 minutes per side until bottoms are lightly browned and sides look matte.
Cool completely then fork-split before toasting and serving with butter.

name: Popovers
description: Dramatic hollow egg-based rolls with a crisp golden shell and airy steam-puffed interior.
ingredients: 2 tbsp unsalted butter softened for serving
1 tbsp honey or maple syrup for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F with rack on a lower shelf; grease all 12 cups and surrounding surface of a standard muffin tin.
Whisk eggs, milk, and salt together until smooth and evenly yellow with no streaks.
Add flour all at once and beat with a wire whisk until frothy and mostly smooth; stir in melted butter.
Let batter rest 15 minutes; whisk briefly again to recombine any lumps.
Pour batter into greased muffin cups filling 2/3 to 3/4 full; place pan on lower oven rack.
Bake at 450°F for 20 minutes without opening the oven door.
Reduce heat to 350°F and bake an additional 10 to 15 minutes until deep golden brown.
Pierce top of each popover with a knife tip to release steam; remove from pan and serve immediately.

name: Pita Bread
description: Soft golden pita rounds that puff dramatically in a hot oven to create a perfect pocket.
instructions: Dissolve yeast and sugar in 1 cup warm water; let sit 5 to 10 minutes until foamy.
Combine flour and salt in a large bowl; add yeast mixture and olive oil and stir until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a floured surface for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic; add water 1 tbsp at a time if dough is too stiff.
Place dough in a greased bowl; cover and let rise 1 to 1.5 hours at warm room temperature until doubled.
Punch down dough and divide into 8 equal pieces; roll each into a smooth ball then flatten into a 6-inch round about 1/4-inch thick.
Let rounds rest on a floured surface for 20 minutes covered with a towel.
Preheat oven to 500°F with a baking stone or inverted baking sheet on the middle rack for at least 30 minutes.
Bake pita rounds in batches for 3 to 5 minutes until puffed and just lightly colored; wrap in a towel to keep soft.

name: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
description: Classic chewy oatmeal cookies with golden raisins and a hint of cinnamon and nutmeg.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; line two baking sheets with parchment.
Beat butter, granulated sugar, brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and vinegar until fairly smooth.
Beat in egg until smooth.
Add baking soda and flour and beat until well incorporated.
Stir in oats and raisins until evenly combined.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto prepared baking sheets leaving 2 inches between cookies.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes rotating pans halfway through until light golden brown with slightly darker edges.
Sprinkle lightly with salt immediately from oven; cool on pan then transfer to a rack.

name: Soft Dinner Rolls
description: Pillowy pull-apart yeasted dinner rolls brushed with honey butter and baked until golden.
ingredients: 2 tbsp unsalted butter melted for brushing
instructions: Whisk 1/4 cup warm milk, yeast, and 1 tsp honey in stand mixer bowl; cover and let sit 5 to 10 minutes until foamy.
Add remaining honey, egg, egg yolk, 4 tbsp melted butter, 3 cups flour, salt, and 3/4 cup warm milk; mix with dough hook on low 1 minute then add remaining 1/2 cup flour.
Mix on low 1 minute then increase to medium-low and knead 8 minutes until soft and slightly tacky dough forms.
Shape into a ball in a greased bowl; cover and let rise 1 to 1.5 hours at warm room temperature until doubled.
Punch down dough and divide into 12 equal pieces; shape each into a smooth ball.
Arrange balls in a greased 9x13-inch baking dish; cover and let rise 45 minutes until puffed and touching.
Preheat oven to 350°F; bake rolls 18 to 22 minutes until tops are golden brown.
Stir 2 tbsp melted butter with 1 tbsp honey and brush over warm rolls; serve immediately.

name: Shortbread Cookies
description: Crisp buttery shortbread with a melt-in-the-mouth texture from a simple four-ingredient dough.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F; line two baking sheets with parchment.
Whisk flour, powdered sugar, and salt together in a food processor; add cold butter and vanilla.
Pulse until dough just comes together into a ball that holds when squeezed.
Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface; roll to 1/4-inch thickness.
Cut into rectangles or rounds with a cookie cutter or knife; place on prepared baking sheets 1 inch apart.
Sprinkle with coarse sugar and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes until edges are just barely golden; centers should look pale.
Cool completely on baking sheets before transferring; cookies firm up as they cool.

name: Flaky All-Butter Pie Crust
description: Shatteringly crisp pie crust made by smashing cold butter flat into flour for incredible flaky layers.
ingredients: 2 tbsp cold vodka or additional water
1 large egg beaten with 1 tsp water for egg wash
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, and salt together in a medium bowl.
Toss cold butter cubes into flour mixture to coat; using fingertips smash each cube flat without rubbing or cutting.
Stir in cold water until dough comes together into a shaggy ball; dough temperature should be 65 to 70°F.
On a generously floured surface roll dough into a roughly 10x15-inch rectangle.
Fold the 10-inch sides to the center then close like a book; fold in half again bringing short sides together to create a thick block.
Divide in half with a bench scraper; flatten each half into a disc.
Wrap each disc in plastic wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour or up to 3 days before rolling.
Roll out as needed on a floured surface to 1/8-inch thickness; fit into pie plate and crimp edges before filling and baking.

name: Quiche Lorraine
description: Classic French custard quiche with caramelized leeks, ham, and Gruyere in a buttery pastry shell.
ingredients: 8 tbsp cold unsalted butter cut into small pieces
4 leeks white and pale green parts thinly sliced
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine flour, cornstarch, and 1/4 tsp salt in a bowl; cut butter in until very tiny bits form then mix in 1 egg until dough forms.
On a floured surface roll dough into a 12-inch circle; fit into a 9-inch pie plate crimp edges and refrigerate 30 minutes.
Saute leeks in olive oil over low heat 30 to 40 minutes until caramelized; remove from heat and cool.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix heavy cream and sour cream together; whisk in 3 eggs and season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Spread leek mixture evenly over pastry shell; scatter ham then cheese over leeks.
Pour custard over filling; bake in upper third of oven 25 to 30 minutes until puffed and golden.
Remove from oven; cool on rack for 10 minutes before slicing and serving warm or at room temperature.

name: Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Brown butter chocolate chip cookies with crisp edges and a thick chewy center.
ingredients: 2 cups chopped bittersweet chocolate or chips
instructions: Brown butter in a large saucepan over medium heat until golden and nutty-smelling; remove from heat and let cool until solidified but not hard about 1 hour in fridge.
Preheat oven to 375°F; line baking sheets with parchment.
Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt together in a medium bowl.
Beat cooled brown butter with granulated and brown sugars in stand mixer until fluffy; add eggs one at a time then beat in vanilla.
Add flour mixture and mix on low until just combined; fold in chocolate.
Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough onto prepared baking sheets leaving 2 inches between.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes until golden around edges but still slightly soft in centers.
Sprinkle with flaky salt immediately; cool on baking sheet 5 minutes then transfer to rack.

name: Soft Sandwich Bread
description: Tender everyday sandwich loaf with a fine crumb from enriched dough and a glossy golden crust.
ingredients: 1 tbsp unsalted butter melted for brushing
instructions: Whisk warm milk, yeast, and honey in stand mixer bowl; let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Add flour, salt, softened butter, and egg; knead with dough hook on medium speed for 8 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky.
Shape into a ball in a greased bowl; cover and let rise at warm room temperature 1 to 1.5 hours until doubled.
Punch down dough and shape into a log; press into a greased 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Cover and let rise 45 to 60 minutes until dough crowns 1 inch above pan rim.
Preheat oven to 350°F; brush top of loaf gently with melted butter.
Bake 28 to 32 minutes until golden brown and loaf sounds hollow when tapped; internal temperature should read 190°F.
Turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely before slicing.

name: Classic Cornbread
description: Moist golden cornbread with a tender crumb baked in a cast iron skillet until lightly crisp at edges.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F; lightly grease a 9-inch square pan or cast iron skillet.
Whisk together flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl.
Whisk together milk, melted butter, vegetable oil, and egg in another bowl.
Pour liquid ingredients all at once into dry ingredients and stir quickly and gently just until combined; do not overmix.
Spread batter into prepared pan.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until edges begin to pull away from pan and a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Remove from oven and cool on a rack for 5 minutes.
Cut into squares and serve warm; store leftovers wrapped at room temperature.

name: Chocolate Chunk Coconut Banana Bread
description: Moist banana bread made with coconut oil and honey and loaded with dark chocolate chunks throughout.
ingredients: 4 medium very ripe bananas mashed about 1 1/4 cups
1 cup semi-sweet or dark chocolate chunks
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl stir together mashed bananas, coconut oil, honey, eggs, and vanilla until combined.
Add flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt and mix until just combined; do not overmix.
Fold in chocolate chunks.
Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes until center is just set and a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.
Remove from oven and let cool in pan for at least 30 minutes before cutting.
Serve warm with a smear of butter or drizzle of honey.

name: Cream Biscuits
description: Ultra-simple heavy cream biscuits with just four ingredients that bake up golden and tender in minutes.
ingredients: 3 tbsp unsalted butter melted for dipping
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F; line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Sift flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar into a large bowl.
Fold in 1 1/4 cups heavy cream until dough is soft and just holds together; add remaining cream 1 tbsp at a time if dough is too dry.
Turn dough onto a floured surface and press to a thickness of about 3/4 inch.
Cut rounds with a 2.5-inch round cutter; gather scraps gently and cut more rounds.
Melt butter in a small dish; dip the top of each round in melted butter then place butter side up on prepared baking sheet.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes until golden brown.
Serve immediately or flash freeze unbaked rounds for future baking.

name: Classic White Sandwich Bread
description: Soft and fluffy white sandwich bread baked to golden perfection in the bread machine on the Basic cycle.
instructions: Add water and oil to the bread machine pan.
Add salt and sugar.
Spoon in the bread flour on top covering the liquid completely.
Make a small well in the flour and add the yeast making sure it does not touch the salt.
Insert pan into machine and select Basic/White cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust.
When cycle is complete remove pan with oven mitts and shake loaf out onto a wire rack.
Cool at least 30 minutes before slicing.

name: 100% Whole Wheat Bread
description: Hearty whole wheat loaf made entirely with whole wheat flour on the Whole Wheat cycle.
instructions: Add warm water honey and butter to the bread machine pan.
Add salt and vital wheat gluten.
Spoon whole wheat flour on top of the liquids.
Make a small well in the flour and add the yeast keeping it away from the salt.
Select the Whole Wheat cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust and press Start.
Check dough after 10 minutes of kneading and add water or flour 1 tbsp at a time if needed.
When baking cycle completes remove loaf and cool on a wire rack for 1 hour before slicing.

name: Bread Machine Sourdough Bread
description: Tangy sourdough-style bread using active starter made on the French Bread cycle for a long slow rise.
instructions: Add sourdough starter and warm water to the bread machine pan.
Add salt and sugar on top of the liquid.
Spoon bread flour over the liquids covering them completely.
Make a small indent in the flour and add yeast.
Select the French Bread cycle or a similar long-rising cycle on your machine and press Start.
Check dough consistency after 10 minutes of kneading and adjust with water or flour as needed.
Remove loaf when cycle finishes and cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.

name: French Bread
description: Crusty classic French bread made in the bread machine using the Basic cycle with a crackly crust.
instructions: Beat egg whites with a whisk for 2 to 3 minutes until frothy and bubbly.
Pour beaten egg whites and water into the bread machine pan.
Add flour on top covering the liquid completely.
Make a small well in flour and add sugar and salt on one side and yeast on the opposite side.
Select Basic White cycle with medium crust and press Start.
Watch the first few minutes of kneading; add 1 tbsp water if dough is dry or 1 tbsp flour if too wet.
Allow machine to complete cycle then remove loaf and cool on a wire rack at least 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Honey Oat Bread
description: Lightly sweet honey oat bread made with old-fashioned rolled oats on the Basic cycle.
instructions: Add warm water milk honey and butter to the bread machine pan.
Add salt then spoon flour on top of the liquid ingredients.
Add rolled oats on top of the flour.
Make a small well in the flour mixture and add yeast keeping it away from salt.
Select Basic White cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust and press Start.
Check dough ball after 5 minutes of kneading and add water or flour as needed.
When cycle is complete remove loaf and cool on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Cinnamon Raisin Bread
description: Sweet cinnamon-scented bread studded with plump raisins perfect for breakfast toast.
instructions: Add warm milk water butter eggs and vanilla to the bread machine pan.
Spoon flour on top of the liquid ingredients.
Add sugar cinnamon and salt and make a small well for the yeast in the flour keeping salt and yeast separated.
Select Basic or Sweet cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf and press Start.
Add raisins when the machine beeps during the mix-in phase or about 5 minutes before the end of the second kneading cycle.
When cycle is complete remove pan with oven mitts and turn loaf out onto a wire rack.
Cool completely before slicing for best texture.

name: Rye Bread with Caraway
description: Earthy caraway rye bread with a hearty crumb made on the Basic or Rye cycle in the bread machine.
instructions: Add water olive oil and molasses to the bread machine pan.
Add salt then spoon rye flour and all-purpose flour on top.
Sprinkle caraway seeds over the flour.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast.
Select the Rye Bread setting or Whole Wheat setting for a 1.5 lb loaf and press Start.
Allow machine to complete all cycles.
Remove loaf from pan and cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Multigrain Seeded Loaf
description: Nutty multigrain bread packed with seeds and whole grains baked on the Whole Wheat cycle.
instructions: Add warm water olive oil and honey to the bread machine pan.
Add salt then spoon bread flour and whole wheat flour on top.
Add oats flaxseed sunflower seeds and millet on top of the flour.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast.
Select Whole Wheat cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust and press Start.
After 10 minutes of kneading check dough consistency and add water or flour 1 tbsp at a time as needed.
Cool loaf completely on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Italian Herb and Olive Oil Bread
description: Fragrant Italian herb bread made with olive oil rosemary and garlic on the Basic cycle.
instructions: Add warm water and olive oil to the bread machine pan.
Add salt garlic powder and dried herbs.
Spoon bread flour on top then add sugar.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast keeping it away from the salt.
Select Basic/White cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust and press Start.
Check dough ball after 5 minutes of kneading and adjust hydration if needed.
Remove baked loaf and cool on a wire rack at least 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Pumpernickel Dark Rye Bread
description: Rich dark pumpernickel bread with molasses and cocoa powder made on the Basic cycle.
instructions: Add warm water and oil to the bread machine pan.
Add salt and brown sugar.
Spoon bread flour whole wheat flour and dark rye flour on top.
Add cocoa powder and instant coffee over the flour.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast.
Select Basic cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust and press Start.
Once baking cycle is complete remove loaf from pan and cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Gluten-Free White Bread
description: Light and fluffy gluten-free white bread made with gluten-free bread flour on the Gluten-Free cycle.
instructions: Add warm water melted butter eggs and apple cider vinegar to the bread machine pan.
Whisk together gluten-free flour sugar salt and yeast in a bowl.
Add the dry ingredient mixture on top of the liquid ingredients without stirring.
Select Gluten-Free cycle or Basic cycle with dark crust setting and press Start.
Allow machine to complete the full cycle without opening the lid.
Remove pan with oven mitts and turn loaf out onto a wire rack.
Cool completely before slicing for best texture and structure.

name: Banana Bread
description: Moist and tender banana bread made with ripe bananas using the bread machine on the Quick Bread cycle.
instructions: Mash ripe bananas well in a bowl and set aside.
Add melted butter sugar eggs and vanilla to the bread machine pan first.
Add mashed bananas and stir lightly to combine with the wet ingredients.
Spoon flour on top then add baking soda baking powder salt and cinnamon.
Select the Quick Bread or Cake cycle on your machine and press Start.
When cycle is complete check center with a toothpick; it should come out clean.
Remove bread from pan and cool on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Beer Bread
description: Savory yeast beer bread made with amber ale and whole wheat flour on the Basic cycle.
instructions: Pour beer into the bread machine pan followed by sugar and oil.
Spoon bread flour and whole wheat flour on top of the liquid ingredients.
Sprinkle salt around the edges of the flour and make a small well in the center for the yeast.
Select Basic or White Bread cycle with medium or dark crust and press Start.
Check dough ball after 5 minutes of kneading and add flour if batter is too wet.
When cycle is complete promptly remove loaf from pan.
Cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Focaccia Dough
description: Pillowy olive oil focaccia with rosemary and sea salt using the bread machine Dough cycle.
instructions: Add water and onion to the bread machine pan.
Spoon flour on top then add sugar making two small wells in the flour for salt and yeast separately.
Select Dough cycle and press Start.
When dough cycle is complete generously brush a baking sheet with olive oil and turn dough out onto it.
Use oiled fingers to press dough out to about 1 inch thick.
Cover with plastic wrap and let rise 40 minutes until doubled.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Dimple dough with fingers drizzle with olive oil sprinkle with rosemary and sea salt then bake 20-25 minutes until golden brown.

name: Pizza Dough
description: Classic chewy pizza crust made in the bread machine on the Dough cycle ready to top and bake.
instructions: Add warm water to the bread machine pan.
Add olive oil then spoon flour on top covering the liquid.
Add sugar and salt making a small well in the flour for the yeast keeping it away from the salt.
Select Dough cycle and press Start.
After cycle is complete turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface.
Divide into portions and roll out to desired thickness.
Top with sauce and toppings and bake at 400-425°F for 18-25 minutes until cheese is bubbly and crust is golden.

name: Soft Pretzel Dough
description: Chewy homemade soft pretzels made using the bread machine Dough cycle then boiled and baked.
ingredients: 1 tbsp unsalted butter cut into pieces
2 tbsp coarse sea salt for topping
instructions: Add water butter sugar and salt to the bread machine pan.
Spoon flour on top and make a small well for the yeast.
Select Dough cycle and press Start. Allow 1.5 hours.
Remove dough and chill wrapped in plastic wrap in refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Divide dough into 8 pieces and roll each into an 18-20 inch rope. Form into pretzel shapes.
Bring 6 cups water and baking soda to a rapid boil. Boil pretzels for 30 seconds per side then transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Brush with egg wash sprinkle with coarse salt and bake at 425°F for 12-15 minutes until golden brown.

name: Hamburger Buns
description: Soft golden hamburger buns made with the bread machine Dough cycle then shaped and baked.
instructions: Add egg milk water butter sugar and salt to the bread machine pan in order listed.
Spoon flour on top and make a small well for the yeast.
Select Dough cycle and press Start.
When cycle is complete transfer dough to a floured surface and divide into 8 equal pieces.
Shape each piece into a ball and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet flattening each to about 1/2 inch thick.
Cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled about 30-35 minutes.
Brush with egg wash sprinkle with sesame seeds and bake at 400°F for 10-12 minutes until golden brown. Cool on wire rack.

name: Challah Bread
description: Rich golden egg bread with honey and olive oil made on the Basic cycle in the bread machine.
instructions: Add water eggs egg yolk honey and olive oil to the bread machine pan.
Spoon flour on top covering the liquid ingredients.
Create a small well in the flour and nestle the salt on one side and yeast on the other.
Select Basic cycle with medium crust setting for a 2 lb loaf and press Start.
Optional: during the final rise just before baking open lid and brush top with egg white and sprinkle poppy seeds.
Allow cycle to complete fully.
Remove loaf from pan and cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Honey Whole Wheat Bread
description: Sweet whole wheat honey bread with a soft tender crumb made on the Basic or Whole Wheat cycle.
instructions: Warm milk to 80°F. Add milk water oil honey and egg to the bread machine pan.
Spoon bread flour and whole wheat flour on top of the liquid ingredients.
Add salt and make a small well for the yeast in the flour.
Select Basic cycle with medium crust for a 1.5 lb loaf and press Start.
Check dough consistency after 5 minutes of kneading; it should be a soft tacky ball. Adjust with water or flour 1 tbsp at a time if needed.
When cycle is complete remove bread and cool on a wire rack.
Store wrapped at room temperature for up to 4 days.

name: Oatmeal Bread
description: Moist hearty oatmeal bread with a tender crumb baked on the Basic cycle for perfect everyday slices.
instructions: Add warm water and butter to the bread machine pan.
Add brown sugar honey and salt.
Spoon rolled oats into pan then cover with bread flour.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast keeping it away from the salt.
Select Basic/White cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust and press Start.
After about 10 minutes of kneading check dough; adjust with water or flour 1 tbsp at a time if needed.
Remove loaf when done and cool on a wire rack at least 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Brioche Bread
description: Rich buttery brioche with a tender golden crumb made in the bread machine on the Sweet cycle.
ingredients: 8 tbsp unsalted butter softened and cut into pieces
instructions: Add warm water and eggs to the bread machine pan.
Distribute pieces of softened butter evenly over the liquid.
Spoon flour on top then add dry milk powder and sugar.
Make a well in the flour adding salt on one side and yeast on the other.
Select Sweet or Basic cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf and press Start.
Check dough after 10 minutes; the dough should be soft and slightly sticky. Add flour 1 tbsp at a time if too wet.
Cool loaf on a wire rack for at least 1 hour before slicing for best texture.

name: Rosemary Garlic Focaccia Dough
description: Aromatic rosemary and roasted garlic focaccia made via the Dough cycle then dimpled and baked in olive oil.
ingredients: 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil plus more for pan
1/4 tsp flaky sea salt for topping
instructions: Add warm water and 2 tbsp olive oil to the bread machine pan.
Add roasted garlic then spoon flour on top.
Add sugar and salt in small wells in the flour and add yeast separately.
Select Dough cycle and press Start.
Once dough cycle is complete oil an 18x13 inch baking pan generously. Turn dough out and stretch it into the pan.
Cover and let rise 30 minutes. Dimple dough with fingertips drizzle with remaining olive oil and scatter rosemary and flaky salt on top.
Bake at 425°F for 20-25 minutes until light golden brown. Serve warm.

name: Multigrain Honey Bread
description: Hearty bread made with multiple flours rolled oats and millet sweetened with honey on the Whole Wheat cycle.
instructions: Add warm water oil and honey to the bread machine pan.
Add salt then layer in whole wheat flour and bread flour.
Add rolled oats millet and flaxseed meal on top.
Make a small well in the grain mixture and add yeast.
Select Whole Wheat cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf and press Start.
After kneading begins check consistency and add water or flour 1 tbsp at a time if needed.
Remove baked loaf and cool on a rack at least 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Sweet Potato Bread
description: Soft golden bread with mashed sweet potato and warm spices baked on the Basic cycle.
instructions: Add warm water mashed sweet potato butter and honey to the bread machine pan.
Add salt cinnamon and nutmeg.
Spoon bread flour on top covering the liquid.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast keeping it away from salt.
Select Basic cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust and press Start.
Check dough after 10 minutes of kneading; sweet potato adds moisture so add flour 1 tbsp at a time if dough is too sticky.
Cool loaf on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Anadama Bread
description: Old-fashioned New England cornmeal and molasses bread with a chewy crumb made on the Basic cycle.
instructions: Add warm water cornmeal molasses and butter to the bread machine pan.
Add salt then spoon bread flour on top.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast.
Select Basic/White cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with medium crust and press Start.
After 10 minutes of kneading check dough; it should be a soft ball. Add flour 1 tbsp at a time if too sticky.
Allow machine to complete all cycles.
Remove loaf and cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Cheddar Jalapeño Bread
description: Bold and cheesy bread with jalapeño heat baked on the Basic cycle for a crowd-pleasing savory loaf.
instructions: Add warm water and oil to the bread machine pan.
Add sugar and salt then spoon flour on top.
Make a small well in the flour and add yeast.
Select Basic/White cycle and press Start.
Add shredded cheddar and diced jalapeños when the machine beeps for mix-ins or about 5 minutes before the end of the kneading cycle.
Allow machine to complete baking cycle.
Remove loaf and cool completely on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Honey Butter White Bread
description: Ultra-soft enriched white bread with butter and honey for a pillowy rich everyday loaf on the Basic cycle.
instructions: Warm milk to 110°F and add to bread machine pan with butter and honey.
Add egg to the pan.
Spoon flour on top of the liquid ingredients.
Add salt and make a small well in the flour for the yeast.
Select Basic cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf with light or medium crust and press Start.
Check dough consistency after 5 minutes of kneading. Dough should be soft and smooth; adjust with flour or water as needed.
Remove loaf when done and cool on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Pretzel Dough Rolls
description: Chewy homemade pretzel rolls shaped from bread machine dough and baked with a baking soda bath.
instructions: Add warm water butter salt and brown sugar to the bread machine pan.
Spoon flour on top and add yeast in a small well in the flour.
Select Dough cycle and press Start.
Once dough cycle is complete divide dough into 10 equal pieces and shape each into a smooth ball then flatten slightly to 3 inches across.
Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet cover and rest 15 minutes.
Bring 8 cups water and baking soda to a boil. Boil rolls 30 seconds per side then return to baking sheet.
Brush with egg wash cut a cross on top of each roll sprinkle with coarse salt and bake at 400°F for 20-22 minutes until deep golden brown.

name: Sun-Dried Tomato Herb Bread
description: Mediterranean-inspired sun-dried tomato bread with basil and garlic made on the Basic cycle.
ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil from sun-dried tomato jar
instructions: Add warm water and olive oil to the bread machine pan.
Add salt and sugar then spoon flour on top.
Add dried basil oregano and garlic powder and make a small well in the flour for the yeast.
Select Basic cycle for a 1.5 lb loaf and press Start.
Add chopped sun-dried tomatoes when the machine beeps for mix-ins or about 5 minutes before the end of the kneading cycle.
Allow machine to complete full baking cycle.
Remove loaf cool on a wire rack for 30 minutes and slice.

name: Cinnamon Swirl Bread
description: Soft white bread swirled with cinnamon sugar filling made on the Dough cycle then shaped and baked.
instructions: Add warm milk water butter sugar and salt to the bread machine pan.
Spoon flour on top and add yeast in a small well in the flour.
Select Dough cycle and press Start.
When cycle is complete turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and roll into a 9x18 inch rectangle.
Brush with melted butter and sprinkle evenly with cinnamon-sugar filling leaving a 1 inch border on one short end.
Roll tightly from the filled end into a log and pinch seam to seal. Place seam-side down in a greased 9x5 inch loaf pan.
Cover and let rise until domed 1 inch over pan rim about 1 hour. Bake at 350°F for 35-40 minutes until golden and internal temperature reaches 190°F. Cool completely before slicing.

name: Soft Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Thick and chewy chocolate chip cookies with crisp edges and gooey centers.
instructions: Beat butter and sugars on medium speed until creamy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in egg and vanilla; scrape bowl.
Whisk flour, cornstarch, baking soda, and salt; add to wet ingredients on low speed until combined.
Fold in chocolate chips. Cover dough and chill at least 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°F and line baking sheets with parchment. Roll dough into 1.5-tablespoon balls and place 3 inches apart.
Bake 11-12 minutes until barely golden around edges. Cool on baking sheet 5 minutes before transferring.

name: King Arthur Fudge Brownies
description: Dense and fudgy scratch brownies with a shiny crackle top and deep chocolate flavor.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 9x13-inch pan with parchment.
Whisk eggs, cocoa, salt, baking powder, espresso powder, and vanilla in a large bowl until smooth.
Melt butter in a saucepan; stir in sugar and heat to 110-120°F but not bubbling.
Add hot butter-sugar to egg-cocoa mixture and stir until smooth. Stir in flour and chocolate chips.
Cool batter 20 minutes then spread into pan. Bake 28-32 minutes until edges are set and a toothpick shows moist crumbs.
Cool completely on a rack before cutting.

name: Classic New York Cheesecake
description: Silky cream cheese cheesecake on a buttery graham cracker crust baked in a water bath.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Mix crumbs, 1/3 cup sugar, and butter; press into a 9-inch springform pan. Bake crust 8 minutes; cool.
Beat cream cheese and 1 cup sugar until completely smooth, about 2 minutes.
Add sour cream, lemon juice, and vanilla; beat until combined. Add eggs one at a time, beating just until combined.
Pour batter over crust. Wrap pan in heavy-duty foil; place in a roasting pan with 1 inch of boiling water.
Bake 55-70 minutes until edges set and center jiggles slightly. Turn off oven; leave door ajar 1 hour.
Cool on rack; refrigerate at least 4 hours before slicing.

name: Smitten Kitchen Apple Pie
description: Flaky double-crust apple pie with tender spiced filling and a golden pastry shell.
ingredients: 1 cup cold unsalted butter cut into cubes
3 lbs mixed baking apples peeled and sliced
1 large egg beaten with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Pulse flour, salt, and sugar in a food processor. Add cold butter; pulse until pea-sized. Drizzle in ice water 1 tbsp at a time until dough comes together. Divide, flatten, wrap, and refrigerate 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 375°F. Toss apples with sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice.
Roll out one disc to a 12-inch circle and fit into a 9-inch pie plate. Add filling. Roll out second disc; lay over filling. Trim, fold, and crimp edges. Cut vents. Brush with egg wash.
Place on a baking sheet; bake 20 minutes. Reduce to 350°F and bake 40-50 minutes more until crust is golden and juices bubble.
Cool on a wire rack at least 2 hours before slicing.

name: Maple Pecan Pie
description: Rich and buttery pecan pie made with pure maple syrup for a deep caramel flavor.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Blind-bake chilled pie crust with pie weights 15 minutes; remove weights.
Spread pecans evenly inside warm crust. Set aside.
Whisk melted butter, brown sugar, and flour together. Whisk in vanilla, salt, eggs, and maple syrup until combined.
Pour filling evenly over pecans. Shield crust edges with foil.
Bake 40-50 minutes until top is lightly browned. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt immediately.
Cool completely on a wire rack before slicing; filling sets as it cools.

name: Classic Key Lime Pie
description: Tangy and creamy key lime pie with a crisp graham cracker crust and silky custard filling.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F. Mix crumbs, sugar, and butter; press into a 9-inch pie pan. Bake 15 minutes; cool.
Whisk lime zest and egg yolks at high speed 4 minutes until lightened.
Stir in condensed milk; beat at high speed 3 minutes. Add lime juice and stir just to combine.
Pour into crust and bake 25 minutes until set around edges but wobbly in center.
Cool to room temperature then refrigerate at least 3 hours.
Whip cream with powdered sugar to medium peaks. Serve each slice with whipped cream.

name: Smitten Kitchen Lemon Bars
description: Buttery shortbread crust under a bright and tangy lemon curd filling dusted with powdered sugar.
ingredients: 1/2 lb unsalted butter at room temperature
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.
Cream butter and 1/2 cup sugar until light. Mix in 2 cups flour and salt until just combined. Press into pan building up 1/2-inch edges. Refrigerate 15 minutes.
Bake crust 15-20 minutes until very lightly browned. Cool; leave oven on.
Whisk eggs, 2 1/2 cups sugar, lemon zest, lemon juice, and 1 cup flour. Pour over crust.
Bake 30-35 minutes until filling is set. Cool to room temperature.
Cut into rectangles and dust generously with confectioners sugar before serving.

name: Chocolate Lava Cakes
description: Individual molten chocolate cakes with a gooey flowing center for an elegant dinner-party dessert.
instructions: Spray four 6-oz ramekins with nonstick spray and dust with cocoa powder. Preheat oven to 425°F.
Microwave butter and chocolate in 10-second increments until smooth.
Whisk flour, confectioners sugar, and salt in a small bowl. Whisk eggs and yolks in another bowl.
Pour flour mixture and eggs into chocolate mixture; stir with a spatula until smooth and slightly thick.
Divide batter among ramekins on a baking sheet. Bake 12-14 minutes until sides are firm but tops are still soft.
Cool 1 minute then cover each with an inverted plate; flip and let release 10 seconds. Remove ramekin. Serve immediately with ice cream.

name: Classic Tiramisu
description: Luxurious layers of espresso-soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cream dusted with cocoa.
ingredients: 1 cup mascarpone cheese at room temperature
1 oz dark chocolate shaved for garnish
instructions: Beat egg yolks and 1/4 cup sugar until pale yellow and tripled in volume, about 4 minutes. Set aside.
Whip cream and remaining 1/4 cup sugar to soft peaks. Add mascarpone; whip to medium peaks.
Gently fold mascarpone mixture into sweetened yolks until combined.
Combine espresso and rum in a shallow bowl. Dust bottom of an 8x8-inch pan with 1 tbsp cocoa.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger in espresso mixture; arrange in a single layer in the pan. Cover with half the cream.
Repeat with remaining ladyfingers and cream. Dust top with remaining cocoa. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours. Garnish with shaved chocolate.

name: Strawberry Cream Pretzel Tart
description: Honey-cream tart in a pretzel-gingersnap crust swirled with jam and topped with fresh berries.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Pulse pretzels and gingersnaps until fine crumbs. Add melted butter and 2 tbsp honey; pulse until mixture holds together. Press into a 9-inch tart pan with removable bottom. Bake 8 minutes; cool.
Combine cream, 1/3 cup honey, and lemon zest in a large pot over high heat. Bring to a boil; boil 5 minutes. Remove from heat; whisk in lemon juice and vanilla. Cool 10 minutes.
Pour lemon cream into crust. Dollop jam over cream and gently swirl with a knife.
Cover and chill 1.5-2 hours until set.
Before serving remove tart from pan and top with fresh berries. Slice and serve immediately.

name: Vanilla Panna Cotta
description: Silky and wobbly Italian set cream perfumed with vanilla and served with fresh berry coulis.
instructions: Sprinkle gelatin over cold water; let sit 5 minutes to bloom.
Combine cream, milk, and sugar in a saucepan over medium heat; stir until sugar dissolves and mixture just steams. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin, vanilla extract, vanilla bean seeds, and salt until dissolved.
Pour into six lightly oiled 6-oz ramekins. Refrigerate uncovered at least 4 hours or overnight.
Make coulis: simmer raspberries, sugar, and lemon juice 5 minutes. Press through a sieve; cool.
Run a thin knife around edge of each panna cotta and invert onto plates. Spoon berry coulis over top.

name: Old-School Chocolate Mousse
description: Light yet intensely rich chocolate mousse made with whipped egg whites for an airy texture.
instructions: Melt chocolate and butter in a double boiler until smooth. Cool to lukewarm.
Whisk egg yolks and 2 tbsp sugar until pale. Stir into melted chocolate.
Beat egg whites with cream of tartar and salt to soft peaks. Gradually add remaining 2 tbsp sugar; beat to medium-stiff peaks.
Whip heavy cream and vanilla to soft peaks.
Fold one-third of egg whites into chocolate to lighten; fold in remaining whites. Fold in whipped cream.
Spoon into cups; refrigerate at least 2 hours. Serve with additional whipped cream and chocolate shavings.

name: Magic Cookie Bars
description: Seven-layer bars with a graham cracker base and layers of chocolate chips, nuts, coconut, and condensed milk.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line an 8-inch square pan with a parchment sling and grease sides.
Mix graham cracker crumbs and melted butter; press firmly into bottom of pan.
Whisk condensed milk with cocoa powder until smooth; pour over crust.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup chocolate chips, then walnuts, cranberries, and coconut over the top.
Bake 25-30 minutes until coconut is lightly toasted.
Melt remaining chocolate chips and drizzle over bars. Cool 90 minutes at room temperature then refrigerate 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Classic Blondies
description: Chewy brown sugar bars packed with vanilla and chocolate chips finished with flaky sea salt.
ingredients: 14 tbsp unsalted butter melted and slightly cooled
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 9-inch square pan with parchment leaving overhang on the sides.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk melted butter and brown sugar until combined. Whisk in egg, egg yolk, and vanilla.
Pour wet into dry; stir until combined. Fold in chocolate chips. Spread into pan; sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
Bake 30-34 minutes until golden brown with only a few moist crumbs on a toothpick.
Cool completely in pan about 1 hour before lifting out and cutting.

name: Apple Cranberry Crisp
description: Tender spiced apples and tart cranberries baked under a buttery oat-almond streusel topping.
ingredients: 3 lbs apples peeled cored and sliced
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Toss apples and cranberries with granulated sugar, cornstarch, cinnamon, nutmeg, and lemon juice; spread in dish.
Make streusel: combine oats, flour, brown sugar, and salt. Cut in cold butter until crumbly. Stir in almonds.
Sprinkle streusel evenly over fruit.
Bake 45-55 minutes until topping is golden and juices bubble. Tent with foil if streusel browns too quickly.
Cool 15 minutes and serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

name: Blueberry Peach Cobbler
description: Juicy summer fruit baked under a tender drop-biscuit topping that comes out golden and flaky.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Toss blueberries and peaches with 1/2 cup sugar, cornstarch, and lemon juice; spread in dish.
Make biscuit topping: whisk flour, 2 tbsp sugar, baking powder, and salt. Cut in cold butter until crumbly. Stir in milk just until a shaggy dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over fruit leaving some fruit exposed. Sprinkle with coarse sugar.
Bake 40-45 minutes until biscuit topping is golden and fruit is bubbling.
Cool 10 minutes; serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

name: Homemade Chocolate Eclairs
description: Classic French eclairs filled with silky pastry cream and dipped in a rich chocolate glaze.
ingredients: 2 cups whole milk for pastry cream
instructions: Make pastry cream: whisk yolks and cornstarch. Heat 2 cups milk and 1/2 cup sugar to simmer; slowly whisk into yolks. Return to pan; cook over medium heat until thick and bubbling. Remove; stir in 1 tbsp butter and vanilla. Press plastic wrap on surface; refrigerate 3 hours.

Make choux: combine butter, water, milk, salt, and sugar; bring to simmer. Add flour; stir vigorously until dough forms a ball. Cool 5 minutes then beat in eggs gradually until dough is smooth and shiny.
Preheat oven to 400°F. Pipe 4-inch logs onto parchment-lined sheets. Bake 20 minutes; reduce to 350°F and bake 10-15 more minutes until golden. Cool completely.
Make glaze: heat cream until steaming; pour over chopped chocolate. Stir until smooth.
Pierce base of each eclair; pipe with pastry cream. Dip tops in chocolate glaze.
Refrigerate until ready to serve.

name: Smitten Kitchen Birthday Cake
description: Classic moist vanilla butter cake layered with rich sour cream chocolate frosting.
ingredients: 2 1/4 cups sour cream at room temperature
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Butter two 9-inch round pans and line with parchment. Sift flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Beat butter and sugar until pale and fluffy. Beat in vanilla; add eggs one at a time.
Alternately beat in flour mixture and buttermilk in three additions each, beginning and ending with flour.
Divide batter between pans; bake 35-40 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in pans 10 minutes then on racks completely.
Make frosting: melt chocolate in a double boiler; cool to tepid. Whisk sour cream, 1/4 cup corn syrup, and vanilla. Stir in chocolate until uniform. Chill until spreadable, about 30 minutes.
Place one layer on plate; spread with frosting. Top with second layer; frost top and sides. Refrigerate 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Classic Creme Brulee
description: Perfectly silky vanilla custard with a crackling caramelized sugar crust baked in a water bath.
ingredients: 6 tbsp granulated sugar for brulee topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F. Heat cream with vanilla bean pod and seeds until just simmering. Remove; steep 15 minutes. Discard pod.
Whisk egg yolks, 1/2 cup sugar, and salt until pale. Slowly whisk in warm cream to temper. Strain through a fine sieve.
Divide among six 6-oz ramekins. Place in a roasting pan; add boiling water to come halfway up ramekins.
Bake 40-45 minutes until just set around edges but wobbly in center.
Remove from water bath; cool to room temperature. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or up to 2 days.
Just before serving sprinkle 1 tbsp sugar over each custard. Torch until deep amber and crackly. Serve immediately.

name: Carrot Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
description: Supremely moist one-layer carrot cake packed with warm spices and tangy cream cheese frosting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; spray a 9-inch springform pan with nonstick spray.
Beat brown sugar, oil, and yogurt until combined. Add eggs one at a time; mix in vanilla.
Whisk flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt; fold into wet ingredients until just combined. Fold in carrots and pecans.
Pour into pan; bake 32-38 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Make frosting: beat cream cheese and butter until smooth, 2 minutes. Add confectioners sugar; beat until thick. Add cream and beat 2 more minutes.
Spread frosting over cooled cake. Refrigerate 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Yeast-Raised Doughnuts
description: Pillowy golden yeast doughnuts fried to perfection and glazed with classic vanilla icing.
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Add warm milk, melted butter, egg, and vanilla; mix until a soft dough forms.
Knead 6-8 minutes until smooth. Place in greased bowl; cover and let rise 1.5-2 hours until doubled.
Punch down dough; roll to 1/4-inch thickness on a floured surface. Cut with a 2.5-inch round cutter; let rise on parchment 30-60 minutes until doubled.
Heat oil in a heavy pan to 350°F. Fry doughnuts 2-3 at a time until golden brown, about 1 minute per side. Drain on paper towels.
Make glaze: whisk powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla until smooth.
Dip warm doughnuts in glaze and set on a wire rack 15 minutes until glaze is set.

name: Chocolate Budino
description: Silky Italian chocolate pudding made rich with egg yolks and topped with lightly whipped cream.
ingredients: 1/2 cup additional heavy cream for serving
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar in the bottom of a medium saucepan. Slowly drizzle in 2 cups cream while whisking.
Warm over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Do not simmer.
Place chopped chocolate in a bowl; set a fine-mesh sieve over it. Pour hot egg mixture through the sieve onto chocolate.
Stir until chocolate melts. Add butter, salt, vanilla, and bourbon if using; stir until smooth.
Divide among small cups; refrigerate until cold and set, about 2 hours.
Just before serving whip remaining 1/2 cup cream with powdered sugar to very soft peaks. Spoon gently over each budino.

name: No-Bake Berry Cheesecake
description: Luscious no-bake cream cheese filling in a graham cracker crust swirled with fresh raspberries.
ingredients: 16 oz cream cheese at room temperature
instructions: Mix crumbs and melted butter; press into an 8-9 inch springform pan. Freeze 15 minutes.
Beat cream cheese, powdered sugar, and 2 tsp vanilla until smooth. Add 1 cup cream; whip until soft peaks form.
Mash 1/2 cup raspberries into a sauce; swirl into cream cheese filling. Pour into crust. Refrigerate at least 8 hours.
Make berry sauce: simmer 1 cup raspberries with lemon juice and 1 tbsp honey 2-3 minutes. Stir in cornstarch dissolved in 2 tbsp water; boil 1 minute. Strain; cool completely.
Whip remaining 1 cup cream with remaining 1 tsp vanilla and 2 tbsp honey to soft peaks.
Remove from pan. Spoon berry sauce on top; pile with fresh berries and dollop with whipped cream.

name: Banana Pudding with Vanilla Wafers
description: Creamy vanilla custard layered with ripe bananas and vanilla wafers for a Southern-style dessert.
instructions: Whisk sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a saucepan. Add eggs and yolks one at a time whisking smooth. Whisk in vanilla bean paste then gradually pour in milk and then cream.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, whisking constantly until thickened and bubbling; cook 1 minute more. Stir in butter and vanilla. Cool 5 minutes.
Lay vanilla wafers in the bottom of a 9x9-inch dish. Slice bananas over wafers.
Pour warm custard through a sieve over bananas. Press plastic wrap on custard surface; chill 1-2 hours until set.
Whip 1 cup cream with 1 tbsp sugar to soft peaks. Dollop over chilled pudding.
Garnish with crumbled wafers and sliced banana. Serve within a few hours.

name: Blueberry Crisp
description: Bubbling blueberry filling under a crispy oat-brown sugar topping ready in under an hour.
ingredients: 6 tbsp cold unsalted butter cut into small pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F; grease a 9-inch square baking dish.
Toss blueberries with granulated sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, and zest; spread in dish.
Make topping: combine oats, flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, and salt. Cut in cold butter until crumbly with pea-sized clumps.
Spread topping evenly over blueberries.
Bake 40-45 minutes until topping is golden and fruit is bubbling vigorously.
Cool at least 15 minutes before serving; best warm with vanilla ice cream.

name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: Warm date sponge cake drenched in a luscious butterscotch toffee sauce for the ultimate comfort dessert.
ingredients: 8 oz Medjool dates pitted and chopped
1 cup packed dark brown sugar for sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; grease a 9x9-inch pan. Place chopped dates in a bowl; pour boiling water over them and stir in baking soda. Soak 10 minutes then mash slightly.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt. Beat butter and 3/4 cup brown sugar until fluffy; beat in eggs one at a time then vanilla.
Fold in flour mixture alternately with date mixture until just combined. Pour into pan.
Bake 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Make toffee sauce: combine 1 cup brown sugar, cream, 4 tbsp butter, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until melted and combined; boil gently 2 minutes.
Poke warm cake all over with a skewer; pour half the sauce over cake. Absorb 5 minutes then slice. Serve warm drizzled with remaining sauce.

name: Vanilla Bean Ice Cream
description: Custard-based homemade vanilla ice cream with a rich egg yolk base and intense vanilla flavor.
instructions: Combine milk, cream, vanilla bean pod and seeds in a saucepan; bring just to a simmer. Remove from heat; steep 15 minutes. Discard pod.
Whisk egg yolks, sugar, and salt until pale and slightly thick.
Slowly ladle warm cream into yolks while whisking to temper; return mixture to saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until custard coats the back of a spoon at 170-175°F. Do not boil.
Strain through a sieve into a clean bowl; stir in vanilla. Chill over an ice bath then refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Churn in an ice cream maker 20-25 minutes. Transfer to a container and freeze at least 2 hours until firm.

name: Half Baked Harvest Chocolate Lava Cakes
description: Rich molten chocolate cakes with a flowing dark chocolate center served with vanilla ice cream.
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F. Grease four 6-oz ramekins and dust with cocoa powder; place on a baking sheet.
Melt butter and semisweet chocolate in microwave in 15-second increments until smooth.
Beat eggs, egg yolks, sugar, and vanilla on high speed 10 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Fold chocolate-butter into egg mixture; fold in flour until just combined.
Divide batter among ramekins. Press one dark chocolate square into center of each.

Bake 10-15 minutes until tops and sides are set but centers remain very soft. Rest 5 minutes; invert onto plates or serve in ramekins. Dust with powdered sugar; serve immediately with vanilla ice cream.

name: Banana Cream Pie
description: Custardy banana cream pie layered with ripe bananas in a vanilla wafer crust topped with whipped cream.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Mix wafer crumbs, 1/4 tsp salt, and melted butter; press into a 9-inch pie dish. Bake 9-10 minutes until lightly browned. Cool in refrigerator.
Whisk sugar, cornstarch, and remaining salt in a saucepan. Whisk in eggs and yolks one at a time; whisk in vanilla bean paste then gradually pour in milk and then cream.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, whisking constantly until thickened and bubbling; cook 1 minute. Stir in butter and vanilla. Cool 5 minutes.
Slice bananas into the cooled crust. Strain warm custard through a sieve over bananas; press plastic wrap on surface and chill 1-2 hours.
Whip 1 cup cream with 1 tbsp sugar to soft peaks; spread over chilled custard.
Decorate with sliced banana; slice into wedges and serve within a few hours.

name: Pecan Pie Bars with Brown Butter Crust
description: Brown-butter shortbread bars topped with a maple-pecan caramel filling baked into irresistible squares.
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter cut into pieces
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; line a 9x13-inch pan with parchment leaving overhang.
Brown 1 cup butter in a light-colored skillet over medium heat 5-8 minutes until golden and nutty. Pour into a bowl; cool 10 minutes.
Stir sugar, water, vanilla, and salt into brown butter. Mix in flour and cornstarch until no dry flour remains. Press evenly into pan; bake 15 minutes until lightly browned.

In the same skillet combine maple syrup, brown sugar, 6 tbsp butter, and cream; stir until butter melts. Cool 5 minutes; whisk in beaten eggs then fold in pecans. Pour over warm crust; sprinkle with flaky sea salt.
Bake 25-28 minutes until a toothpick comes out mostly clean. Tent with foil if browning too quickly.
Cool completely before lifting out and cutting into squares.

name: Peanut Butter Overnight Oats
description: Creamy overnight oats with peanut butter and chia seeds for a filling make-ahead breakfast.
instructions: Add almond milk, chia seeds, peanut butter, and maple syrup to a mason jar and stir to combine.
Add oats and stir a few more times, pressing down to ensure all oats are submerged.
Cover and refrigerate overnight or at least 6 hours.
Top with sliced banana and granola before serving.
Enjoy cold or microwave for 45-60 seconds if preferred warm.

name: Mixed Berry Smoothie Bowl
description: A thick soft-serve smoothie base of berries and banana topped with crunchy seeds and coconut.
ingredients: 1 small ripe banana sliced and frozen
instructions: Add frozen berries and banana to a blender and blend on low until broken into small bits.
Add coconut milk and protein powder and blend on low scraping down sides until thick soft-serve consistency forms.
Scoop into a bowl and top with chia seeds, hemp seeds, coconut, and granola.
Serve immediately.

name: Classic Avocado Toast
description: Simple whole-grain toast topped with mashed ripe avocado and flaky sea salt for a satisfying breakfast.
instructions: Toast the bread until golden and firm.
Halve the avocado, remove pit, and scoop flesh into a bowl.
Add lemon juice and kosher salt and mash with a fork to desired consistency.
Spread avocado over the toast.
Finish with flaky sea salt and red pepper flakes.
Serve immediately.

name: Basic Chia Seed Pudding
description: A silky chia pudding that sets overnight for a no-cook high-fiber breakfast with fresh toppings.
instructions: Combine almond milk, chia seeds, maple syrup, and cinnamon in a lidded jar.
Seal and shake vigorously to combine.
Chill for 2 hours then stir well to break up clumps.
Cover and refrigerate 8 hours or overnight until set.
Top with blueberries and walnuts before serving.

name: Shakshuka with Feta
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and red pepper sauce topped with crumbled feta cheese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F. Warm olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add onion, bell pepper, and salt; cook stirring often until softened about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, tomato paste, cumin, paprika, and red pepper flakes; cook stirring 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and parsley; simmer 5 minutes.
Make wells with a spoon and crack one egg into each well; spoon a bit of sauce over the whites.
Transfer skillet to oven and bake 8-12 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still soft.
Top with crumbled feta and additional parsley; serve with crusty bread.

name: Freezer Breakfast Burritos
description: Hearty scrambled egg and veggie burritos made in bulk and frozen for quick weekday breakfasts.
instructions: Saute onion and bell pepper in 1/2 tbsp butter over medium heat until softened about 5 minutes; transfer to a bowl.
Cook ham in another 1/2 tbsp butter until browned about 5 minutes; transfer to a separate bowl.
Whisk eggs; melt remaining butter in skillet over medium heat; pour in eggs and scramble until just set but still moist.
Lay out tortillas and distribute eggs, peppers and onions, ham, and cheese evenly.
Fold bottom of each tortilla up, tuck in sides, and roll up tightly.
Wrap each burrito in parchment paper and freeze.
To reheat thaw overnight in fridge and microwave 1-2 minutes or air fry at 350 degrees F for 6-10 minutes.

name: Blueberry Baked Oatmeal
description: A warm wholesome baked oatmeal casserole packed with blueberries and pecans for a crowd-friendly breakfast.
ingredients: 12 oz fresh or frozen blueberries divided
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F and grease a 9-inch square baking dish.
Toast pecans on a rimmed baking sheet 4-5 minutes until fragrant.
Whisk oats, pecans, cinnamon, baking powder, salt, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Whisk milk, maple syrup, eggs, half the oil, and vanilla in a smaller bowl.
Spread 2/3 of the blueberries in the baking dish, cover with dry oat mixture, then drizzle wet ingredients over.
Wiggle pan so milk seeps through; scatter remaining blueberries on top.
Bake 42-45 minutes until golden. Drizzle remaining oil over top before serving.

name: Asparagus and Goat Cheese Frittata
description: A golden broiled frittata with shaved asparagus ribbons and creamy goat cheese.
instructions: Shave asparagus into ribbons using a vegetable peeler discarding tough ends.
Preheat broiler with a rack 6 inches from the heat.
Beat eggs with milk, salt, and pepper; stir in scallions and gently fold in asparagus ribbons.
Heat olive oil in a 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat until fully hot.
Pour in egg mixture and crumble goat cheese over the top.
Cook on medium-low until edges are set and bottom is lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Transfer to broiler and cook 1-3 minutes until top is golden and eggs are just set.
Let cool slightly then slice into wedges and serve.

name: Loaded Veggie Egg Muffins
description: Portable baked egg cups loaded with spinach and bell pepper for easy high-protein meal prep.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F and generously spray a 12-cup muffin tin with olive oil spray.
Whisk eggs in a large bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Mix in spinach, tomatoes, onion, bell pepper, and bacon.
Pour egg mixture evenly into muffin cups filling about 3/4 full.
Top each cup with shredded cheddar.
Place tin on a baking sheet and bake 20-25 minutes until set.
Cool 5-10 minutes before removing from tin.

name: PBJ Acai Bowl
description: A thick acai and banana smoothie base with peanut butter finished with fresh fruit and hemp seeds.
instructions: Add frozen acai, frozen banana, peanut butter powder, and almond milk to a high-speed blender.
Add spinach if using.
Blend on low using a blender wand to push fruit down, scraping sides as needed, until thick and smooth.
Add only as much milk as needed to achieve a thick smoothie consistency.
Divide between two bowls and top with sliced banana, coconut, hemp seeds, and berries.
Serve immediately.

name: Super Green Smoothie Bowl
description: A nutrient-dense green smoothie bowl packed with spinach and kale topped with granola and seeds.
instructions: Add avocado, frozen bananas, frozen berries, spinach, kale, almond milk, flaxseed meal, and almond butter to a blender.
Blend until creamy and smooth adding more milk as needed to thin.
Taste and adjust sweetness with a ripe banana or a drizzle of maple syrup if needed.
Divide between two bowls and top with granola, hemp seeds, and fresh berries.
Serve immediately.

name: Whole Wheat Banana Bread Pancakes
description: Fluffy whole wheat pancakes made with mashed bananas and a touch of cinnamon for natural sweetness.
instructions: Whisk flour, baking powder, brown sugar, and salt in a large bowl.
Mash bananas in a medium bowl and add milk, vanilla, egg, and melted coconut oil; whisk to combine.
Fold wet ingredients into dry ingredients, stirring until a smooth batter forms; do not overmix. Let batter rest 5 minutes.
Heat a skillet or griddle over medium heat and lightly grease with coconut oil or spray.
Pour about 1/3 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form on surface about 2-3 minutes.
Flip and cook another 1-2 minutes until golden.
Serve hot with maple syrup.

name: Egg White and Veggie Omelet
description: A high-protein omelet made with egg whites and fresh vegetables folded with melted cheddar.
instructions: Lightly beat the whole egg and egg whites with a fork in a bowl; add vegetables, salt, and pepper and mix well.
Heat a 9-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat; spray with oil.
Pour in egg mixture and let sit to start cooking.
Gently lift cooked edges with a spatula to allow uncooked egg to flow to the sides.
Once eggs are mostly set, scatter cheese along the center.
Let cheese melt briefly then fold both sides toward the center.
Slide onto a plate and serve immediately.

name: Egg White Muffins with Turkey Bacon
description: Protein-packed egg white cups lined with turkey bacon and filled with colorful vegetables and cheese.
ingredients: 6 slices uncured turkey bacon cut in half
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F and generously spray a 12-cup muffin tin with olive oil spray.
Saute shallots, scallions, and bell pepper in olive oil over medium-low heat 5-6 minutes until tender.
