ingredients: 4 large leeks, white and light green parts only, sliced
3 medium Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and diced
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add leeks and cook until very soft, about 10 minutes. Do not brown.
Add potatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 20 minutes until potatoes are completely tender.
Blend soup until completely smooth with an immersion blender. Stir in heavy cream and milk. Season with salt and white pepper.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight. Serve cold in chilled bowls, garnished with chives.

name: Creamy Mushroom Soup
description: A rich, velvety mushroom soup blended smooth with caramelized cremini and a splash of sherry.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms in a single layer (in batches) and cook until browned and liquid evaporates, about 12 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Add onion and cook until softened, 3 minutes. Add garlic and flour; stir 1 minute.
Pour in sherry and scrape up browned bits. Add broth, milk, thyme, and bay leaf. Simmer 20 minutes. Remove thyme and bay leaf.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender. Squeeze in lemon juice, season to taste, and serve garnished with parsley.

name: Creamy Wild Rice Chicken Soup
description: Cozy, creamy chicken soup with nutty wild rice, roasted mushrooms, carrots, and Parmesan.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: In a large pot, combine chicken, wild rice, carrots, celery, shallots, broth, thyme, and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes until rice is tender.
Meanwhile, roast mushrooms: toss with 3 tbsp butter, garlic, rosemary, and salt on a sheet pan. Roast at 425°F for 25 minutes until golden and crisp.
Shred cooked chicken with two forks. Stir cream, Parmesan, and spinach into the soup; cook until wilted.
Mash roasted garlic and stir mushrooms into soup. Divide into bowls and serve topped with fresh rosemary.

name: Cajun Chicken and Andouille Gumbo
description: Authentic Louisiana gumbo with a dark chocolate roux, chicken, andouille sausage, and okra.
ingredients: sliced green onions and hot sauce for serving
instructions: Make the roux: heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook, stirring constantly, until a deep chocolate brown color, 20 to 25 minutes. Do not burn.
Add onion, bell pepper, and celery to the roux. Cook until very soft, about 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth. Add Cajun seasoning, thyme, bay leaves, sausage, and chicken. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 45 minutes.
Remove chicken, shred, and return to pot. Add okra and simmer 10 more minutes. Remove bay leaves. Serve over rice with green onions and hot sauce.

name: Pork Posole Rojo
description: A Mexican pork and hominy stew with a rich dried chile broth and classic garnishes.
ingredients: 4 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
shredded cabbage, radishes, lime, and dried oregano for serving
instructions: Toast dried chiles in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side. Soak in hot water for 15 minutes. Drain and blend with garlic and 1 cup soaking liquid to form a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a large pot. Brown pork in batches over high heat. Remove pork and set aside.
Add onion and cook until softened, 5 minutes. Add chile paste and cook 3 minutes. Add broth, pork, oregano, and cumin. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add hominy and simmer uncovered for 30 more minutes until pork is very tender. Season with salt. Serve with cabbage, radishes, and lime wedges.

name: Kimchi Jjigae
description: Bold and fiery Korean kimchi stew with pork belly, silken tofu, and a deeply savory red broth.
ingredients: 1/2 lb pork belly, cut into bite-sized pieces
instructions: In a medium pot, add pork belly, kimchi, onion, and garlic. Cook over medium heat, stirring, for 5 minutes to sauté slightly.
Add gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, and sugar. Stir to coat everything.
Pour in water or broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes until pork is tender.
Gently add tofu and simmer 5 more minutes. Drizzle with sesame oil and garnish with green onions. Serve with steamed white rice.

name: Irish Lamb Stew
description: Traditional Irish stew with tender lamb shoulder, waxy potatoes, carrots, and pearl barley.
ingredients: 2 lbs lamb shoulder, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season lamb with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a Dutch oven over high heat; sear lamb in batches until browned, about 4 minutes per batch. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and garlic; cook 5 minutes.
Add broth, water, barley, thyme, bay leaves, and seared lamb. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots. Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender and broth has thickened slightly. Remove bay leaves, season, and serve garnished with parsley.

name: Beef Bourguignon
description: The classic French braised beef stew with red wine, lardons, mushrooms, and pearl onions.
ingredients: 3 lbs beef chuck, cut into 2-inch cubes
6 oz lardons or thick-cut bacon, diced
instructions: Marinate beef in wine with carrots and bouquet garni for 2 hours. Drain and pat beef dry, reserving marinade.
Cook lardons in a Dutch oven until crispy; remove. Brown beef in batches in lardon fat. Remove and set aside. Add garlic and tomato paste; cook 1 minute.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables in pot; stir. Add reserved marinade, broth, beef, and lardons. Bring to a boil, cover, and braise in 325°F oven for 2.5 hours.
In the last 30 minutes, sauté pearl onions and mushrooms in butter until browned; add to stew. Remove bouquet garni, season, and serve with crusty bread or mashed potatoes.

name: Spiced Pumpkin Soup
description: Silky pumpkin soup with coconut milk, ginger, and warming spices for a cozy autumn meal.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) pure pumpkin puree
salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook 6 minutes until softened. Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute. Add cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves; stir 30 seconds.
Stir in pumpkin puree, coconut milk, and broth. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring well.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Blend until completely smooth if desired.
Stir in maple syrup and lime juice. Season with salt and white pepper. Serve garnished with toasted pepitas and a swirl of coconut milk.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork
description: Tender spice-rubbed pork shoulder slow cooked and tossed in tangy homemade BBQ sauce.
instructions: Mix brown sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, pepper, and cayenne into a rub.
Pat pork shoulder dry and coat all over with the spice rub.
Place pork in slow cooker and pour apple cider around it.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8-10 hours or HIGH for 5-6 hours until fall-apart tender.
Remove pork and shred with two forks, discarding excess fat.
Whisk ketchup, vinegar, and Worcestershire into drippings in the slow cooker.
Return shredded pork to sauce, stir well, and cook on HIGH for 20 minutes.
Serve on buns with coleslaw.

name: White Chicken Chili
description: Creamy slow cooker chili with shredded chicken, white beans, salsa verde, and cream cheese.
ingredients: 15 oz canned white navy beans (drained and rinsed)
instructions: Add chicken breasts, white beans, chicken broth, salsa verde, cumin, oregano, and salt to slow cooker; stir to combine.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6-8 hours or HIGH for 3-4 hours until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks; return to slow cooker.
In a small bowl, temper cream cheese by stirring in a few spoonfuls of hot broth until smooth.
Add cream cheese mixture back to slow cooker and whisk until fully incorporated.
Stir in lime juice and adjust seasoning.
Serve topped with Monterey Jack cheese and fresh cilantro.

name: Classic Beef Chili
description: Hearty slow cooker chili packed with ground beef, kidney beans, and bold smoky spices.
ingredients: 16 oz canned red kidney beans (drained and rinsed)
16 oz canned black beans (drained and rinsed)
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Brown ground beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, crumbling as it cooks; drain excess fat.
Add garlic, onion, and poblano to the skillet and cook 1 minute until fragrant; transfer to slow cooker.
Stir in beef broth, kidney beans, black beans, crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, chili powder, paprika, oregano, cumin, and hot sauce.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on LOW for 7-8 hours or HIGH for 5-6 hours.
Stir before serving; garnish with sour cream and green onions.

name: Mississippi Pot Roast
description: Buttery chuck roast slow cooked with ranch seasoning and pepperoncini for tangy, tender perfection.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place chuck roast in the slow cooker and pour in beef broth.
Mix cornstarch with 2 tbsp water until smooth; stir into broth.
Sprinkle ranch seasoning over the top of the roast.
Arrange pepperoncini peppers around the roast and lay butter slices on top.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 4-5 hours or LOW for 8-10 hours until internal temp reaches 205°F.
Shred beef with two forks or slice and return to juices.
Serve over mashed potatoes, rice, or egg noodles with cooking liquid as gravy.

name: Slow Cooker Carnitas
description: Juicy Mexican pulled pork with orange and lime, broiled crispy for perfect taco filling.
instructions: Pat pork dry and rub all over with salt, pepper, cumin, chili powder, and oregano; drizzle with olive oil.
Place seasoned pork in the slow cooker.
Add onion, garlic, green chilies, cilantro, orange juice, and lime juice around and over the pork.
Cover and cook on LOW for 10 hours or HIGH for 7 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Remove pork to a baking sheet and shred with two forks, reserving cooking liquid.
Drizzle a few spoonfuls of cooking liquid over the shredded pork.
Broil on high for 3 minutes, toss, and broil 3 more minutes until edges are crispy.
Serve in warm corn tortillas with desired toppings.

name: Barbacoa Beef
description: Chipotle-inspired slow cooker beef barbacoa with smoky adobo spices, perfect for tacos and bowls.
ingredients: 3 lbs boneless chuck roast (cut into large pieces)
instructions: In a blender, combine chipotle peppers, apple cider vinegar, garlic, lime juice, beef broth, cumin, oregano, cloves, tomato paste, salt, and pepper; blend until smooth.
Place beef pieces and sliced onion in slow cooker; add bay leaves on top.
Pour blended sauce over the beef and toss to coat.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8-10 hours or HIGH for 4-6 hours until beef is fall-apart tender.
Discard bay leaves; shred beef in the slow cooker with two forks.
Toss shredded beef in the juices and let sit 10 minutes to absorb flavors.
Serve in tacos, burritos, or bowls with rice and beans.

name: Slow Cooker Butter Chicken
description: Rich Indian butter chicken with aromatic spices, heavy cream, and tender chunks of chicken thighs.
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless skinless chicken thighs (cut into chunks)
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together chicken stock, tomato paste, curry powder, garam masala, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Place chicken thighs, onion, garlic, and ginger into a 4-quart slow cooker; pour stock mixture over top and stir.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4 hours or HIGH for 2 hours until chicken is tender.
Stir in heavy cream, lime juice, and brown sugar; season with additional salt and pepper if needed.
Serve immediately over basmati rice garnished with fresh cilantro.

name: Slow Cooker Ropa Vieja
description: Cuban shredded flank steak slow cooked in a savory tomato sauce with peppers, olives, and warming spices.
instructions: Add beef broth, tomato paste, diced tomatoes, oregano, cumin, turmeric, vinegar, salt, and pepper to the slow cooker and stir to combine.
Add flank steak and flip to coat in the sauce.
Top with diced onion, bell peppers, olives, and garlic cloves; mix the vegetables together on top of the meat.
Cover and cook on LOW for 9 hours or HIGH for 5 hours without lifting the lid.
Shred the beef directly in the slow cooker using two forks and stir to combine with the sauce.
Serve over yellow rice with fresh cilantro if desired.

name: Slow Cooker Beef Stew
description: Classic hearty beef stew with tender chuck, potatoes, carrots, and rich savory broth.
ingredients: 2 lbs beef stew meat (chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes)
instructions: Add potatoes, carrots, and onion to the slow cooker.
Combine flour, salt, pepper, onion powder, and thyme in a zip-lock bag; add beef cubes and shake to coat.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high and brown beef on all sides in batches; transfer to slow cooker.
Deglaze the skillet with beef broth, scraping up brown bits; whisk in tomato paste until smooth.
Pour broth mixture over the beef and vegetables in the slow cooker; stir.
Cover and cook on LOW for 7-8 hours until beef and vegetables are tender.
Add frozen peas during the last 15 minutes and stir.
Season to taste and serve with crusty bread.

name: French Dip Sandwiches
description: Slow-cooked chuck roast piled onto toasted hoagie rolls with provolone and savory au jus for dipping.
instructions: Place butter and onion in the slow cooker and nestle chuck roast on top.
Pour in beef broth, soy sauce, and Worcestershire sauce; add garlic and pepper.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours or HIGH for 4-5 hours until meat is fork-tender.
Remove roast and shred or thinly slice; return meat to slow cooker for 30 minutes.
Slice hoagie rolls and toast cut-side up in the oven under broiler.
Layer shredded beef and provolone on rolls; broil 2 minutes until cheese melts.
Strain cooking liquid into small bowls as au jus for dipping and serve.

name: Slow Cooker Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Aromatic Indian chicken tikka masala slow cooked in a spiced tomato-yogurt sauce, served over basmati rice.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into bite-size pieces)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat; cook onion until golden, about 3 minutes.
Add ginger and garlic; cook 1 minute. Add cumin, garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, and salt; cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and milk; transfer mixture to slow cooker.
Add chicken pieces and stir to coat in the sauce.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4-5 hours or HIGH for 2-3 hours until chicken is cooked through.
Temper the yogurt by mixing 1/2 cup of the hot sauce into the yogurt in a bowl, then stir yogurt mixture back into the slow cooker.
Serve over basmati rice topped with fresh cilantro.

name: Slow Cooker Sesame Chicken
description: Sweet and savory crockpot sesame chicken with soy, honey, and ginger sauce served over fluffy rice.
instructions: Place chicken thighs in slow cooker and season with black pepper.
Whisk together soy sauce, honey, tomato paste, rice wine vinegar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, sriracha, and 1 tbsp water in a bowl; pour over chicken.
Cover and cook on LOW for 3-4 hours until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks; leave sauce in slow cooker.
Dissolve cornstarch in remaining 1/4 cup water; stir into the slow cooker sauce.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 15-20 minutes until sauce thickens.
Return shredded chicken to slow cooker and toss to coat.
Serve over rice topped with sesame seeds and chopped scallions.

name: Thai Peanut Chicken
description: Slow-cooked shredded chicken in a creamy Thai peanut coconut sauce with garlic and ginger.
ingredients: fresh cilantro and lime wedges for serving
instructions: In a skillet over medium-low heat, cook garlic, onion, and ginger in 1 tsp sesame oil until soft, about 3-4 minutes.
Add curry powder and cook 1-2 more minutes; transfer to slow cooker.
Add peanut butter, soy sauce, remaining sesame oil, rice vinegar, sriracha, and coconut milk to the slow cooker; whisk to combine.
Add chicken and coat well with the sauce.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 2-3 hours or LOW for 4-6 hours until chicken is cooked through and tender.
Remove chicken, shred with two forks, and return to slow cooker; cook on LOW 15 more minutes.
Serve over jasmine rice topped with chopped peanuts, cilantro, and lime wedges.

name: Slow Cooker Beef Bourguignon
description: French-inspired braised beef with red wine, bacon, mushrooms, and root vegetables in a silky sauce.
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless beef chuck (cut into 2-inch cubes)
2 pearl onions or 1/2 cup diced onion
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook diced bacon in a large skillet over medium-high until crispy; remove to slow cooker.
Season beef cubes with salt and pepper; sear in bacon drippings for 3-4 minutes per side until browned; transfer to slow cooker.
Add carrots, potatoes, onions, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Whisk together red wine, beef broth, tomato paste, and flour; pour over the slow cooker contents.
Add thyme and bay leaf.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8-10 hours or HIGH for 6 hours until beef is tender.
Stir in mushrooms during the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Discard bay leaf; season to taste and garnish with fresh parsley.

name: Slow Cooker Lamb Shanks
description: Fall-off-the-bone lamb shanks braised in red wine with aromatics and root vegetables.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season lamb shanks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over high heat; sear shanks in 2 batches until browned all over, about 5 minutes each; transfer to slow cooker.
Reduce heat to medium-low in same skillet; sauté onion, garlic, carrot, and celery for 5 minutes until softened.
Add red wine to skillet; bring to simmer and scrape up browned bits.
Stir in chicken stock, crushed tomatoes, and tomato paste; bring to simmer then pour into slow cooker.
Add thyme sprigs and bay leaves.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours until lamb is fall-apart tender.
Remove shanks; strain and reduce sauce on stovetop if desired. Serve over mashed potatoes.

name: Slow Cooker BBQ Brisket
description: Juicy spice-rubbed beef brisket slow cooked in BBQ sauce, broiled for a caramelized crust.
instructions: Mix brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, and cayenne into a spice rub; coat brisket all over.
In the slow cooker, whisk together beef broth, 1/2 cup BBQ sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and soy sauce.
Place rubbed brisket into the slow cooker, squeezing in if needed.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8-10 hours until very tender.
Remove brisket to a foil-lined baking sheet; pour cooking liquid into a saucepan and simmer to thicken.
Brush brisket with remaining 1/2 cup BBQ sauce; broil 3-5 minutes until caramelized.
Rest 5 minutes then slice against the grain; return to slow cooker with thickened sauce.

name: Slow Cooker Chicken Cacciatore
description: Italian hunter-style chicken with bell peppers, mushrooms, and crushed tomatoes, served over pasta.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper; place in slow cooker.
Add onion, garlic, bell pepper, and mushrooms around the chicken.
Pour crushed tomatoes and chicken broth over everything; sprinkle with Italian seasoning, oregano, and red pepper flakes.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6-8 hours or HIGH for 3-4 hours until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken and roughly chop or shred; return to slow cooker.
Stir in balsamic vinegar; season to taste.
Serve over cooked pasta topped with fresh parsley and grated Parmesan.

name: Slow Cooker Asian Short Ribs
description: Tender beef short ribs braised in a sweet soy-ginger glaze, garnished with sesame seeds and parsley.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together soy sauce, beef broth, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes.
Place short ribs into a 6-quart slow cooker and pour sauce over ribs.
Cover and cook on LOW for 7-8 hours or HIGH for 3-4 hours until ribs are fall-off-the-bone tender.
Remove ribs carefully; whisk cornstarch with 1/4 cup water and stir into the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 30 more minutes until sauce thickens.
Serve ribs over rice drizzled with thickened sauce, garnished with parsley and sesame seeds.

name: Slow Cooker Kalua Pig
description: Hawaiian-style smoky shredded pork made with just three ingredients for an authentic luau flavor.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Hawaiian sea salt (or kosher salt)
2 large banana leaves (optional for lining slow cooker)
instructions: Pierce pork shoulder all over with a fork or paring knife.
Rub Hawaiian sea salt all over the pork, then drizzle liquid smoke on top and rub in.
If using banana leaves, line slow cooker with them; otherwise spray with nonstick spray.
Place seasoned pork in slow cooker and scatter garlic cloves around it.
Cover and cook on LOW for 10-12 hours without lifting the lid during cooking.
When pork is tender, transfer to a plate and shred with two forks, discarding excess fat and bone.
Return shredded pork to slow cooker and stir into the accumulated juices.
Serve with steamed white rice and Hawaiian macaroni salad.

name: Slow Cooker Pulled Chicken
description: Easy BBQ pulled chicken with tender shredded chicken breasts smothered in smoky barbecue sauce.
instructions: Whisk together BBQ sauce, chicken broth, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, and salt in the slow cooker.
Place chicken breasts in the slow cooker and spoon sauce over to coat.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 hours or HIGH for 3-4 hours until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks; return to the slow cooker.
Stir shredded chicken into the sauce and cook on HIGH for 15 minutes.
Pile pulled chicken onto buns and top with creamy coleslaw.

name: Slow Cooker Honey Garlic Chicken
description: Sticky honey garlic glazed chicken thighs slow cooked until tender and served over rice.
ingredients: sesame seeds and scallions for garnish
instructions: In the slow cooker, whisk together honey, soy sauce, ketchup, ginger, garlic, minced onion, and red pepper flakes.
Remove 1/2 cup of the sauce and reserve in the fridge.
Season chicken with salt and pepper; add to slow cooker and toss to coat in sauce.
Cover and cook on LOW for 5-6 hours or HIGH for 2.5-3 hours until internal temp reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken and tent with foil; whisk cornstarch with cold water and stir into slow cooker on HIGH for 15 minutes until thickened.
Add reserved sauce and return chicken; toss to coat.
Serve over rice garnished with sesame seeds and sliced scallions.

name: Slow Cooker Salsa Chicken
description: Ultra-easy two-ingredient crockpot salsa chicken perfect for tacos, burritos, or rice bowls.
ingredients: shredded cheese, sour cream, and cilantro for serving
corn tortillas or cooked rice for serving
instructions: Place chicken breasts in the bottom of a 4-6 quart slow cooker.
Sprinkle taco seasoning, garlic powder, cumin, salt, and pepper over the chicken.
Pour salsa over the top and stir to coat the chicken.
Cover and cook on HIGH for 3-4 hours or LOW for 6-7 hours until chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken to a bowl and shred with two forks; return to slow cooker and stir into the salsa.
Serve in tortillas or over rice topped with shredded cheese, sour cream, and cilantro.

name: Slow Cooker Balsamic Chicken
description: Tangy balsamic glazed chicken thighs with garlic, herbs, and tomatoes, cooked low and slow.
instructions: Whisk together balsamic vinegar, honey, garlic, olive oil, rosemary, thyme, oregano, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place chicken thighs in slow cooker and pour balsamic mixture over them; toss to coat.
Add drained diced tomatoes around the chicken.
Cover and cook on LOW for 5-6 hours or HIGH for 2.5-3 hours until chicken reaches 165°F.
Remove chicken; transfer cooking liquid to a small saucepan and simmer 5-10 minutes to reduce into a glaze.
Drizzle glaze over chicken and garnish with fresh basil.
Serve over mashed potatoes, polenta, or roasted vegetables.

name: Classic Slow Cooker Pot Roast
description: Traditional Sunday pot roast with fork-tender chuck, carrots, potatoes, and rich savory gravy.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
2 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water for gravy
instructions: Season chuck roast generously on all sides with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder.
Place onion, potatoes, and carrots in the bottom of the slow cooker; add garlic.
Set seasoned roast on top of vegetables.
Whisk together beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, tomato paste, thyme, and rosemary; pour over the roast.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8-10 hours or HIGH for 4-5 hours until roast is fork-tender.
Remove roast and vegetables to a serving platter; tent with foil.
Whisk cornstarch with water; stir into slow cooker liquid and cook on HIGH 15 minutes until thickened into gravy.
Slice or shred roast and serve with vegetables and gravy.

name: Slow Cooker Lentil Soup
description: Hearty and nourishing slow cooker lentil soup with spinach, cumin, and a drizzle of olive oil.
instructions: Add lentils, carrots, celery, onion, garlic, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, cumin, paprika, oregano, cayenne, and salt to the slow cooker; stir to combine.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6-8 hours or HIGH for 3-4 hours until lentils are completely tender.
About 15 minutes before serving, stir in baby spinach and olive oil; recover and cook until spinach wilts.
Stir in fresh lemon juice and adjust seasoning.
Optional: Remove 2 cups of soup and blend until smooth, then stir back in for a creamier texture.
Serve garnished with fresh herbs and crusty bread.

name: Slow Cooker Split Pea Soup
description: Thick and comforting slow cooker split pea soup with diced ham and tender carrots.
instructions: Add split peas, chicken broth, carrots, onion, garlic, ham, thyme, and olive oil to a 5-quart or larger slow cooker.
Season with salt and pepper; stir to combine.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6-8 hours until peas break down and soup becomes very thick.
About 5 hours in, use a potato masher to help break down the peas further.
Add water to loosen the soup if it becomes too thick for your liking.
Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper.
Ladle into bowls and serve with crusty bread.

name: Slow Cooker Ham and Bean Soup
description: Classic slow cooker ham and bean soup with a ham bone, tomatoes, and savory herbs.
instructions: Sort and rinse beans; place in slow cooker.
Add diced onion, garlic, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, water, salt, pepper, paprika, and bay leaf; stir to combine.
Place ham bone in the center of the slow cooker, pressing down into the beans.
Cover and cook on LOW for 10-12 hours until beans are completely tender.
One hour before serving, carefully remove ham bone with tongs; pull all meat from the bone and chop.
Return chopped ham meat to the slow cooker; discard bone and bay leaf.
Stir soup well, adjust seasoning, and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Slow Cooker Minestrone
description: Classic Italian vegetable minestrone with kidney beans, pasta, and Parmesan in the slow cooker.
ingredients: 15 oz canned kidney beans (drained and rinsed)
15 oz canned cannellini beans (drained and rinsed)
instructions: Add vegetable broth, diced tomatoes, tomato paste, kidney beans, cannellini beans, carrots, celery, onion, garlic, oregano, basil, and bay leaves to slow cooker; stir.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6-8 hours or HIGH for 3-4 hours.
Add zucchini and ditalini pasta; turn to HIGH and cook 20-25 more minutes until pasta is tender.
Stir in baby spinach and cook 5 more minutes until wilted.
Discard bay leaves; adjust seasoning.
Serve topped with grated Parmesan and garlic toasted bread.

name: Slow Cooker Sweet and Sour Chicken
description: Tender crockpot chicken in a tangy pineapple sweet and sour sauce with bell peppers.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs boneless skinless chicken thighs (cut into chunks)
instructions: In the slow cooker, whisk together reserved pineapple juice, ketchup, brown sugar, rice wine vinegar, soy sauce, garlic powder, and ginger.
Add chicken chunks and toss to coat; place pineapple chunks on top.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4-5 hours or HIGH for 2-3 hours until chicken is cooked through.
Add diced bell peppers in the last 30 minutes of cooking.
Dissolve cornstarch in cold water; stir into the slow cooker and cook on HIGH for 15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Serve over rice garnished with sesame seeds.

name: Slow Cooker Chili Verde
description: New Mexico-style green pork chili with tomatillos, roasted green chiles, and cumin-spiced pork.
ingredients: 2.5 lbs boneless pork shoulder (cut into 1-inch chunks)
instructions: Season pork chunks with salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano.
Brown pork in a skillet over high heat in batches; transfer to slow cooker.
Add tomatillos, diced green chiles, roasted poblanos, onion, garlic, and chicken broth to the slow cooker.
Stir to combine and nestle pork into the vegetable mixture.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours or HIGH for 4-5 hours until pork is very tender.
Use a fork to break apart larger pieces of pork if desired.
Stir in fresh cilantro and lime juice; adjust seasoning.
Serve with warm flour tortillas, rice, or over baked potatoes.

name: Greek Salad
description: A classic Horiatiki salad with tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and creamy feta in olive oil.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Cut tomatoes into wedges and cucumber into thick half-moons.
Thinly slice red onion and green pepper.
Combine all vegetables and olives in a large bowl.
Place feta block on top or crumble over salad.
Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle oregano, season with salt and pepper, and serve.

name: Chicken Souvlaki
description: Juicy grilled chicken skewers marinated in lemon, garlic, and oregano, served with pita.
instructions: Cut chicken into 1.5-inch cubes and place in a bowl.
Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper.
Pour marinade over chicken, toss to coat, and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.
Thread chicken onto metal or soaked wooden skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through.
Serve in warm pita with tzatziki and fresh vegetables.

name: Lamb Gyros
description: Seasoned ground lamb cooked on a sheet pan and sliced thin for authentic-style gyros.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F.
Pulse onion and garlic in a food processor until finely minced.
Combine lamb with onion mixture and all spices, mixing thoroughly for 5 minutes until very smooth.
Pack the meat mixture tightly into a loaf pan, pressing out all air bubbles.
Bake for 50-60 minutes until internal temperature reaches 165°F.
Let rest 5 minutes, then slice very thin.
Serve in warm pita with tzatziki, tomatoes, and red onion.

name: Moussaka
description: Layered Greek casserole of spiced ground lamb, roasted eggplant, and creamy béchamel.
instructions: Slice eggplant 1/4-inch thick, salt and let drain 30 minutes, then pat dry.
Brush eggplant slices with olive oil and roast at 400°F for 20 minutes.
Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft; add lamb and brown well.
Add wine, crushed tomatoes, cinnamon, and allspice; simmer 20 minutes until thick.
Make béchamel: melt butter, whisk in flour, gradually add milk, cook until thick.
Remove from heat and stir in eggs and half the Parmesan.
Layer eggplant, then meat sauce, then remaining eggplant in a baking dish.
Pour béchamel over top, sprinkle remaining Parmesan, and bake at 375°F for 45 minutes until golden.

name: Pastitsio
description: Greek baked pasta with spiced ground beef, tube pasta, and a thick creamy béchamel topping.
instructions: Cook pasta al dente according to package directions; drain and toss with 1 tbsp olive oil.
Sauté onion and garlic, add ground beef, and brown until cooked through.
Add wine, tomatoes, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and pepper; simmer 20 minutes.
Make béchamel: whisk butter and flour, add milk gradually, cook until very thick; beat in eggs off heat.
Stir half the Parmesan into the pasta.
Spread pasta evenly in a greased 9x13 baking dish.
Layer meat sauce over pasta, then pour béchamel on top.
Sprinkle remaining Parmesan and bake at 375°F for 45-50 minutes until deep golden.

name: Classic Hummus
description: Silky smooth chickpea hummus blended with tahini, lemon, and garlic, drizzled with olive oil.
instructions: Drain and rinse chickpeas, reserving a few for garnish.
Add tahini and lemon juice to food processor and blend 1 minute until creamy.
Add garlic, cumin, and salt; blend another minute.
Add chickpeas and blend 3-4 minutes, drizzling in ice water for ultra-smooth texture.
Taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Spread into bowls, drizzle with olive oil, and garnish with paprika, parsley, and reserved chickpeas.

name: Baba Ganoush
description: Smoky fire-roasted eggplant dip blended with tahini, garlic, and lemon juice.
instructions: Char eggplants directly over a gas flame or under a broiler, turning occasionally, 30-40 minutes until completely collapsed and skin is blackened.
Transfer to a colander and let cool and drain for 15 minutes.
Peel off charred skin, discard seeds if very large, and squeeze out excess moisture.
Roughly chop eggplant flesh and add to food processor with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, and salt.
Pulse until creamy but slightly textured.
Transfer to a plate, drizzle with olive oil, garnish with paprika, parsley, and pomegranate seeds.

name: Tabbouleh
description: Fresh Lebanese herb salad loaded with parsley, mint, bulgur, tomatoes, and bright lemon dressing.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Soak bulgur in cold water for 10-15 minutes until tender; drain thoroughly and squeeze dry.
Finely chop parsley and mint leaves (mostly leaves, few stems).
Dice tomatoes small and slice green onions thin.
Combine bulgur, parsley, mint, tomatoes, and green onions in a large bowl.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, allspice, salt, and pepper together.
Pour dressing over salad, toss well, and let sit 15 minutes before serving.

name: Fattoush Salad
description: Levantine bread salad with crispy pita chips, seasonal vegetables, and tangy sumac dressing.
instructions: Tear pita into bite-sized pieces and toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, and half the sumac.
Bake pita chips at 375°F for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy.
Whisk remaining olive oil, lemon juice, remaining sumac, minced garlic, salt, and pepper to make dressing.
Chop romaine, tomatoes, cucumber, and radishes; slice green onions.
Combine vegetables, mint, and parsley in a large bowl.
Toss with dressing, then fold in pita chips just before serving.

name: Crispy Falafel
description: Herb-packed chickpea and fava patties fried until deeply golden and crispy throughout.
instructions: Drain soaked chickpeas and fava beans thoroughly.
Pulse all ingredients (except oil and sesame seeds) in a food processor until a coarse, moist meal forms — do not over-process.
Refrigerate mixture 30 minutes, then form into 1.5-inch balls, pressing in sesame seeds.
Heat 3 inches of oil to 350°F in a deep pot.
Fry falafel in batches for 3-4 minutes until deep golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately in pita or on a platter with tahini sauce.

name: Dolmades
description: Grape leaves stuffed with herbed rice and pine nuts, simmered in olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Rinse grape leaves and blanch in boiling water 2 minutes; drain and spread flat.
Sauté onion and garlic in 3 tbsp olive oil until soft; add rice and stir 2 minutes.
Add pine nuts, dill, mint, allspice, cinnamon, salt, pepper; mix well and let cool.
Place a heaping teaspoon of filling on each leaf, fold sides over, and roll tightly.
Line a pot bottom with extra grape leaves; arrange stuffed dolmades seam-side down in tight layers.
Pour remaining olive oil, lemon juice, and water over dolmades.
Weight with a plate, cover, and simmer on low 45 minutes until rice is tender.

name: Kotopoulo Lemonato
description: Greek braised chicken thighs slowly simmered with lemon, garlic, and olive oil until tender.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high; sear chicken skin-side down 5-6 minutes until golden.
Flip and sear 3 minutes more; remove chicken and set aside.
Add garlic to pot and sauté 1 minute; deglaze with lemon juice and broth.
Add potato wedges, lemon slices, and thyme; nestle chicken back in skin-side up.
Cover and simmer on medium-low for 45 minutes until chicken is very tender.
Uncover last 10 minutes to reduce sauce slightly; garnish with parsley.

name: Lebanese Kibbeh
description: Baked bulgur and ground lamb patties with a spiced meat and pine nut filling.
instructions: Soak bulgur in cold water 15 minutes; drain and squeeze very dry.
Knead bulgur with 1 lb ground lamb, half the onion (grated), 1 tsp allspice, salt, and pepper until smooth paste forms.
For filling: sauté remaining onion in butter until golden, add 1/2 lb lamb, remaining spices, and pine nuts; cook until lamb is done.
Grease a baking dish; press half the bulgur-lamb shell into the dish.
Spread filling evenly over shell, then top with remaining shell mixture.
Score top into diamond shapes, drizzle with olive oil, and bake at 375°F for 35 minutes until golden.
Serve with mint and yogurt.

name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine
description: Slow-braised lamb shoulder with warming spices, preserved lemon, and Castelvetrano olives.
instructions: Season lamb pieces with cumin, coriander, turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, cayenne, and salt.
Heat olive oil in a tagine or Dutch oven; sear lamb on all sides until browned, about 10 minutes.
Remove lamb; sauté onion until soft, about 5 minutes; add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Return lamb to pot, add diced tomatoes and broth, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat 1.5-2 hours until lamb is fall-apart tender.
In the last 15 minutes, stir in preserved lemon rind and olives.
Serve over couscous garnished with fresh cilantro.

name: Spanish Seafood Paella
description: Classic Valencian rice dish with saffron, shrimp, mussels, and squid cooked in a wide pan.
instructions: Steep saffron in 1/4 cup warm broth for 10 minutes.
Heat olive oil in a wide paella pan; sauté onion and pepper until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and grated tomatoes; cook until sauce thickens, 10 minutes.
Add rice and smoked paprika; stir to coat in the sofrito.
Pour in hot broth and saffron mixture; arrange seafood evenly over rice.
Cook on medium-high without stirring until broth is absorbed, 18-20 minutes.
Scatter peas over top, increase heat briefly to form socarrat (crispy bottom), then cover and rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and lemon wedges.

name: Andalusian Gazpacho
description: Chilled Spanish tomato soup blended with cucumber, peppers, garlic, and sherry vinegar.
instructions: Remove crusts from bread and soak in cold water for 5 minutes; squeeze dry.
Roughly chop tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion, and garlic.
Combine all vegetables, bread, garlic, vinegar, olive oil, cumin, salt, and pepper in a blender.
Blend on high speed 2-3 minutes until very smooth.
Pass through a fine-mesh strainer for silkier texture if desired.
Adjust seasoning and thin with cold water if too thick.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours until well chilled; serve in bowls with a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Classic Caprese Salad
description: Fresh mozzarella and ripe tomatoes layered with basil, olive oil, and aged balsamic glaze.
instructions: Slice mozzarella and tomatoes into 1/4-inch rounds.
Arrange alternating slices of tomato and mozzarella on a serving platter.
Tuck basil leaves between slices.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic glaze.
Season with flaky salt and black pepper and serve immediately.

name: Tuscan Panzanella
description: Rustic Italian bread salad with juicy tomatoes, soaked ciabatta, basil, and red wine vinaigrette.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Tear bread into rough 1.5-inch pieces; toss with 2 tbsp olive oil and bake at 400°F until toasted and golden, about 10 minutes.
Cut tomatoes into wedges; season with salt and let sit in a colander 10 minutes to drain juices.
Reserve tomato juices for the vinaigrette.
Thinly slice red onion; toss with 1 tbsp vinegar and let marinate.
Whisk remaining olive oil, remaining vinegar, minced garlic, capers, and tomato juices.
Combine bread, tomatoes, onion, sliced cucumber, and basil.
Toss with vinaigrette, let sit 15 minutes for bread to absorb, and serve.

name: Branzino al Limone
description: Whole roasted branzino stuffed with lemon and fresh herbs, finished with caper butter.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F. Score fish 3 times on each side with a sharp knife.
Season fish inside and out with salt and pepper; stuff cavity with lemon slices, rosemary, thyme, and garlic.
Rub outside with olive oil.
Place in a roasting pan and pour white wine around fish.
Roast 18-20 minutes until flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Meanwhile, melt butter in a small pan and cook capers until sizzling.
Pour caper butter over roasted branzino and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Mediterranean Baked Cod
description: Flaky cod fillets baked in a vibrant tomato, olive, caper, and herb sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat until softened.
Add white wine and cook 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add diced tomatoes, olives, capers, oregano, basil, and red pepper flakes; simmer 5 minutes.
Season cod fillets with salt and pepper and nestle into the tomato sauce.
Bake uncovered for 15-18 minutes until cod is opaque and flakes easily.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve with crusty bread.

name: Lemon Herb Orzo
description: Creamy one-pot orzo with bright lemon zest, fresh herbs, spinach, and Parmesan.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat; sauté garlic 1 minute.
Add orzo and toast, stirring, for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered 10-12 minutes, stirring frequently, until orzo is al dente and broth is mostly absorbed.
Stir in butter, lemon zest, lemon juice, and Parmesan.
Fold in baby spinach and cook 1 minute until wilted.
Remove from heat, stir in dill and parsley, season with salt and pepper, and serve.

name: Lamb Kofta
description: Spiced Middle Eastern ground lamb skewers grilled over high heat and served with tahini sauce.
instructions: Finely grate onion and squeeze out moisture; mince garlic and parsley.
Combine lamb, onion, garlic, parsley, and all spices; knead for 2-3 minutes until well mixed and sticky.
Refrigerate 30 minutes (optional, helps hold shape).
Divide mixture into 8 portions; mold each around a flat metal skewer into a sausage shape.
Grill over high heat 10-12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until cooked through and charred.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, and water to make sauce.
Serve kofta with tahini sauce and flatbread.

name: Sicilian Eggplant Caponata
description: Sweet and sour Sicilian eggplant stew with tomatoes, olives, capers, and pine nuts.
instructions: Cut eggplant into 1-inch cubes, salt generously, and let drain in a colander 30 minutes; pat dry.
Fry eggplant in hot olive oil in batches until golden on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté onion and celery until softened.
Add crushed tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in olives, capers, red wine vinegar, and sugar; cook 5 minutes.
Return eggplant to pan; season with salt and pepper and simmer 5 more minutes.
Toast pine nuts in a dry pan; scatter over caponata with fresh basil. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Provençal Ratatouille
description: Classic French Provençal vegetable stew with zucchini, eggplant, peppers, and herbes de Provence.
instructions: Dice all vegetables into 3/4-inch pieces.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large Dutch oven; cook onion and garlic until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add eggplant and cook 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add bell peppers and cook 5 more minutes.
Stir in tomato paste, diced tomatoes, herbes de Provence, and dried basil.
Add zucchini, season well with salt and pepper, and cover; simmer on medium-low 25-30 minutes.
Uncover and cook 10 more minutes to thicken. Stir in fresh basil and remaining olive oil before serving.

name: Harissa Roasted Vegetables
description: Vibrant North African spiced roasted cauliflower, carrots, and chickpeas with yogurt drizzle.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F and line a large sheet pan with parchment.
Cut cauliflower into florets and carrots into sticks; drain and rinse chickpeas.
Toss all vegetables and chickpeas with harissa, olive oil, cumin, coriander, and salt.
Spread in a single layer on the sheet pan; roast 30-35 minutes, turning once, until caramelized and tender.
Stir together yogurt and lemon juice to make a drizzle.
Transfer vegetables to a platter, drizzle with yogurt, and scatter cilantro and sesame seeds over top.

name: Freekeh Pilaf with Herbs
description: Smoky whole-grain freekeh cooked pilaf-style with toasted nuts, dried fruit, and warming spices.
instructions: Rinse freekeh under cold water; drain.
Toast slivered almonds in a dry pan until golden; set aside.
Heat olive oil in a medium saucepan; sauté onion until golden, about 7 minutes.
Add garlic and spices; cook 1 minute.
Add freekeh and stir to coat in the oil and spices.
Pour in broth, season with salt and pepper, bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 20-25 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Fluff with a fork; fold in almonds, chopped dried apricots, parsley, and mint.

name: Mediterranean Stuffed Peppers
description: Bell peppers filled with herbed rice, ground beef, tomatoes, and feta, baked until tender.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Slice tops off peppers and remove seeds and membranes.
Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until soft; add ground beef and brown completely.
Drain excess fat; stir in diced tomatoes, cooked rice, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Remove from heat and fold in feta and parsley.
Place peppers in a baking dish; fill each generously with the beef and rice mixture.
Pour tomato sauce around the base of the peppers and cover with foil.
Bake 35 minutes covered, then uncover and bake 10 more minutes until peppers are tender.

name: Turkish Menemen
description: Silky Turkish scrambled eggs cooked in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce with fresh herbs.
instructions: Dice onion and peppers; grate or finely chop tomatoes.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet; sauté onion 4 minutes until softened.
Add peppers and cook 3 more minutes.
Stir in garlic, cumin, Aleppo pepper, and paprika; cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook on medium heat until sauce thickens slightly, 5 minutes.
Crack eggs directly into the pan; stir gently with a spatula to create soft folds — do not scramble completely, keep creamy.
Remove from heat while still glossy and soft; season with salt and scatter parsley over top. Serve immediately with bread.

name: Israeli Couscous Salad
description: Pearl couscous tossed with roasted vegetables, sun-dried tomatoes, olives, and lemon dressing.
instructions: Cook pearl couscous in salted boiling water 8-10 minutes until al dente; drain and cool.
Halve zucchini and bell pepper; toss with 1 tbsp olive oil and roast at 425°F for 15 minutes until caramelized; dice.
Halve cherry tomatoes; slice sun-dried tomatoes and olives.
Whisk remaining olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, and oregano for dressing.
Combine couscous, roasted vegetables, cherry tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes, and olives in a large bowl.
Pour dressing over and toss; fold in feta and fresh basil.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Spanish Tortilla
description: Classic Tortilla Española with slowly poached potatoes and onions set in silky golden eggs.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice potatoes (1/8-inch); halve and slice onion thinly.
Heat olive oil in a 10-inch non-stick skillet; add potatoes and onion with salt; cook on medium-low, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are very tender but not browned, about 20 minutes.
Drain potatoes and onions in a colander over a bowl, reserving the oil.
Beat eggs in a large bowl; fold in the warm potato-onion mixture and season with pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp of the reserved oil in the skillet over medium heat; pour in the egg mixture.
Cook until edges are set and bottom is golden, 5-7 minutes; cover skillet with a large plate and flip confidently in one motion.
Slide tortilla back into pan uncooked-side down and cook 3-4 more minutes until just set. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.

name: Carnitas
description: Slow-braised pork shoulder confited in lard and citrus until fall-apart tender and crisped in its own fat.
ingredients: 4 lb pork shoulder cut into 2-inch chunks
instructions: Season pork chunks generously with salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano.
Place pork in a large Dutch oven with lard, garlic, onion, squeezed orange halves (add the juice too), and bay leaves.
Cook covered in a 275°F oven for 3 to 3.5 hours until pork is completely tender and shreddable.
Remove pork from fat and shred into large chunks.
Return shredded pork to a hot cast iron skillet with some of the rendered fat.
Cook undisturbed over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side until crispy and caramelized.
Serve in warm corn tortillas with cilantro, diced onion, and a squeeze of lime.

name: Al Pastor Tacos
description: Marinated pork spit-style with guajillo chiles, achiote, and pineapple served in small corn tortillas.
ingredients: 2 lb boneless pork shoulder thinly sliced
instructions: Toast dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend softened chiles with achiote paste, garlic, onion, vinegar, oregano, cumin, and salt until smooth.
Coat sliced pork thoroughly in the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Cook marinated pork in a hot cast iron skillet or grill pan over high heat in batches until charred at the edges, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Chop cooked pork into small pieces and toss with caramelized pineapple chunks.
Warm tortillas on a comal and fill with pork and pineapple.
Top with diced onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

name: Birria de Res
description: Rich Jalisco-style beef stew braised in a deep red chile consommé until fall-apart tender.
ingredients: 3 lb beef chuck roast cut into 4-inch chunks
instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper, then sear in olive oil in a Dutch oven over high heat until deeply browned on all sides.
Simmer guajillo, ancho, and arbol chiles with tomatoes, onion, cinnamon, and bay leaves in water for 10 minutes until softened.
Blend softened chiles and vegetables with beef broth, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, and cloves until smooth.
Strain blended sauce through a fine mesh strainer over the seared beef.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 3 to 3.5 hours until beef is completely tender.
Remove beef and shred with two forks, then return to the consommé.
Serve in bowls garnished with diced onion, cilantro, and lime wedges alongside warm corn tortillas.

name: Quesabirria Tacos
description: Crispy corn tortillas dipped in birria consommé and filled with shredded beef and melted Oaxaca cheese, served with consommé for dunking.
ingredients: 1 tbsp birria fat skimmed from consommé
salsa verde or salsa roja for serving
instructions: Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium heat and add birria fat.
Dip each corn tortilla briefly in the warm consommé to coat, then place in the hot skillet red side down.
Immediately sprinkle shredded Oaxaca cheese on one half of the tortilla.
Add a generous portion of shredded birria beef on top of the cheese.
Fold the tortilla over and cook for 2 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Repeat with remaining tortillas, adding fresh birria fat as needed.
Serve immediately with small bowls of hot consommé, diced onion, cilantro, and lime for squeezing.

name: Barbacoa
description: Slow-braised beef cheeks or chuck in chile and spice paste, steamed until meltingly tender and deeply flavored.
ingredients: 4 lb beef cheeks or chuck roast
banana leaves or foil for wrapping
instructions: Blend chipotle chiles, soaked ancho chiles, garlic, onion, vinegar, cumin, oregano, cloves, salt, and broth into a smooth paste.
Score beef and coat thoroughly with the chile paste.
Line a large pot or Dutch oven with banana leaves, place seasoned beef inside, add bay leaves, and fold leaves over to enclose.
Add 1 cup water to the bottom of the pot, cover tightly, and cook in a 300°F oven for 5 hours until completely tender.
Alternatively, cook in a slow cooker on low for 8 hours.
Shred the beef and mix with cooking juices.
Serve on warm corn tortillas topped with diced onion, cilantro, and fresh lime juice.

name: Cochinita Pibil
description: Yucatecan slow-roasted pork shoulder marinated in achiote and citrus, wrapped in banana leaves until fall-apart tender.
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder cut into large chunks
instructions: Blend achiote paste, orange juice, lime juice, onion, garlic, salt, and cumin until completely smooth.
Combine pork and marinade in a large bowl, toss to coat, cover, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 325°F.
Line a Dutch oven with banana leaves so they cover the bottom and hang over the sides.
Add marinated pork including all marinade juices, then fold banana leaves over the top.
Cover and bake for 3.5 hours until pork is completely fall-apart tender.
Shred the pork, mix with 1/3 cup of the cooking liquid, and serve in corn tortillas topped with pickled red onions and queso fresco.

name: Tinga de Pollo
description: Shredded chicken in a smoky chipotle-tomato sauce, perfect for tacos or tostadas.
ingredients: corn tortillas or tostada shells for serving
instructions: Poach chicken thighs in seasoned water for 15-20 minutes until cooked through, reserve 1 cup broth, then shred.
Broil tomatoes and onion on a baking sheet for 10 minutes until charred.
Blend charred tomatoes and onion with chipotle peppers, garlic, oregano, cumin, salt, and 1/2 cup reserved broth until smooth.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the blended tinga sauce for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add shredded chicken and stir to coat evenly in the sauce.
Cook for another 10 minutes until sauce thickens and reduces.
Serve on warm tortillas or tostadas with cotija cheese, diced avocado, and cilantro.

name: Enchiladas Verdes
description: Corn tortillas filled with shredded chicken, smothered in bright roasted tomatillo salsa verde, and baked with melted cheese.
ingredients: 2 cups shredded Monterey Jack or Mexican blend cheese
thinly sliced red onion for serving
instructions: Broil tomatillos, jalapeños, and garlic on a baking sheet for 10 minutes flipping halfway until charred.
Blend charred vegetables with onion, cilantro, lime juice, and salt until smooth salsa verde forms.
Preheat oven to 350°F and pour 1/2 cup salsa verde into a 9x13 baking dish.
Warm tortillas in microwave wrapped in damp paper towel for 1 minute until pliable.
Spoon about 2 tbsp chicken onto each tortilla, roll tightly, and place seam-side down in the baking dish.
Pour remaining salsa verde over enchiladas and top with shredded cheese.
Bake for 10-15 minutes until cheese melts and sauce bubbles, then garnish with crema, red onion, and cotija.

name: Enchiladas Rojas
description: Rolled corn tortillas filled with shredded beef and drenched in a rich dried-chile red sauce, topped with crema and onion.
ingredients: 2 cups shredded cooked beef or chicken
instructions: Toast dried chiles briefly in a dry skillet, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes until softened.
Blend softened chiles with tomatoes, garlic, onion, oregano, cumin, and broth until smooth, then strain.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan, add strained chile sauce, and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Dip each corn tortilla in the warm red chile sauce and cook briefly in an oiled skillet for 20 seconds per side.
Fill each sauced tortilla with shredded meat, roll up, and arrange in a baking dish.
Pour remaining sauce over the enchiladas.
Serve topped with crumbled queso fresco, sliced onion, drizzle of crema, and cilantro.

name: Enchiladas Suizas
description: Creamy tomatillo-cream sauce enchiladas stuffed with chicken and blanketed with melted Gruyère or Swiss cheese.
ingredients: 1 cup Mexican crema or heavy cream
1 cup shredded Gruyère or Swiss cheese
instructions: Simmer tomatillos and serrano chiles in water for 10 minutes until soft, then drain.
Blend cooked tomatillos, serranos, garlic, onion, and cilantro until smooth.
In a saucepan over medium heat, cook tomatillo sauce for 5 minutes, then stir in Mexican crema and salt.
Preheat oven to 375°F and spread 1/2 cup sauce in a baking dish.
Briefly fry each tortilla in hot oil for 10 seconds to soften, then fill with chicken and roll tightly.
Arrange rolled enchiladas seam-side down, pour remaining creamy sauce over all, and top with Gruyère and mozzarella.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until bubbly and golden, then serve immediately.

name: Chicken Mole Poblano
description: Roasted chicken smothered in the legendary complex sauce of dried chiles, nuts, spices, and Mexican chocolate from Puebla.
instructions: Toast dried chiles in hot lard for 1-2 minutes per side until fragrant but not burnt, then soak in hot water for 30 minutes.
In the same pot fry onion and garlic until golden, then add almonds, peanuts, raisins, and seeds and cook 3 minutes.
Add tortilla pieces, bread, tomatoes, tomatillos, and all spices and cook 2-3 more minutes.
Add soaked chiles and chicken broth, bring to a boil, then simmer 15 minutes.
Let mixture cool, then blend in batches until completely smooth.
Fry blended mole in remaining hot lard for 5 minutes, stir in chocolate until melted, season with salt, and simmer 20 minutes.
Brown chicken in oil, pour mole over, cover, and braise 45 minutes until chicken is cooked through. Garnish with sesame seeds.

name: Pozole Rojo
description: Hearty Mexican hominy soup with tender pork in a rich guajillo-chile broth, topped with fresh garnishes.
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder cut into 2-inch pieces
1 large can (110 oz) hominy drained and rinsed
instructions: Place pork shoulder and ribs in a large stockpot with water, half the onion, 3 garlic cloves, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, skim foam, then simmer for 1.5 hours.
Remove pork and set aside; strain and reserve the broth.
Toast dried chiles briefly, then soak in 2 cups hot reserved broth with remaining onion for 20 minutes until softened.
Blend soaked chiles, soaking broth, remaining garlic, and oregano until smooth.
Return strained broth to the pot, add rinsed hominy, and bring to a simmer.
Pour strained chile sauce into the broth, stir, and cook 30 minutes.
Shred the cooked pork, add back to the pot, season with salt, and serve in deep bowls with all garnishes on the side.

name: Pozole Verde
description: One-pot green pozole with chicken, tomatillos, and pumpkin seeds in a vibrant herbal broth.
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems
instructions: Toast pumpkin seeds in the bottom of a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat until they pop, about 4 minutes, then transfer to a bowl.
Add chicken, tomatillos, onion, poblanos, jalapeños, chicken stock, oregano, epazote, and salt to the Dutch oven. Bring to a boil then simmer 40 minutes until chicken is tender.
Remove chicken and set aside to cool. Strain broth and transfer solids to a blender.
Add toasted pumpkin seeds and cilantro to the blender and blend until completely smooth.
Return strained broth to the pot over medium heat, whisk in the green puree, and add hominy. Bring to a simmer.
Shred chicken and stir back into the soup. Season with salt.
Ladle into bowls and serve with avocado, radishes, cabbage, and lime.

name: Chiles Rellenos
description: Whole roasted poblano chiles stuffed with Oaxaca cheese, dipped in light egg batter, and simmered in tomato broth.
ingredients: 2 cups shredded Oaxaca or Monterey Jack cheese
1/2 cup lard or neutral oil for frying
instructions: Blister poblano peppers directly over an open flame or under the broiler on all sides until charred, then place in a bowl, cover with foil, and steam for 10 minutes.
Peel off charred skin, make a vertical slit, and carefully remove seeds with a spoon, keeping pepper intact.
Stuff each pepper with shredded cheese and seal with a toothpick. Lightly dust in flour and place in freezer for 10 minutes.
Beat egg whites to stiff peaks, then fold in yolks one at a time to form a light batter.
Heat oil to 325°F. Dip stuffed peppers in egg batter and fry for 3-4 minutes per side until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Blend tomatoes, onion, and garlic; cook in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes; add broth, bay leaves, oregano, and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Add fried chiles to the tomato broth and simmer gently for 20 minutes before serving.

name: Tamales de Puerco (Red Chile Pork Tamales)
description: Traditional masa-wrapped tamales filled with tender pork in red guajillo-chile sauce, steamed in corn husks.
instructions: Soak corn husks in very hot water for 30 minutes until pliable.
Simmer pork in salted water with onion and garlic for 1.5 hours until tender, then shred and reserve broth.
Toast chiles, soak in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend with garlic, onion, cumin, and 1 cup pork broth until smooth. Strain.
Simmer strained chile sauce with shredded pork for 10 minutes.
Beat lard until fluffy, then mix in masa harina, baking powder, salt, and warm broth to form a soft spreadable dough.
Spread a thin layer of masa on the wide end of each husk, add a spoonful of pork filling, and fold the husk to enclose. Fold up the narrow end.
Steam upright in a steamer pot over boiling water for 50-60 minutes until masa pulls cleanly from the husk.

name: Tamales de Pollo con Rajas (Chicken and Poblano Tamales)
description: Light steamed masa tamales filled with shredded chicken and roasted poblano strips in a tangy salsa verde.
ingredients: 1.5 lb boneless chicken thighs poached and shredded
3 poblano peppers roasted peeled and cut into strips
instructions: Soak corn husks in hot water for 30 minutes until soft and pliable.
Mix shredded chicken with salsa verde and sliced roasted poblano strips; season with salt.

Beat lard in a stand mixer until fluffy, about 5 minutes. Gradually add masa harina, baking powder, salt, and warm broth, beating until a soft spreadable dough forms. Test readiness by dropping a small ball of dough in water; it should float.
Spread 2-3 tbsp masa dough onto the wide end of a soaked corn husk, leaving a 1-inch border.
Spoon chicken and poblano filling down the center.
Fold one side of the husk over the filling, then fold the other side over, and fold up the narrow bottom end.
Steam tamales upright in a steamer pot for 50-60 minutes, checking water level periodically.

name: Chilaquiles Rojos
description: Lightly fried tortilla chips simmered in smoky guajillo-tomato salsa roja and topped with eggs, crema, and cotija.
instructions: Toast guajillo chiles in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side, soak in hot water for 10 minutes, then blend with tomatoes, onion, garlic, oregano, and broth until smooth. Strain.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add strained sauce, and simmer for 8 minutes until reduced and deep in color.
Meanwhile, fry tortilla triangles in remaining oil at 350°F until lightly crispy but not hard, about 2 minutes. Drain.
Add fried tortilla chips to the sauce and gently stir to coat. Cook for 2-3 minutes; chips should soften slightly but retain some texture.
In a separate pan fry eggs sunny-side up.
Divide chilaquiles between plates and top with fried eggs.
Drizzle with crema, sprinkle with cotija and sliced onion, and garnish with cilantro.

name: Chilaquiles Verdes
description: Crispy tortilla chips bathed in bright tomatillo-chipotle salsa verde with chorizo and sunny-side up eggs.
instructions: Roast tomatillos in a 350°F oven for 15-20 minutes until army green in color.
Blend roasted tomatillos with chipotle chiles, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Toss tortilla triangles in a thin layer of olive oil on a sheet pan and bake at 350°F for 13 minutes until lightly golden.
Cook chorizo in the oven or a skillet until cooked through.
Heat a dollop of oil in a skillet over medium heat, add tomatillo sauce, and cook for a few minutes until bubbly.
Fry eggs sunny-side up in a separate pan.
Add baked tortilla chips to the sauce, stir quickly to coat, plate immediately with fried eggs, cilantro, and chorizo on the side.

name: Huevos Rancheros
description: Fried corn tortillas topped with refried beans and sunny-side up eggs smothered in a spicy ranch-style tomato salsa.
instructions: Blend tomatoes, serrano, onion, garlic, and thyme with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat, pour in blended sauce, and simmer for 10 minutes until thick and deep red. Season with salt.
Heat 1/4 cup oil in a medium skillet over medium heat and fry tortillas one at a time for about 20 seconds per side until just softened. Drain on paper towels.
In the same oil, fry eggs sunny-side up until whites are set and yolks remain runny.
Spread a generous spoonful of warm refried beans over each tortilla.
Place 2 fried tortillas on each plate and gently lay one fried egg on each tortilla.
Spoon warm salsa ranchera over the eggs and garnish with cilantro and crumbled queso fresco.

name: Tacos de Camarón (Grilled Shrimp Tacos)
description: Juicy chipotle-marinated grilled shrimp in corn tortillas with avocado crema and cabbage slaw.
ingredients: 1.5 lb large shrimp peeled and deveined
1/2 cup Mexican crema or sour cream
instructions: Blend chipotle peppers, olive oil, garlic, cumin, paprika, and salt into a marinade. Toss shrimp with marinade and let sit for 15 minutes.
Make avocado crema by blending avocado, crema, and lime juice until smooth; season with salt.
Toss shredded cabbage with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt.
Grill or cook shrimp in a hot skillet over high heat for 2 minutes per side until pink, opaque, and lightly charred.
Warm corn tortillas on a dry comal or skillet.
Build tacos with 3-4 shrimp per tortilla.
Top with cabbage slaw, a drizzle of avocado crema, sliced jalapeño, and fresh cilantro.

name: Tacos de Huevo con Chorizo (Breakfast Tacos)
description: Scrambled eggs cooked with spicy Mexican chorizo and potato, served in warm corn tortillas for a hearty Mexican breakfast.
instructions: Heat oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat and cook diced potato for 8-10 minutes until golden and tender. Remove and set aside.
In the same skillet, cook chorizo over medium heat breaking up with a spoon for 5 minutes until browned and fat is rendered.
Add diced onion and serrano and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Crack eggs directly into the pan and scramble together with the chorizo mixture over medium-low heat.
Fold in cooked potato and diced tomato and cook just until eggs are set but still slightly moist.
Warm tortillas wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave for 1 minute.
Fill tortillas with egg and chorizo mixture and serve with salsa roja, cilantro, and lime wedges.

name: Tostadas de Tinga
description: Crunchy fried tortilla rounds piled with chipotle chicken tinga, refried beans, lettuce, avocado, and cotija cheese.
ingredients: 8 tostada shells (store-bought or homemade fried corn tortillas)
2 cups chicken tinga (shredded chicken in chipotle-tomato sauce)
instructions: If making tostada shells from scratch, fry 6-inch corn tortillas in 1/4 inch of oil at 350°F for 1-2 minutes per side until completely crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Warm refried beans in a small saucepan over medium heat with a splash of water, stirring until smooth.
Warm chicken tinga in a skillet over medium heat until heated through.
Spread a generous spoonful of warm refried beans on each tostada shell.
Top with a portion of chicken tinga.
Layer with shredded lettuce and sliced avocado.
Finish with a drizzle of crema, crumbled cotija, salsa verde, and a squeeze of lime.

name: Sopes
description: Thick handmade masa discs with pinched edges, lightly fried and loaded with refried beans, meat, crema, and salsa.
ingredients: 1.5 cups cooked shredded beef or chicken
instructions: Mix masa harina and warm water until a smooth dough forms, like play dough. Cover with a damp cloth and rest 5 minutes.
Divide into 8 equal balls and press each between plastic wrap to form a 4.5-inch round about 1/4-inch thick.
Cook on a hot ungreased comal over medium-high heat for 1 minute per side, flip once more for 20 seconds.
While still hot, pinch a 1/2-inch rim around the edge of each sope to create a wall for the toppings.
Heat oil in a skillet and lightly fry the sopes 30 seconds per side until light golden.
Spread warm refried beans over each sope.
Top with shredded meat, lettuce, queso fresco, diced onion, crema, and salsa.

name: Flautas de Pollo
description: Tightly rolled corn tortillas filled with spiced chicken and deep-fried until golden and crunchy, served with guacamole and salsa.
ingredients: 1.5 lb boneless chicken thighs poached and shredded
1/4 cup crumbled cotija or queso fresco
instructions: Mix shredded chicken with diced tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, and salt. Cook in a skillet for 5 minutes to reduce moisture.
Warm corn tortillas in a damp paper towel in the microwave for 1-2 minutes until pliable.
Place a heaping spoonful of chicken filling on each tortilla, roll tightly, and secure with a toothpick along the seam.
Heat vegetable oil to 350°F in a deep skillet.
Fry flautas in batches of 3-4, cooking 1.5-2 minutes per side until deeply golden. Drain on paper towels and remove toothpicks.
Arrange on a platter over a bed of shredded lettuce.
Top with guacamole, salsa verde, a drizzle of crema, and crumbled cotija.

name: Elote (Mexican Street Corn)
description: Grilled corn on the cob slathered in creamy mayo and crema, rolled in cotija cheese and dusted with chili powder.
ingredients: 2 tbsp Mexican crema or sour cream
instructions: Grill corn directly over medium-high heat, turning every 2-3 minutes for about 12 minutes until cooked and lightly charred in spots.
Alternatively, boil corn in salted water for 10 minutes then grill briefly for char.
Mix mayonnaise and Mexican crema together in a small bowl.
While corn is still hot, brush the creamy mixture all over each ear.
Roll or press each corn ear into crumbled cotija cheese to coat generously.
Dust with chili powder and a squeeze of fresh lime juice.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve immediately on a stick or as is.

name: Esquites (Mexican Street Corn in a Cup)
description: Off-the-cob version of elote featuring sautéed corn kernels in a cup with lime, mayo, chili, and cotija cheese.
ingredients: 4 ears corn kernels cut from cob (about 4 cups)
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over high heat until slightly browned.
Add corn kernels in a single layer and cook undisturbed for 3-4 minutes until kernels begin to char on one side.
Add diced onion and serrano and stir, cooking another 2 minutes.
Add epazote or cilantro and toss to combine. Season with salt.
Divide corn mixture into cups or bowls.
Top each serving with a tablespoon of mayo, a drizzle of crema, and a big squeeze of lime.
Sprinkle generously with cotija and chili powder and serve immediately.

name: Salsa Verde
description: Bright roasted tomatillo salsa with serrano chile, onion, garlic, and cilantro — the essential Mexican green table sauce.
instructions: Remove stems from tomatillos and place on a baking sheet.
Roast tomatillos in a 400°F oven for 15-20 minutes until they start to wrinkle and turn army green in color.
Add roasted tomatillos to a blender.
Add onion, garlic, cilantro, and 1/4 of the serrano pepper to the blender.
Pulse blend and taste for heat level; add more serrano incrementally until the desired spice is reached.
Salt to taste.
Serve immediately or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

name: Pico de Gallo
description: Fresh uncooked salsa of ripe tomatoes, white onion, jalapeño, lime juice, and cilantro — the classic Mexican fresh salsa.
ingredients: 4 medium ripe Roma tomatoes seeded and finely diced
1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves roughly chopped
instructions: Dice tomatoes and place in a fine mesh strainer for 5 minutes to drain excess juice.
Finely dice the white onion and mince the jalapeño, adjusting seeds for desired heat level.
Combine drained tomatoes, onion, and jalapeño in a medium bowl.
Add chopped cilantro and pour in lime juice.
Season with salt and stir gently to combine.
Let rest for at least 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Taste and adjust lime juice and salt as needed before serving.

name: Guacamole
description: Classic hand-mashed avocado dip with lime, jalapeño, white onion, cilantro, and tomato — made to order in a molcajete.
ingredients: 1 small Roma tomato seeded and diced
3 tbsp fresh cilantro leaves roughly chopped
instructions: Halve and pit avocados, then scoop flesh into a molcajete or large bowl.
Add lime juice and salt and mash with a pestle or fork to your desired texture — chunky is preferred.
Fold in minced onion, jalapeño, and garlic if using.
Add diced tomato and cilantro and stir gently to combine.
Taste and adjust salt and lime juice as needed.
If not serving immediately, press plastic wrap directly onto the surface to prevent browning.
Serve at room temperature with tortilla chips or alongside tacos.

name: Frijoles Refritos (Refried Beans)
description: Authentic pinto beans cooked from scratch and mashed with lard, garlic, and jalapeño into a creamy, deeply savory side dish.
ingredients: 1 lb dried pinto beans rinsed and picked over
instructions: Combine beans, half the onion, 2 smashed garlic cloves, bay leaf, 1/2 tsp oregano, and 1.5 tsp salt in a large pot with enough water to cover by 3 inches.
Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5-2 hours until beans are completely soft. Reserve cooking liquid and discard bay leaf.
Finely dice remaining onion half and 3 garlic cloves.
Heat oil or lard in the same pot over medium-high heat and add diced onion, garlic, jalapeño, remaining oregano, and salt. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add cooked beans and stir for 2 minutes. Add 3/4 cup reserved cooking liquid.
Mash beans with a potato masher for chunky texture or use an immersion blender for smooth, adding more liquid as needed.
Taste and adjust salt; serve topped with cotija cheese and a squeeze of lime.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
description: Sichuan stir-fry with tender chicken, dried chilies, peanuts, and a bold sweet-spicy-tangy sauce.
ingredients: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs cut into 3/4-inch cubes
instructions: Toss chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch; marinate 15 minutes.
Mix sauce: remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, hoisin, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Heat wok over high heat until smoking; add oil and stir-fry chilies and peppercorns 30 seconds.
Add chicken and stir-fry 3-4 minutes until cooked through; remove from wok.
Add garlic and ginger; stir-fry 30 seconds.
Return chicken to wok; pour in sauce and toss to coat.
Add scallions and peanuts; toss for 30 seconds and serve over rice.

name: General Tso's Chicken
description: Crispy fried chicken tossed in a glossy sweet-spicy-savory sauce, a Chinese-American takeout classic.
ingredients: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs cut into 2-inch pieces
1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
instructions: Marinate chicken with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and baking soda for 20 minutes.
Mix cornstarch and flour; coat chicken pieces evenly and shake off excess.
Heat oil to 350°F and fry chicken in batches 3-4 minutes until golden; drain on paper towels.
Combine sauce ingredients: soy sauce, stock, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil in a bowl.
In a clean wok heat 1 tbsp oil; fry chilies, garlic, and ginger 30 seconds.
Add sauce and bring to simmer; add cornstarch slurry and stir to thicken.
Toss fried chicken in sauce and serve immediately with rice.

name: Mapo Tofu
description: Silky tofu simmered in a fiery Sichuan sauce of doubanjiang, ground pork, and numbing peppercorns.
ingredients: 14 oz firm tofu cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Bring salted water to boil; gently simmer tofu cubes 3 minutes and drain.
Heat oil in wok over medium-high; add pork and cook until browned, breaking into small pieces.
Add doubanjiang and stir-fry 1-2 minutes until darkened and fragrant.
Add garlic and ginger; stir-fry 30 seconds.
Pour in stock, soy sauce, wine, and sugar; bring to a gentle boil.
Slide tofu in carefully; simmer 3-4 minutes to absorb flavors.
Stir in cornstarch slurry and cook until sauce thickens.
Drizzle with sesame oil, sprinkle Sichuan peppercorn powder and scallions; serve over rice.

name: Char Siu
description: Cantonese honey-glazed BBQ pork marinated overnight in a fragrant five-spice and hoisin sauce.
ingredients: 2 lb pork shoulder cut into 1-inch thick strips
instructions: Pierce pork strips all over with a fork; combine garlic salt, brown sugar, oyster sauce, soy sauce, hoisin, Shaoxing wine, mashed red bean curd, and five spice into a marinade.
Coat pork in marinade and refrigerate overnight or at least 8 hours.
Preheat oven to 425°F; line a baking pan with foil and set a rack on top.
Lay pork on rack and add 2 tbsp water to pan bottom.
Roast 15 minutes; baste with reserved marinade, flip and baste; roast another 15 minutes.
Mix honey with 2 tsp water for glaze; baste pork and roast 10 more minutes at 450°F.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing; serve with rice or use in fried rice.

name: Chinese Potstickers
description: Pan-fried dumplings with a pork and cabbage filling, crispy on the bottom and tender on top.
ingredients: 1 cup napa cabbage finely chopped and salted
instructions: Mix flour with boiling water; knead into smooth dough and rest covered 30 minutes.
Salt cabbage, let sit 10 minutes, then squeeze out excess liquid; mix with pork, scallions, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, sugar, and white pepper.
Roll dough into a log; cut into 24 pieces and roll each into a 3-inch round.
Place 1 tsp filling in center; fold and pleat edges to seal.
Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high; arrange dumplings flat-side down and cook 2 minutes until golden.
Add 1/2 cup water and cover; steam 6-7 minutes until water evaporates.
Uncover and cook another minute until bottoms are crispy; serve with dipping sauce.

name: Yangzhou Fried Rice
description: Classic Chinese fried rice with shrimp, char siu pork, eggs, and vegetables tossed over high heat.
ingredients: 3 large eggs beaten with pinch of salt
2 scallions separated into white and green parts
instructions: Blanch carrots and peas 40 seconds; cook shrimp in same water 3 minutes; drain and set aside.
Heat wok to high heat until smoking; add 1 tbsp oil.
Pour in eggs and immediately add rice; stir-fry vigorously 2-3 minutes until eggs coat the grains.
