Season with salt and soy sauce; push rice to sides and add char siu to center; cook 1 minute.
Mix char siu into rice; add shrimp, peas, and carrots; stir-fry on high 2 minutes.
Add remaining oil and scallion greens; toss to combine and serve immediately.

name: Dan Dan Noodles
description: Sichuan spicy noodles topped with seasoned pork mince in a sesame-chili sauce with preserved mustard greens.
ingredients: 2 oz sui mi ya cai (preserved mustard greens)
instructions: Make the sauce: whisk together sesame paste, chili oil, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, chicken stock, and Sichuan peppercorn; divide among 4 bowls.
Cook pork with hoisin, soy sauce, wine, and five spice until browned; set aside.
Warm preserved mustard greens briefly in pan; set aside.
Cook noodles per package directions; blanch any greens in last minute and drain.
Divide noodles among bowls over the sauce.
Top with pork, preserved mustard greens, scallions, and crushed peanuts.
Toss everything together before eating.

name: Pad See Ew
description: Thai stir-fried wide rice noodles with Chinese broccoli, egg, and a sweet dark soy sauce.
ingredients: 8 oz wide fresh rice noodles (chow fun)
2 stalks Chinese broccoli cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Marinate chicken with soy sauce and sugar 10 minutes.
Separate noodles into individual strands; if refrigerated warm briefly in microwave.
Mix sauce: oyster sauce, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar.
Heat wok on high until smoking; add oil and fry garlic 15 seconds.
Add chicken; stir-fry until just cooked through; push to the side and crack in egg.
Scramble egg until 70% set then mix with chicken.
Add noodles and sauce; toss to coat and spread noodles out to sear and get wok char.
Add Chinese broccoli; toss briefly until stems are tender-crisp; season with white pepper and serve.

name: Pad Krapow Gai
description: Thai street-food classic of ground chicken stir-fried with holy basil, chilies, and a savory sauce, topped with a fried egg.
ingredients: 1 cup holy basil leaves loosely packed
instructions: Pound Thai chilies to a paste in mortar; add garlic and pound to a rough paste.
Combine oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, dark soy sauce, water, and sugar; stir until dissolved.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over medium-high; fry chili-garlic paste until garlic is golden, 1-2 minutes.
Add onion and cook 30 seconds.
Add ground chicken and toss until no longer pink.
Pour in sauce; toss until chicken is coated; turn off heat and stir in holy basil to wilt.
In separate pan heat 2 tbsp oil; fry eggs with very hot oil until edges are crispy.
Serve stir-fry over jasmine rice topped with a fried egg.

name: Thai Red Curry
description: Creamy coconut milk curry with tender chicken and vegetables in a vibrant Thai red curry paste.
ingredients: 1.5 lb boneless chicken thighs cut into pieces
1 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok or pot over medium-high; fry curry paste 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add half the coconut milk and stir to combine; cook 3-4 minutes until oil separates.
Add chicken and stir to coat; cook until mostly done, 5-6 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk, stock, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves.
Add fish sauce and sugar; simmer 10 minutes.
Add bell pepper and zucchini; simmer 5 more minutes until tender.
Stir in Thai basil; taste and adjust seasoning; serve over jasmine rice.

name: Massaman Curry
description: Rich Thai curry with tender braised beef, potatoes, and peanuts in a warming massaman paste and coconut milk.
ingredients: 1.5 lb beef chuck cut into 2-inch pieces
2 cans (14 oz each) full-fat coconut milk
1 tbsp palm sugar or brown sugar
instructions: Heat 1/4 cup coconut milk in a pot over medium heat; add curry paste and fry 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add beef and stir to coat in paste; cook 5 minutes, browning lightly.
Add remaining coconut milk, cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaves, and kaffir lime leaves; bring to simmer.
Cover and braise on low heat 40 minutes until beef is nearly tender.
Add potatoes and onion; cook 15 more minutes until potatoes are cooked through.
Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, tamarind paste, and peanuts.
Simmer uncovered 5 minutes; adjust seasoning and serve with jasmine rice.

name: Goi Cuon
description: Fresh Vietnamese spring rolls filled with pork belly, shrimp, rice vermicelli, and herbs, served with peanut sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 lb medium shrimp peeled and deveined
instructions: Simmer pork belly in water with salt and onion 25-30 minutes until cooked; cool and slice thin.
Boil shrimp in salted water 2 minutes; drain, cool, peel, and halve lengthwise.
Cook rice vermicelli per package directions; rinse in cold water and drain.
Make peanut sauce: sauté garlic in oil 30 seconds; add hoisin, peanut butter, and water; simmer until thick.
Dip rice paper in warm water 4-6 seconds; lay on plate.
Layer lettuce, herbs, noodles, and pork belly on bottom third; roll halfway.
Place 3 shrimp halves pink-side down; fold in sides and roll tightly.
Serve immediately with peanut sauce topped with crushed peanuts.

name: Bun Cha
description: Hanoi-style grilled pork patties and belly served in a light sweet-savory broth with rice noodles and herbs.
instructions: Mix ground pork with shallots, fish sauce, sugar, pepper, and baking soda; form into 12 patties.
Marinate pork belly slices in fish sauce, sugar, and shallots 15 minutes.
Make broth: dissolve sugar in hot water; add fish sauce, vinegar, garlic, and chili.
Grill or pan-fry pork patties over medium-high heat 3-4 minutes per side until caramelized.
Grill pork belly slices 2 minutes per side.
Place grilled meats in broth to serve.
Serve with rice vermicelli, fresh herbs, and bean sprouts alongside; dip noodles into broth.

name: Chicken Teriyaki
description: Juicy chicken thighs glazed in a homemade teriyaki sauce of soy, mirin, and sake, grilled to perfection.
instructions: Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a small bowl to make teriyaki sauce.
Pat chicken dry; season lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high; lay chicken skin-side down and cook 5-6 minutes until skin is golden.
Flip and cook 4-5 more minutes until cooked through.
Pour in teriyaki sauce and simmer, turning chicken to glaze, until sauce thickens and coats the chicken, 2-3 minutes.
Slice chicken and serve over steamed rice; garnish with scallions and sesame seeds.

name: Gyudon
description: Japanese beef rice bowl with thinly sliced ribeye and onion simmered in a savory-sweet dashi broth.
ingredients: pickled red ginger (beni shoga) for serving
instructions: In a cold frying pan combine dashi, sake, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar; stir to dissolve sugar.
Spread onion slices in the broth; separate beef slices and layer on top of onions.
Cover and turn heat to medium; bring to a simmer and cook 3-4 minutes.
Skim any scum that rises to the surface.
Sprinkle green onions on top; cook covered another minute.
Divide rice into bowls; drizzle with pan sauce; top with beef and onion mixture.
Garnish with pickled red ginger and serve immediately.

name: Katsudon
description: Japanese pork cutlet rice bowl with a soft egg and onion simmered in a dashi-soy sauce.
ingredients: 2 pork loin chops (6 oz each) pounded thin
instructions: Season pork with salt and pepper; dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat in panko.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 350°F and fry pork cutlets 3-4 minutes per side until golden; drain and rest before cutting.
In a small skillet simmer onion in dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar 3-4 minutes until softened.
Slice katsu into strips; lay over the onion mixture.
Beat 3 eggs and pour over the cutlet; cover and cook on medium-low until eggs are just set, 1-2 minutes.
Slide over a bowl of steamed rice and serve immediately.

name: Okonomiyaki
description: Japanese savory cabbage pancake with pork belly, topped with okonomiyaki sauce, mayo, and bonito flakes.
ingredients: 4 tbsp okonomiyaki sauce (or Worcestershire mixed with ketchup)
instructions: Whisk flour and dashi until smooth; beat in eggs until combined.
Fold in shredded cabbage and scallions to make a thick batter.
Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium; pour in half the batter and shape into a round pancake.
Lay pork belly slices on top; press gently into batter.
Cook 4-5 minutes until the underside is set and golden.
Flip carefully and cook the pork side 4-5 minutes until cooked through and caramelized.
Flip once more; transfer to plate and drizzle with okonomiyaki sauce and mayo; top with bonito flakes and aonori.

name: Tonkatsu
description: Japanese breaded and deep-fried pork cutlet served with tangy tonkatsu sauce and shredded cabbage.
ingredients: 2 pork loin chops (6 oz each) pounded to 1/2-inch thickness
instructions: Mix Worcestershire, ketchup, oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sugar for tonkatsu sauce; set aside.
Pat pork dry; make small cuts along fat cap to prevent curling; season with salt and white pepper.
Dredge in flour, shake off excess; dip in beaten egg; press into panko on all sides.
Heat oil to 340-350°F; fry pork 4-5 minutes per side until deep golden brown and cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack 2 minutes then slice into strips.
Serve over rice with shredded cabbage; drizzle tonkatsu sauce over cutlet.

name: Japanese Curry Rice
description: Mild and comforting Japanese curry with chicken, potatoes, and carrots in a rich roux-based sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs cut into 1-inch pieces
3.5 oz Japanese curry roux (1/2 block such as S&B or Vermont)
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high; brown chicken in batches and remove.
Sauté onions until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Return chicken; add carrots and potatoes and stir to coat.
Pour in water or stock and bring to a boil; skim off foam.
Reduce heat and simmer 20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Remove from heat and break curry roux blocks into the pot; stir until fully dissolved.
Return to low heat; add soy sauce and simmer 5 minutes, stirring until sauce thickens.
Serve over steamed rice.

name: Miso-Glazed Eggplant
description: Silky Japanese eggplant broiled with a sweet miso glaze until caramelized and deeply savory.
instructions: Preheat broiler to high and line a baking sheet with foil.
Halve eggplants lengthwise; score the flesh in a crosshatch pattern and brush with vegetable oil.
Broil eggplant cut-side up 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly charred.
Mix miso, mirin, sake, and sugar until smooth.
Spread miso glaze generously over eggplant cut surfaces.
Broil another 3-5 minutes until glaze is caramelized and bubbly.
Drizzle with sesame oil; garnish with sesame seeds and scallions; serve immediately.

name: Bibimbap
description: Korean mixed rice bowl with seasoned vegetables, beef, a fried egg, and gochujang sauce.
ingredients: 1 cup bean sprouts blanched and seasoned
instructions: Cook each vegetable (spinach, bean sprouts, carrots, zucchini) separately in oil with a pinch of salt and garlic; season with sesame oil.
Cook beef with soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and garlic until browned.
Mix gochujang sauce: gochujang, sesame oil, sugar, and water.
Fry eggs sunny-side up in a nonstick pan.
Divide rice into 4 bowls.
Arrange vegetables, beef, and a fried egg on top of rice.
Drizzle with gochujang sauce and sesame seeds; mix everything together before eating.

name: Japchae
description: Korean glass noodle stir-fry with sweet potato noodles, colorful vegetables, beef, and sesame seasoning.
ingredients: 8 oz sweet potato starch noodles (dangmyeon) soaked 40 minutes
4 oz beef filet minced sliced thin
4 dried shiitake mushrooms soaked and sliced
instructions: Marinate beef with soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic; cook in pan until done; set aside.
Sauté onion, carrot, bell pepper, and mushrooms separately with pinches of salt; set aside.
Season spinach with soy sauce and sesame oil.
Boil noodles per package directions until chewy; drain and cut with scissors into 5-inch lengths.
Toss noodles with 2 tsp sesame oil and 1 tsp soy sauce to prevent sticking.
Combine all ingredients in a large bowl with soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, and black pepper.
Mix well by hand; top with egg garnish strips and sesame seeds; serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Kimchijeon
description: Crispy and tangy Korean kimchi pancake made with well-fermented kimchi and scallions.
ingredients: 1/2 lb well-fermented napa cabbage kimchi chopped
instructions: Combine kimchi, kimchi brine, scallions, sugar, flour, and water in a bowl; mix until a batter forms.
Heat a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat; add 2 tbsp oil and swirl to coat.
Pour in batter and spread into a large circle with the back of a spoon.
Cook until bottom is golden brown and crisp, 3-5 minutes.
Drizzle remaining 2 tbsp oil around edges; carefully flip the pancake.
Cook until other side is golden brown and crisp, 3-5 minutes.
Flip once more and cook 1 more minute; slide onto a platter and serve with dipping sauce.

name: Tteokbokki
description: Chewy Korean rice cakes simmered in a spicy gochujang-anchovy broth with fish cakes and scallions.
ingredients: 2 fish cake sheets cut into triangles
instructions: Boil water with anchovies and kelp over medium-high 15 minutes; remove and discard.
Mix gochujang, gochugaru, sugar, and soy sauce in a small bowl.
Add rice cakes and fish cakes to the anchovy broth and bring to a boil.
Stir in the spicy sauce mixture.
Cook stirring gently until rice cakes soften and the sauce thickens and looks shiny, 10-15 minutes; add water if needed.
Add scallions and hard-boiled eggs; stir gently and cook 1-2 more minutes.
Remove from heat and serve hot.

name: Sweet and Sour Pork
description: Twice-fried crispy pork tossed with vibrant bell peppers and pineapple in a glossy sweet and sour sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb pork shoulder cut into 1-inch pieces
1 red bell pepper cut into chunks
1 green bell pepper cut into chunks
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water
instructions: Marinate pork with garlic salt, soy sauce, and beaten egg 20 minutes.
Coat pork in flour then cornstarch; fry at 325°F 7-8 minutes until cooked through; drain.
Heat oil to 400°F and fry pork again 1-2 minutes for extra crispiness.
Make sauce: combine sugar, vinegar, ketchup, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and water in a pan and bring to simmer.
Stir-fry bell peppers and pineapple in a clean wok 1-2 minutes.
Add sauce and cornstarch slurry; simmer until thickened, 1-2 minutes.
Toss in fried pork quickly; serve immediately over rice.

name: Pancit Canton
description: Filipino stir-fried egg noodles with pork, shrimp, and vegetables in a soy-oyster sauce.
ingredients: calamansi or lemon wedges for serving
instructions: Heat oil in a large wok over medium-high; sauté garlic and onion until soft.
Add pork and cook until browned; add shrimp and cook 2 minutes until pink.
Add carrots and cook 2 minutes; add cabbage and snow peas and stir-fry 2 more minutes.
Push vegetables to the side and add chicken broth, soy sauce, oyster sauce, and fish sauce to the center.
Add noodles and toss to coat; cook 3-5 minutes until noodles are tender, adding more broth if needed.
Mix everything together; season with black pepper.
Serve with calamansi or lemon wedges squeezed over top.

name: Lumpia Shanghai
description: Crispy Filipino fried spring rolls filled with seasoned ground pork and vegetables, served with sweet chili sauce.
ingredients: 3 cups vegetable oil for deep frying
instructions: Mix ground pork, carrots, water chestnuts, garlic, onion, soy sauce, sesame oil, and black pepper until combined.
Beat egg and set aside.
Place 2 tbsp filling along one edge of a lumpia wrapper; roll tightly halfway, fold in sides, and roll completely; seal edge with beaten egg.
Heat oil to 350°F in a deep pan.
Fry lumpia in batches 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy; do not crowd the pan.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with sweet chili sauce.

name: Palak Paneer
description: Indian cottage cheese cubes in a vibrant spinach sauce spiced with garam masala and aromatic spices.
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling salted water 2 minutes; drain and blend to a smooth puree.
Pan-fry paneer cubes in 1 tbsp ghee until golden on two sides; remove and set aside.
In same pan heat remaining ghee; fry cumin seeds until they sputter.
Add onion and cook until golden, 8-10 minutes; add garlic, ginger, and green chili; cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, and cayenne; cook 8-10 minutes until oil separates.
Stir in spinach puree; add garam masala and kasuri methi; simmer 5 minutes.
Fold in paneer and cream; simmer 3 more minutes; serve with naan or rice.

name: Dal Makhani
description: Slow-cooked black lentils and kidney beans in a rich buttery tomato cream sauce, a Punjabi classic.
instructions: Soak lentils and kidney beans overnight; drain and rinse.
Pressure cook with 3.5 cups water for 18-20 whistles (or Instant Pot high pressure 30 minutes) until very soft.
Heat butter and oil in a pan; fry cumin seeds until they pop.
Add onion and cook until light golden, 10 minutes; add garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes.
Add crushed tomatoes, chili powder, and turmeric; cook 10-15 minutes until oil separates.
Add cooked lentils and 1 cup water; stir to combine; simmer on low 30-45 minutes stirring every 10 minutes.
Stir in cream and garam masala; simmer 5 more minutes; garnish with cilantro and serve with naan.

name: Beef Rendang
description: Malaysian slow-braised beef in a rich coconut and spice paste that reduces until the meat is tender and caramelized.
ingredients: 2 lb beef chuck cut into 2-inch cubes
4 dried red chilies soaked and drained
1 turmeric leaf tied in a knot
1 tbsp palm sugar or brown sugar
instructions: Blend chilies, shallots, garlic, galangal, and ginger to a fine paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over high; sear beef in batches until browned; remove.
Reduce heat to medium; fry spice paste 3-4 minutes until darkened and fragrant.
Return beef; add coconut milk, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric leaf, sugar, and salt.
Bring to a simmer then reduce heat to low; cover and cook 75 minutes until beef is tender.
Uncover and increase heat to medium; stir frequently and cook 30-40 minutes until sauce reduces to a thick paste that coats the beef and meat begins to brown.
Stir in kerisik if using; taste and adjust seasoning; serve with steamed rice.

name: Matzo Ball Soup
description: Classic Ashkenazi chicken broth with fluffy, tender matzo balls simmered to perfection.
instructions: Place chicken in a large stockpot, cover with 5 quarts water, bring to a boil and skim foam.
Add carrots, celery, onion, dill, salt, and pepper; simmer covered for 90 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Strain broth, reserving vegetables and picking chicken meat from bones; discard skin and bones.
For matzo balls, whisk eggs with schmaltz in a bowl; stir in matzo meal, baking powder, and salt until combined.
Refrigerate matzo ball mixture for 30 minutes to firm up.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil; with wet hands form mixture into golf-ball-sized balls and drop into boiling water.
Reduce heat to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook matzo balls for 30 minutes until puffed and cooked through.
Add matzo balls and reserved chicken meat to the warm broth and serve garnished with fresh dill.

name: Slow-Braised Brisket
description: Tender beef brisket braised low and slow with caramelized onions, garlic, and rich savory sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Season brisket generously with paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper on all sides.
Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat; sear brisket 4-5 minutes per side until deeply browned; remove and set aside.
Sauté onions in the same pot over medium heat for 15 minutes until caramelized; add garlic and cook 2 minutes more.
Whisk together beef stock, ketchup, chili sauce, and brown sugar; pour over onions.
Return brisket to pot, spoon sauce over top, cover tightly with foil and lid.
Braise in oven for 3 to 3.5 hours until very tender when pierced with a fork.
Cool, refrigerate overnight, slice against the grain, and reheat covered in sauce before serving.

name: Potato Latkes
description: Crispy golden shredded potato pancakes fried until crunchy outside and tender inside for Hanukkah.
ingredients: 3 tbsp matzo meal or all-purpose flour
Sour cream and applesauce for serving
instructions: Grate potatoes using a food processor or box grater; transfer to a large bowl of cold water for 5 minutes.
Grate onion using the same grater and set aside.
Drain potatoes in a colander, then wrap in a clean kitchen towel and squeeze firmly to remove as much liquid as possible.
In a large bowl, combine dry potatoes, grated onion, beaten eggs, matzo meal, salt, and pepper; stir to combine.
Pour oil into a large skillet to a depth of 1/4 inch and heat over medium to 365°F.
Working in batches, scoop about 3 tablespoons of mixture per latke, flatten into a disk, and carefully place in hot oil.
Fry 2-3 minutes per side until deeply golden and crispy; do not crowd the pan.
Drain on a wire rack and serve immediately with sour cream and applesauce.

name: Sweet Lokshen Kugel
description: Creamy baked noodle pudding with eggs, cream cheese, and cinnamon, a beloved Ashkenazi Shabbat side.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; grease a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Cook egg noodles according to package directions until just tender; drain and return to pot.
In a blender or food processor, blend eggs, sour cream, cream cheese, cottage cheese, sugar, melted butter, and salt until smooth.
Soak raisins in hot water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Pour the cream cheese mixture over the noodles and stir to combine; fold in drained raisins.
Pour mixture into prepared baking dish.
Sprinkle top generously with cinnamon and sugar mixture.
Bake for 60 minutes until center is set and noodle tips are golden brown; let rest 15 minutes before slicing.

name: Challah
description: Beautifully braided, golden egg bread with a glossy crust, the iconic Shabbat and holiday loaf.
ingredients: Sesame or poppy seeds for topping
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm water with 1 tsp honey; let stand 5 minutes until foamy.
Combine flour, salt, remaining honey, oil, and 2 eggs in the bowl of a stand mixer; add yeast mixture and knead with dough hook on medium for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place dough in an oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise at room temperature 2 hours until puffy.
Gently deflate dough and divide into 6 equal pieces; roll each into a 20-inch rope.
Braid into two 3-strand loaves or one 6-strand braid; place on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Cover with greased plastic wrap and let rise 60-90 minutes until very puffy.
Preheat oven to 375°F; brush loaves with egg white wash and sprinkle with seeds.
Bake 25-30 minutes until deep golden brown and internal temperature reads 190°F; cool on a rack.

name: Rugelach
description: Flaky cream cheese pastry rolled with jam, cinnamon, walnuts, and chocolate into tender crescent cookies.
ingredients: 1/3 cup walnuts toasted and finely chopped
1 egg beaten with 1 tsp water for egg wash
instructions: Pulse flour and salt in a food processor; add cream cheese in chunks and process until dispersed; add butter in chunks and pulse until dough clumps together.
Divide dough into 4 portions, wrap each in plastic, and refrigerate at least 2 hours or up to 3 days.
Preheat oven to 350°F; line baking sheets with parchment.
Stir together sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl; combine walnuts and chocolate chips in another.
Roll each dough quarter into a 12x8 inch rectangle on a floured surface; spread thinly with 2-3 tbsp jam; sprinkle with 2 tbsp cinnamon-sugar and 4 tbsp nut-chocolate mixture.
Roll dough from the 12-inch side into a tight log; freeze 10-15 minutes.
Slice logs into 10-12 pieces per log; place on baking sheets.
Brush tops with egg wash, sprinkle with remaining cinnamon-sugar, and bake 20-25 minutes until golden brown; cool on racks.

name: Hamantaschen
description: Triangular butter cookies filled with jam or poppy seed paste, baked for the Purim holiday.
ingredients: 1/2 cup fruit jam or prepared poppy seed filling
instructions: Cream butter and cream cheese until smooth; add sugar and beat 1 minute; mix in egg, vanilla, orange zest, and salt.
Add flour and mix until dough just comes together; it should be slightly sticky.
Form dough into a disc, wrap in plastic, and refrigerate at least 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350°F; line baking sheets with parchment.
Roll dough on a floured surface to 1/4-inch thick; cut into 2.5-inch circles.
Place 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of each circle; fold three sides up and crimp corners firmly into a triangle, leaving filling slightly visible.
Place on prepared baking sheets 2 inches apart.
Bake 18-20 minutes until the cookies are golden brown; cool on baking sheet for 2 minutes then transfer to a rack.

name: Chocolate Babka
description: Buttery, yeasted loaf swirled with rich chocolate filling and brushed with simple syrup for Shabbat.
ingredients: 1/4 cup sugar and 1/4 cup water for syrup
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, yeast, and zest; add eggs and water, mix with dough hook until it comes together; add salt then softened butter a spoonful at a time.
Knead on medium 10 minutes until smooth; refrigerate dough overnight in an oiled bowl covered with plastic.
Make filling: melt butter and chocolate together; stir in powdered sugar and cocoa to form a spreadable paste.
Butter and parchment two 9x4-inch loaf pans; take half the dough from fridge and roll to a 10x12-inch rectangle.
Spread half the chocolate filling over dough leaving a 1/2-inch border; roll tightly into a log; freeze 15 minutes for easier cutting.
Cut log in half lengthwise; twist the two halves together with cut sides facing up; place in prepared loaf pan.
Repeat with remaining dough; cover loaves and let rise at room temperature 1-1.5 hours.
Bake at 375°F for 30 minutes until golden; immediately brush with sugar syrup made by simmering sugar and water together; cool in pan 20 minutes then transfer to a rack.

name: Cholent
description: Hearty overnight Shabbat stew of beef, beans, barley, and potatoes slow-cooked for 12 or more hours.
ingredients: 2.5 lbs beef brisket or stew meat cut into chunks
1 cup dried mixed beans soaked overnight
2.5 lbs large red potatoes peeled and halved
instructions: Layer potatoes on the bottom of a large slow cooker; add onions on top.
Place beef chunks in a single layer over the onions; add marrow bones and whole garlic cloves.
Rinse beans and barley; sprinkle over the meat; tuck eggs in shells into the meat if using.
Whisk together broth, salt, pepper, paprika, turmeric, and cumin; pour over everything.
Add water until beans and meat are just covered.
Cover and cook on low heat for 16 hours (or overnight in oven at 200°F).
Check periodically, adding water if too dry.
Peel and slice eggs before serving; dig in and serve from the pot with challah.

name: Kasha Varnishkes
description: Toasted buckwheat groats tossed with caramelized onions and bow-tie pasta, a classic Ashkenazi comfort dish.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh parsley chopped for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F; mix kasha with beaten egg, 1/4 tsp salt, and a dash of pepper until well coated.
Spread kasha mixture in a small oven-safe nonstick skillet and toast in oven 15-20 minutes until dried and fragrant.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp schmaltz in a large skillet over medium; caramelize onions 15-20 minutes, stirring often, until golden.
Bring 3 cups water to a boil in a medium saucepan; add toasted kasha and 1/4 tsp salt; cover and simmer 15 minutes until water is absorbed and kasha is fluffy.
Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente; drain.
Combine cooked pasta, kasha, and caramelized onions with their oil in a large bowl.
Add remaining schmaltz or butter; toss well to combine; season generously with salt and pepper.
Serve hot garnished with fresh parsley.

name: Cheese Blintzes
description: Paper-thin crepes filled with sweet ricotta and cream cheese, pan-fried golden for the Shavuot holiday.
ingredients: 1 cup lowfat ricotta cheese drained overnight
Sour cream or fruit topping for serving
instructions: Blend together eggs, flour, 1/3 cup sugar, milk, water, and vanilla until completely smooth; rest batter 15 minutes.
Make filling by mixing ricotta, cream cheese, 1/4 cup sugar, egg yolk, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt with a fork until smooth.
Heat an 8-inch nonstick skillet over medium and spray with oil; pour in 1/3 cup batter and tilt to coat pan in a thin, even circle.
Cook until edges are dry and bottom is lightly golden, about 60-75 seconds; do not flip; slide blintz onto a plate.
Repeat with remaining batter, separating blintzes with parchment paper.
Place 3 tbsp filling on the lower part of each blintz; fold bottom edge up, fold in sides, then roll up into a neat package.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium; fry blintzes flap-side down in batches for 1.5-2 minutes per side until evenly browned.
Serve warm with sour cream or fruit topping.

name: Gefilte Fish
description: Poached ground fish patties seasoned with onion and matzo meal, the iconic Ashkenazi Passover appetizer.
ingredients: 3/4 lb salmon fillets boned and skinned
instructions: Bring fish stock with celery, lemon, salt, and pepper to a simmer in a large pot.
Sauté onion in oil over medium heat until soft, about 5 minutes; allow to cool.
Finely chop salmon and whitefish with a knife or pulse briefly in a food processor; transfer to a bowl.
Mix in cooled sautéed onion, eggs, matzo meal, parsley, salt, and pepper until well combined; mixture should hold together when formed.
With wet hands, form 2-3 tablespoons of fish mixture into smooth oval patties.
Gently lower fish balls into simmering stock in a single layer; do not boil.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes until cooked through; remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
Serve warm or cold on lettuce with prepared horseradish.

name: Tzimmes
description: Sweet glazed carrots, sweet potatoes, and prunes roasted with honey and cinnamon for Rosh Hashanah.
ingredients: 2 lbs carrots peeled and cut into 1/2-inch slices
2 medium sweet potatoes peeled and cut into chunks
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; lightly grease a 9x13 baking dish.
Place carrots, sweet potatoes, prunes, and raisins in a large bowl.
Drizzle with oil; add brown sugar, cinnamon, salt, and pepper; toss well to coat all pieces.
Pour in orange juice and toss again to combine.
Transfer to prepared baking dish; cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 1 hour, stirring once or twice, until vegetables are very tender.
Remove foil and continue baking 20-30 minutes until sauce has thickened into a glaze.
Serve warm as a side dish.

name: Potato Kugel
description: Crispy-edged baked shredded potato casserole with golden crust, a Passover and Shabbat staple.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F; add 1/4 cup oil to a 9x13 baking dish and place in oven to heat up.
Shred potatoes using a food processor or box grater; place in a large bowl of cold water for 5 minutes.
Shred onions and set aside.
Whisk together eggs, salt, pepper, and garlic powder in a large bowl.
Drain potatoes in a colander, pressing firmly to remove excess liquid; add to egg mixture.
Add shredded onion and potato starch; mix with hands until well combined.

Carefully pour hot oil from dish into potato mixture and stir; quickly transfer mixture to hot dish, spreading evenly with a spoon (it should sizzle); drizzle remaining oil on top and sprinkle with paprika.
Bake uncovered 60-70 minutes until top is deeply golden and crispy; cool 5 minutes before cutting.

name: Sufganiyot
description: Deep-fried yeast doughnuts filled with strawberry jam and dusted with powdered sugar for Hanukkah.
instructions: Whisk yeast, 1 tbsp sugar, and warm water in a small bowl; let stand 5-10 minutes until foamy.
In a stand mixer bowl, combine flour and salt; add yeast mixture, remaining sugar, eggs, canola oil, and vanilla; knead with dough hook on low for 10 minutes until sticky dough forms.
Add vodka and knead 2-3 minutes more; dough should be sticky but cohesive.
Transfer dough to an oiled bowl, cover with a damp towel, and let rise 2 hours until doubled.
Roll dough on a floured surface to 1/2-inch thick; cut into 3-inch circles; place on a floured baking sheet and let rise 45 minutes.
Heat oil in a large pot to 325°F using a thermometer; fry sufganiyot in batches of 4, flipping once, about 90 seconds per side until golden brown.
Drain on a wire rack; cool slightly.
Fill a squeeze bottle with strained jam; insert tip into center of each sufganiyot and squeeze in jam; dust generously with powdered sugar and serve immediately.

name: Honey Apple Cake
description: Moist and warmly spiced apple honey bundt cake, a traditional Rosh Hashanah dessert for a sweet New Year.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F; grease and flour a 10-inch bundt pan.
Beat eggs until frothy; whisk in honey, both sugars, oil, and vanilla.
In a separate bowl, sift together flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg, and salt.
Fold the flour mixture into the wet ingredients, stirring until combined; fold in shredded apples and their juice.
Pour batter into prepared bundt pan.
Bake 75-90 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean; check at 60 minutes if using a dark pan.
Cool cake in pan exactly 10 minutes; invert onto a plate and tap gently to release; cool completely.
Mix powdered sugar with 1-2 tsp water to make a thick glaze; drizzle over cake in a zigzag pattern and allow to set before slicing.

name: Cheese Burekas
description: Flaky puff pastry triangles stuffed with seasoned feta and ricotta cheese, a beloved Israeli-Sephardic snack.
ingredients: 1 egg yolk mixed with 2 tsp water for egg wash
Sesame or poppy seeds for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a mixing bowl, combine feta, kashkaval or mozzarella, ricotta, egg, salt, and pepper; mix well with a fork until blended.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out each puff pastry sheet to a 12x12-inch square; cut each into 9 equal squares (4x4 inches each).
Place 1 scant tablespoon of cheese filling in the center of each square.
Wet edges with a finger dipped in water; fold dough over diagonally to form triangles; press edges firmly to seal, then crimp with a fork.
Arrange on prepared baking sheets spaced evenly apart.
Brush tops with egg wash and sprinkle with sesame or poppy seeds.
Bake 30 minutes, switching pans halfway through, until puffed and golden brown; serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Moroccan Harira Soup
description: Rich Moroccan tomato and lentil soup with chickpeas, warming spices, and fresh herbs.
ingredients: 1/4 cup fresh parsley and cilantro chopped
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; add carrots, celery, and onion; sauté 5-6 minutes until softened.
Add garlic and sauté 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in harissa, turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, and coriander; cook 1 minute; add tomato paste and cook 2 more minutes.
Add green lentils, red lentils, diced tomatoes, and vegetable stock; increase heat to high and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer 60-90 minutes until lentils are very tender and soup begins to thicken; stir occasionally.
Add chickpeas and vermicelli noodles; simmer 15 minutes more until noodles are cooked.
Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle into bowls and finish with generous handfuls of fresh parsley and cilantro.

name: Moroccan Chicken Couscous
description: Aromatic braised chicken and seven vegetables over steamed couscous, a Moroccan-Jewish Shabbat centerpiece.
ingredients: 1 small butternut squash peeled and cubed
1/4 cup fresh cilantro or parsley for garnish
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat; brown chicken pieces on all sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onions over medium heat until caramelized, about 10 minutes; add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Pour in 1.5 cups chicken broth; stir in salt, turmeric, cumin, and cayenne; bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to pot skin-side up; cover and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes.
Add squash, zucchini, and carrots around the chicken; bring back to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in chickpeas; simmer covered 5-10 more minutes until largest vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, bring 2 cups broth to a boil; stir in couscous, cover, remove from heat, and steam 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
Mound couscous on a large platter; top with chicken and vegetables; ladle broth on top and garnish with fresh cilantro.

name: Jachnun
description: Flaky Yemenite overnight pastry rolls baked low and slow, served with grated tomato and schug on Shabbat morning.
ingredients: 10 large eggs in shells for slow cooking
1/2 cup schug green chili sauce for serving
instructions: Combine flour, brown sugar, and salt in a stand mixer with dough hook; gradually add water on low speed; mix 10-15 minutes until soft and slightly sticky dough forms.
Oil the dough, cover, and rest at room temperature 30 minutes; divide into 10 equal balls; place in an oiled dish, cover, and refrigerate at least 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°F; line the bottom of a heavy ovenproof pot with stale bread and parchment paper.
Working with one dough ball at a time, use buttered fingertips to slowly stretch each ball into a very thin, nearly translucent 17x20-inch sheet.
Dab with 2 tsp softened butter; fold the sheet into thirds horizontally then roll into a tight log; place in the pot.
Repeat with remaining dough balls, layering them in the pot; drizzle 2-3 tbsp hot water over the top; cover tightly.
Place eggs in their shells into a small lidded pot; cover with salted water; place both pots in oven for 10-12 hours overnight.
Serve jachnun hot from the oven with slow-cooked brown eggs, grated fresh tomato, and schug.

name: Ashkenazi Charoset
description: Apple and walnut Passover condiment sweetened with wine and cinnamon, symbolizing the mortar of Egypt.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs Gala or Fuji apples (about 4 medium)
instructions: Peel and core the apples; chop finely by hand or pulse in a food processor, being careful not to over-process into applesauce.
Place chopped apples in a large bowl.
Add sweet kosher wine, honey, cinnamon, ginger, allspice, and a pinch of salt; stir to combine.
Fold in finely chopped walnuts.
Taste and adjust sweetness with more wine or honey if needed; the mixture should be moistened but not soupy.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight for the best flavor.
Stir again before serving; the wine will be partially absorbed.
Serve chilled at the Passover seder alongside matzah and the rest of the seder plate.

name: Cinnamon Noodle Kugel
description: Light and fluffy pareve noodle kugel with cinnamon, nutmeg, and raisins baked until golden and set.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; grease a 9x13 baking dish.
Cook egg noodles according to package directions; drain well.
In a large bowl, toss noodles with melted margarine or butter until coated.
In a separate bowl, whisk together sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg; add to noodle mixture and stir.
Separate eggs; beat whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form; lightly beat yolks in another bowl.
Add beaten yolks and raisins to the noodle mixture; stir to combine.
Gently fold stiff egg whites into the noodle mixture until just incorporated.
Pour into greased baking dish and bake 40-45 minutes until top is just beginning to turn golden and crispy.

name: New York Cheesecake
description: Towering, ultra-creamy cream cheese cheesecake on a graham cracker crust, the quintessential Shavuot dessert.
ingredients: 5 packages cream cheese 8 oz each softened
instructions: Make crust: combine ground graham crackers, melted butter, and 1/2 cup sugar; press firmly onto bottom and partway up the sides of a buttered 9.5-inch springform pan; chill in freezer while preparing filling.
Preheat oven to 550°F; beat cream cheese, 1 3/4 cups sugar, flour, and zests with a mixer until smooth.
Add vanilla then eggs and egg yolks one at a time, beating on low after each addition; scrape bowl frequently.
Place pan with crust in a shallow baking pan (to catch drips); pour filling into crust (pan will be very full).
Bake at 550°F for 12 minutes until puffed; reduce oven to 200°F and continue baking 60-70 minutes until mostly firm with a slight wobble in the center.
Run a knife around the top edge to loosen; cool completely on a rack.
Refrigerate loosely covered for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Carefully remove sides of springform; slice with a warm, clean knife and serve at room temperature.

name: Mandelbrot
description: Twice-baked almond and chocolate chip Jewish biscotti, crisp and perfect for dunking in tea or coffee.
ingredients: 2 tsp cinnamon mixed with 2 tbsp sugar for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F; line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Beat eggs and sugar with an electric mixer for 2 minutes; beat in oil, vanilla, and almond extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt; stir into egg mixture until combined.
Fold in almonds and chocolate chips; dough will be soft and slightly sticky.
Divide dough in half; shape each half into a log about 12 inches long and 2.5 inches wide on the prepared baking sheet; logs will spread during baking.
Sprinkle tops with cinnamon-sugar mixture.
Bake 30-35 minutes until golden and set; cool 15 minutes; slice each log diagonally into 1/2-inch slices.
Return slices to baking sheet cut-side up and bake 10-12 minutes more until dry and crisp; cool completely on a rack.

name: Maamoul Date Cookies
description: Tender semolina shortbread cookies filled with spiced date paste, a beloved Sephardic and Mizrahi confection.
instructions: Combine flour, semolina, powdered sugar, and baking powder in a large bowl; add softened butter, oil, rose water, and water; mix by hand until a soft dough forms (do not overmix); refrigerate 20 minutes.
Make filling: combine dates, chopped walnuts, and cinnamon; knead together, adding 1 tbsp water if needed, until a uniform paste forms.
Preheat oven to 350°F; line baking sheets with parchment.
Divide dough into three sections; roll out each portion to 1/4-inch thick on parchment paper.
Press a ball of dough into a floured maamoul mold (or shape by hand into a round); press a teaspoon of date filling into the center; close dough over the filling and smooth.
Tap mold to release shaped cookie or shape into a smooth round ball and press lightly.
Arrange on baking sheets and bake 25-30 minutes until just barely beginning to turn golden on the bottom; do not overbake.
Cool completely; dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

name: T'beet Iraqi Shabbat Rice
description: Iraqi-Jewish slow-cooked whole chicken stuffed with fragrant spiced rice, simmered overnight for Shabbat.
ingredients: 1/4 cup slivered almonds toasted for garnish
instructions: Heat oil in a large heavy pot over medium; sauté onions until golden brown and caramelized, about 15 minutes; add garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add turmeric, allspice, cinnamon, cumin, black pepper, and salt; stir 1 minute.
Mix half of the spiced onion with 1 cup uncooked rice; stuff this mixture loosely into the chicken cavity; tie legs together with kitchen twine.
Add diced tomatoes and chicken broth to the remaining spiced onions in the pot; stir to combine.
Place stuffed chicken breast-side down in the pot; add remaining 1 cup of rice around the chicken.
Add water if needed so rice is submerged; bring to a boil, then reduce to lowest heat; cover tightly.
Cook on lowest heat overnight or bake at 200°F for 10-12 hours until chicken is falling-apart tender and rice has cooked and absorbed the broth.
Serve garnished with toasted almonds and fresh parsley.

name: Sabich
description: Israeli pita sandwich with fried eggplant, hard-boiled eggs, hummus, and Israeli salad, an Iraqi-Jewish street food.
ingredients: 2 medium Italian eggplants sliced 1/2 inch thick
1/4 cup tahini thinned with lemon juice
Amba mango pickle sauce for serving
instructions: Salt eggplant slices generously and let drain in a colander for 20 minutes; pat dry with paper towels.
Heat 1/2 inch vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat; fry eggplant slices in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until deeply golden and tender; drain on a rack.
Make Israeli salad: combine diced tomatoes, cucumbers, and parsley; dress with olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper; toss well.
Warm pitas in a dry skillet or oven; open each pita to form a pocket.
Spread a generous layer of hummus inside each pita.
Layer in 3-4 slices of fried eggplant and 2-3 slices of hard-boiled egg.
Add a scoop of Israeli salad.
Drizzle with thin tahini and amba sauce; add schug for heat; serve immediately.

name: Schug Green Chili Sauce
description: Vibrant Yemenite green chili and herb sauce, an essential condiment for sabich, falafel, and jachnun.
ingredients: 6 serrano or jalapeño peppers stems removed
1 cup fresh cilantro leaves and stems
2 tbsp water or more to thin
instructions: Roughly chop the hot peppers, removing seeds if you prefer less heat.
Add peppers and garlic to a food processor and pulse until roughly chopped.
Add cilantro, parsley, cumin, cardamom, and salt to the processor.
Pulse, scraping down the sides, until a slightly chunky paste forms; do not over-process to a smooth paste.
Add olive oil and water; pulse a few more times to incorporate.
Taste and adjust salt, heat, and lemon juice to your preference.
Transfer to a jar; drizzle a thin layer of olive oil on top to preserve color.
Refrigerate for up to 2 weeks; serve as a condiment alongside sabich, falafel, jachnun, or eggs.

name: Matbucha
description: Slowly cooked Moroccan-Israeli roasted tomato and pepper salad, a classic mezze for dipping with challah.
ingredients: 1-2 hot chili peppers or to taste
instructions: Roast red bell peppers directly over a gas flame or under the broiler, turning, until completely charred on all sides; place in a covered bowl for 15 minutes to steam.
Peel, seed, and roughly chop the charred peppers.
Score the base of the tomatoes with an X; blanch in boiling water 30 seconds; peel, seed, and chop coarsely.
Heat olive oil in a wide heavy pot over medium heat; add garlic and sauté 1-2 minutes until fragrant but not browned.
Add chopped tomatoes, chopped peppers, and whole hot chili peppers; stir to combine.
Stir in tomato paste, paprika, sugar, salt, and pepper.
Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, for 60 minutes until mixture is very thick and most liquid has evaporated.
Cool to room temperature; serve as a mezze with challah, pita, or crackers; refrigerates well for up to 1 week.

name: Malabi
description: Silky Middle Eastern rosewater milk pudding topped with pomegranate syrup and toasted coconut.
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 1/2 cup of the milk until smooth (the slurry).
Combine remaining milk, heavy cream, and 1/2 cup sugar in a medium saucepan over medium heat; stir until sugar dissolves and milk is hot but not boiling.
Whisk the cornstarch slurry into the hot milk mixture; cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 5-8 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in rose water.
Pour pudding into 6 individual dessert cups or ramekins; press plastic wrap directly on the surface to prevent a skin.
Refrigerate at least 3 hours or overnight until fully set and firm.
Make the syrup: simmer pomegranate juice with 2 tbsp sugar over medium heat for 5-8 minutes until slightly thickened and syrupy; cool.
To serve, spoon pomegranate syrup over each pudding and garnish with toasted coconut and crushed pistachios.

name: Butter Chicken
description: Tender broiled chicken simmered in a rich spiced tomato cream sauce with kasoori methi.
instructions: Cut chicken into bite-size pieces and marinate with yogurt, lemon juice, 2 tsp ginger garlic paste, tandoori masala, chili powder, and salt for 2 hours or overnight.
Broil chicken on high for 5-7 minutes per side until slightly charred; set aside.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat; add cardamoms, bay leaf, and cinnamon stick; fry 1 minute.
Add remaining 2 tsp ginger garlic paste; fry 30 seconds then stir in tomato puree.
Add salt, chili powder, and garam masala; simmer 10 minutes until oil separates.
Stir in sugar and crushed kasoori methi; cook 2 minutes then add broiled chicken.
Pour in heavy cream, stir well, and bring just to a boil; taste and adjust seasoning before serving.

name: Paneer Tikka Masala
description: Grilled spiced paneer cubes folded into a velvety onion-tomato-cashew gravy.
instructions: Mix yogurt, chili powder, ginger garlic paste, garam masala, kasuri methi, oil, lemon juice, and salt; coat paneer cubes and marinate 1 hour.
Grill paneer on a hot oiled griddle or in oven at 430 F for 10 minutes until lightly charred; set aside.
Saute onions in oil until golden; add tomatoes, cashews, sugar, and salt; cook until tomatoes are soft.
Cool and blend onion-tomato mixture to a smooth puree.
Heat 2 tbsp oil; add cumin seeds and ginger garlic paste; saute 1 minute then pour in the puree.
Stir in chili powder, garam masala, and water to get a gravy consistency; simmer covered 10 minutes until oil floats on top.
Add grilled paneer; stir in heavy cream and crushed kasuri methi; simmer 3 minutes and serve garnished with coriander.

name: Chana Masala
description: Bold Punjabi chickpea curry with tangy amchur and a deeply spiced onion-tomato base.
instructions: Pressure cook soaked chickpeas with 1.5 cups water for 5-6 whistles until soft; drain and reserve cooking liquid.
Heat oil in a pot; add cumin seeds then onion and green chili; saute 7-8 minutes until golden.
Add ginger garlic paste and saute 2 minutes; stir in tomatoes and cook until mushy for 6-7 minutes.
Lower heat and add chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, cumin powder, and salt; saute 3-4 minutes.
Add drained chickpeas and 1 cup reserved cooking liquid; mix well, cover, and simmer 15 minutes.
Uncover and mash a few chickpeas with the spoon to thicken the gravy; cook 5 more minutes.
Stir in amchur powder and crushed kasuri methi; garnish with coriander leaves and serve with naan or rice.

name: Rajma Masala
description: Slow-simmered Punjabi kidney bean curry in an aromatic spiced onion-tomato gravy.
ingredients: 1 cup dried kidney beans soaked overnight
instructions: Pressure cook soaked kidney beans with 3 cups water for 18-20 minutes until very tender; keep aside.
Heat ghee in a large pot; add cumin seeds then onions; saute until golden stirring often.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook 1 minute; add tomatoes and cook on medium heat until oil separates about 8 minutes.
Stir in turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt; saute the masala until aromatic.
Add cooked kidney beans with 2 cups liquid; stir well.
Simmer uncovered on low-medium heat 12-15 minutes until gravy thickens; mash a few beans to thicken further.
Stir in garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, and cream; simmer 2 more minutes and garnish with coriander.

name: Rogan Josh
description: Slow-braised Kashmiri lamb in a fragrant yogurt-spice sauce with fennel and dried ginger.
ingredients: 800g bone-in lamb shoulder cut in pieces
instructions: Heat ghee in a heavy pot; add cinnamon, cardamoms, and cloves; sizzle 1 minute.
Add lamb and sear on high heat 2 minutes; reduce and fry 4-5 minutes more until lightly browned.
Whisk together yogurt, chili powder, fennel powder, dried ginger powder, and salt in a bowl.
Take pot off stove; stir in yogurt mixture; return to medium heat and cook covered 3-4 minutes.
Pour 1 cup hot water; cook covered on low heat about 2 hours until lamb is fork-tender stirring every 10-15 minutes and adding more water as needed.
Uncover and reduce sauce slightly until it is of medium-thick consistency.
Stir in garam masala, garnish with coriander, and serve with basmati rice or naan.

name: Lamb Vindaloo
description: Fiery Goan-style lamb curry marinated in a vinegar-based spice paste with dark whole chilies.
instructions: Soak chilies in vinegar and 1/4 cup hot water 20 minutes; grind to a smooth paste with spices, jaggery, ginger, and garlic.
Marinate lamb in turmeric, vindaloo paste, and salt; cover and refrigerate overnight or at least 6 hours.
Heat oil in a dutch oven; fry onions over medium heat until golden about 8 minutes.
Add marinated lamb; saute on medium-high 5 minutes until the paste begins to smell aromatic and leave sides.
Cover and cook 3 minutes on medium-low; add curry leaves and saute 2 minutes.
Pour 1 cup boiling water and mix well; cook covered on low for 90 minutes stirring every 15 minutes and adding hot water as needed.
When lamb is fork-tender uncover and cook off excess moisture; taste and adjust with salt and jaggery.

name: Lucknowi Awadhi Biryani
description: Fragrant dum-cooked Awadhi biryani with saffron and cream layered over gently spiced chicken.
ingredients: 1 pinch saffron dissolved in 2 tbsp warm milk
instructions: Marinate chicken with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, chili powder, garam masala, turmeric, and salt for 2 hours.
Make fried onions: thinly slice 2 onions and fry in ghee until deep golden; set aside.
Parboil drained rice with salted boiling water and shahi jeera until 90 percent done; drain and set aside.
Saute marinated chicken in remaining ghee with green chilies 3-4 minutes; add half the fried onions and cook on medium-low until chicken is fully cooked with a thick nearly-dry gravy.
In a wide heavy pot layer chicken at base; top with parboiled rice; scatter mint leaves and remaining fried onions.
Mix cream with saffron-milk and kewra water; drizzle over rice layer.
Seal pot tightly with foil then lid; cook on medium heat 10 minutes then on low 5-10 minutes; rest 10 minutes before serving.

name: Tandoori Chicken
description: Yogurt-and-spice marinated chicken grilled to smoky perfection in oven or on grill.
instructions: Score chicken pieces with deep cuts; rub with lemon juice, chili powder, and salt; rest 20 minutes.
Mix yogurt, ginger garlic paste, garam masala, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, kasuri methi, and oil; coat chicken thoroughly.
Marinate covered in refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 450 F; place chicken on a wire rack over a foil-lined baking sheet.
Roast 20-22 minutes turning halfway until charred in spots and cooked through.
Optionally finish under broiler for 2 minutes for extra char.
Sprinkle chaat masala over chicken and serve with mint chutney and sliced onions.

name: Aloo Gobi
description: Homestyle dry-spiced cauliflower and potato curry with cumin, turmeric, and fresh ginger.
ingredients: 1 small head cauliflower cut in florets
instructions: Heat oil in a wide pan; add cumin seeds and let them sizzle; add onion and saute until translucent.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and cook 2 minutes until slightly soft; stir in turmeric, amchur, chili powder, and coriander powder.
Cover the pan and cook masala on medium heat 2-3 minutes.
Add potato cubes and cauliflower florets and garam masala; mix to coat with masala.
Cover and cook on low-medium heat 18-20 minutes stirring occasionally; add 1-2 tbsp water if masala sticks.
When vegetables are fork-tender add salt, garnish with coriander leaves, and serve hot with roti.

name: Baingan Bharta
description: Smoky fire-roasted eggplant mashed with spiced onion-tomato for a classic Punjabi side.
instructions: Rub eggplants with oil and place directly on a stovetop flame; char on all sides turning with tongs for 15-20 minutes until completely soft inside; cool and peel.
Roughly mash the roasted eggplant pulp and set aside.
Heat oil in a saucepan; add cumin seeds; when they crackle add onions and green chilies; saute until golden.
Add ginger and saute 1 minute; add tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until soft and pulpy.
Stir in turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt; cook 2 minutes.
Add mashed eggplant; mix thoroughly and cook 5 minutes more.
Add garam masala, garnish with coriander leaves, and serve with roti or naan.

name: Aloo Paratha
description: Flaky whole-wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced mashed potato and cooked in butter.
ingredients: 3 tbsp butter or ghee for cooking
instructions: Mix flour, 1/2 tsp salt, and water; knead into a smooth soft dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Combine mashed potatoes, green chili, chili powder, garam masala, amchur, cumin, coriander leaves, and salt; divide into 8 equal portions.
Divide dough into 8 balls; roll each into a 4-inch circle; place a potato filling ball in the center; gather edges and seal.
Gently roll the stuffed dough ball into a 7-8 inch round paratha; press evenly to avoid tearing.
Heat a griddle on medium-high; place paratha and cook 1-2 minutes until bubbles appear and underside is lightly golden.
Flip; apply butter or ghee; cook 1 minute; flip again; apply butter on the other side; press gently and cook until both sides are golden brown and crisp.
Serve hot with plain yogurt, pickle, or butter.

name: Methi Chicken
description: Tender chicken cooked with fresh fenugreek leaves in a fragrant North Indian onion-tomato gravy.
instructions: Wash fenugreek leaves well; sprinkle with a pinch of salt, rest 5 minutes, then squeeze out excess moisture.
Heat oil in a heavy pan; add bay leaf then onions; saute on medium heat until deep golden about 10 minutes.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add tomato puree and cook on medium heat until oil separates about 6-8 minutes.
Stir in chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt; saute 2 minutes.
Add chicken pieces and stir to coat; cook on high heat 3 minutes then reduce to medium; stir in whisked yogurt and fenugreek leaves.
Cook covered on low heat 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through; stir in garam masala, garnish with coriander, and serve with roti.

name: Masala Dosa
description: Crispy South Indian rice-and-lentil crepe filled with spiced potato masala served with sambar.
instructions: Soak rice and fenugreek separately; soak urad dal separately for 5-6 hours; blend each smooth; combine with salt and ferment overnight.
For potato masala: heat 1 tbsp oil; crackle mustard and cumin; add curry leaves, green chilies, ginger, onion, and turmeric; saute until onions soften.
Add mashed potatoes and a few tbsp water; mix and cook 2 minutes; adjust salt; set aside.
Thin fermented batter with water to a spreading consistency; heat a cast iron tawa until very hot; pour a ladle of batter and spread in a spiral to a thin crepe.
Drizzle oil around edges; cook on medium-high until underside is crisp and golden.
Place a portion of potato masala in the center; fold dosa over filling.
Serve immediately with coconut chutney and sambar.

name: Idli with Tiffin Sambar
description: Soft steamed rice-lentil cakes paired with tangy spiced vegetable sambar.
ingredients: 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (carrot, potato, onion, tomato)
instructions: Soak rice and fenugreek seeds together and urad dal separately for 5-6 hours; grind separately to smooth batters; combine with salt and ferment overnight.
Grease idli molds; pour batter to 3/4 full; steam 10-12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean; rest 2 minutes before unmolding.
Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric and 2 cups water for 2 whistles; mash and set aside.
In a pot add vegetables, tamarind pulp, sambar powder, salt, and 1.5 cups water; cook until vegetables are tender.
Stir in mashed dal; bring to a simmer.
For tempering: heat oil in a small pan; crackle mustard and cumin; add dried chilies, curry leaves, and asafoetida; pour over sambar.
Serve hot idlis with sambar and coconut chutney.

name: Uttapam
description: Thick South Indian rice pancakes topped with onions, tomatoes, and green chilies.
instructions: Prepare fermented idli-dosa batter by soaking rice and urad dal separately 5-6 hours; blend; ferment overnight or use ready batter.
Mix chopped onions, tomatoes, green chilies, and coriander leaves in a bowl.
Heat a non-stick tawa on medium heat; pour a large ladle of batter and gently spread to a thick pancake about 6 inches wide.
Immediately scatter a generous portion of the vegetable topping over the wet batter; press lightly with spatula so they adhere.
Drizzle oil around edges; cook on medium heat until underside is golden and set about 3-4 minutes.
Flip carefully and cook the topping side until onions are lightly caramelized 2-3 minutes more.
Serve hot uttapam with sambar and coconut chutney.

name: Chettinad Pepper Chicken
description: Intensely spiced South Indian dry chicken curry ground with fresh peppercorns and aromatic masala.
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy kadai; crackle mustard and cumin seeds; add cardamoms, cloves, and cinnamon; saute 30 seconds.
Add onions and curry leaves; cook on medium heat until onions are deep golden stirring often.
Add ginger garlic paste; fry 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add tomatoes; cook until soft and oil begins to separate.
Stir in chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric, and salt; saute 2 minutes.
Add chicken pieces; mix well; cook on high heat 3 minutes then reduce to medium-low; cover and cook 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through stirring occasionally.
Uncover, increase heat, stir in freshly ground pepper; cook 3-5 minutes until masala coats chicken; garnish with coriander leaves.

name: Kerala Coconut Fish Curry
description: Flaky fish simmered in a tangy tamarind-coconut milk curry with warming spices.
instructions: Heat coconut oil in a clay pot or kadai; crackle mustard and fenugreek seeds.
Add onions, curry leaves, and green chilies; saute until onions are lightly golden.
Add ginger garlic paste; cook 1 minute; reduce heat and stir in chili powder, coriander powder, and turmeric; saute 3-4 minutes.
Stir in tamarind pulp and water; bring to a boil.
Add fish pieces; cook partially covered on medium heat 8-10 minutes gently shaking the pan rather than stirring to avoid breaking fish.
Pour in coconut milk; simmer on low heat 3-4 minutes until fish is cooked through and curry is creamy.
Drizzle extra coconut oil on top and garnish with curry leaves; serve with steamed rice.

name: Macher Jhol
description: Light Bengali fish curry with potatoes in mustard oil with nigella seeds and fresh spices.
ingredients: 600g fresh water fish (rohu or catla) cleaned and cut
instructions: Rub fish with turmeric and salt; rest 10 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a heavy wok until slightly smoky; shallow fry fish 2 minutes per side until lightly crisp; remove to a plate.
In remaining oil fry potatoes until lightly golden; remove.
Crackle bay leaf and nigella seeds in the oil; add green chilies.
Add onion paste; brown on medium heat 3 minutes; add ginger and garlic pastes with spice powders and a splash of water; fry 2-3 minutes until oil separates.
Add tomato, sugar, and salt; cook 2 minutes; pour in hot water; bring to a boil; add fried potatoes and simmer 5 minutes.
Gently add fried fish; simmer 6-8 minutes until cooked through; squeeze lime juice over and rest 15 minutes before serving with rice.

name: Kosha Mangsho
description: Slow-cooked Bengali mutton curry with deeply browned onions and warming whole spices.
ingredients: 700g bone-in goat mutton cut in pieces
instructions: Marinate mutton with yogurt, 1 tbsp mustard oil, ginger garlic paste, and salt; refrigerate 3-4 hours.
Heat 4 tbsp mustard oil in a large heavy pan; add bay leaves, lightly crushed cardamoms, cinnamon, cloves, dried chilies, and sugar; fry 5 seconds.
Add onions; cook on medium heat 15-20 minutes stirring often until very deep golden-brown.
Add ginger and garlic pastes; cook 2 minutes; stir in chili powder, turmeric, and coriander powder.
Add marinated mutton with its marinade; sear on high heat 5-6 minutes until browned.
Reduce heat to low; cover and cook 70-80 minutes stirring every 5-7 minutes and adding splashes of water to prevent sticking until mutton is very tender.
Stir in whisked yogurt and garam masala; cook uncovered 5 minutes; adjust salt and serve with rice or luchi.

name: Pav Bhaji
description: Buttery Mumbai street food: a thick spiced vegetable mash served with toasted bread rolls.
ingredients: 1 medium red bell pepper finely chopped
instructions: Pressure cook potatoes, peas, and cauliflower with 1.5 cups water for 1-2 whistles until soft; mash well.
Heat butter and oil in a large pan; crackle cumin; add onions and green chili; saute until translucent.
Add ginger garlic paste and fry 30 seconds; add bell pepper and cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and salt; cook until mushy 5-6 minutes stirring often.
Stir in pav bhaji masala, chili powder, and turmeric; saute 2 minutes.
Add mashed vegetables and 1/2 cup water; mash together and simmer on low 10 minutes; stir in kasuri methi and lemon juice; adjust salt.
Toast pav buns on a buttered griddle sprinkled with pav bhaji masala until golden; serve alongside bhaji garnished with coriander, butter, and chopped onions.

name: Dhokla
description: Soft and spongy steamed Gujarati gram-flour snack with a sweet-spicy mustard tempering.
ingredients: coriander leaves and coconut for garnish
instructions: Sift besan and semolina together in a large bowl; set aside.
Whisk together 1 cup water, 2 tbsp sugar, salt, ginger-green chili paste, turmeric, 1.5 tbsp oil, and citric acid until sugar dissolves; pour over besan and stir to a thick but flowing batter.
Grease a 9-inch steamer pan with oil; heat steamer with boiling water.
Just before steaming add Eno to batter; stir briskly until it foams; immediately pour into greased pan.
Steam on medium heat 15-17 minutes; test with a toothpick; cool 10 minutes.
For tempering: heat oil in a small pan; crackle mustard seeds; add curry leaves and green chili; add 1/3 cup water with 1 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt; remove from heat.
Cut dhokla into squares; pour tempering evenly over pieces; garnish with coriander and fresh coconut; serve with green chutney.

name: Goan Prawn Curry
description: Succulent prawns in a bright coconut-tamarind curry with Kashmiri chilies and ground spices.
instructions: Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and black pepper in a dry pan until aromatic.
Blend roasted spices with coconut, Kashmiri chilies, garlic, and tamarind pulp with enough water into a smooth paste; set aside.
Heat coconut oil in a pan; saute onion until lightly golden; add tomato and cook 5-7 minutes until broken down.
Add turmeric and salt; stir in ground coconut masala paste; saute 3-4 minutes until raw smell goes.
Pour in coconut milk; bring to a boil; reduce heat and simmer 10-15 minutes until color deepens slightly.
Add prawns and green chilies; cook 5-7 minutes just until prawns curl and turn pink; do not overcook.
Scatter curry leaves on top; rest 5 minutes and serve over steamed rice.

name: Lemon Rice
description: Bright South Indian rice tempered with mustard seeds, curry leaves, peanuts, and fresh lemon juice.
ingredients: 2 cups cooked basmati or sona masoori rice cooled
instructions: Spread cold cooked rice on a tray; sprinkle turmeric and toss gently so grains are coated; set aside.
Heat oil in a wide pan; crackle mustard seeds; add cumin, urad dal, and chana dal; fry until dals turn golden.
Add asafoetida, dried red chilies, green chilies, and curry leaves; fry 30 seconds until leaves turn crisp.
Add roasted peanuts and toss 30 seconds.
Add turmeric-coated rice; gently mix so tempering is evenly distributed; heat through on low-medium heat 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat; pour lemon juice evenly over rice; toss gently; taste and adjust salt and lemon.
Garnish with coriander leaves and serve warm with yogurt or pickle.

name: Samosas
description: Crispy fried pastry triangles filled with spiced potato and peas — India's most beloved street snack.
instructions: Rub ghee into flour with carom seeds and salt until mixture resembles coarse sand; add water gradually to form a firm smooth dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Heat 2 tsp oil in a pan; crackle cumin; add green chilies and ginger paste; fry 1 minute; add peas.
Add chili powder, coriander powder, chaat masala, and garam masala; mix; stir in mashed potatoes and lemon juice; taste and adjust salt; cool completely.
Divide dough into 12 balls; roll each into a 6-inch oval; cut in half; form each half into a cone by sealing the straight edge.
Fill each cone with potato stuffing; seal the open edge with water; press firmly.
Heat oil for deep frying to medium-low; fry samosas in batches 10-12 minutes turning occasionally until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mint chutney and tamarind chutney.

name: Papdi Chaat
description: Crunchy wheat crackers layered with chickpeas, yogurt, chutneys, and savory-sweet spice mix.
instructions: Arrange papdi crackers in a single layer on a serving plate.
Scatter boiled chickpeas and cubed potatoes evenly over the papdis.
Whisk yogurt with a pinch of salt; drizzle generously over the chickpeas and potatoes.
Drizzle green chutney and tamarind chutney evenly over the yogurt layer.
Sprinkle chaat masala, roasted cumin powder, and red chili powder over the entire plate.
Top with a generous handful of sev.
Garnish with coriander leaves and a final drizzle of tamarind chutney; serve immediately so papdis stay crisp.

name: Kheer
description: Slow-cooked Indian rice pudding with saffron, cardamom, and a garnish of toasted nuts.
ingredients: 1/4 cup basmati rice rinsed and soaked 15 minutes
instructions: Pour milk into a heavy-bottom pot; bring to a boil on medium heat stirring often to prevent scorching.
Drain soaked rice; add to hot milk; stir well.
Simmer on low-medium heat 25-30 minutes stirring every 3 minutes until rice is completely soft and slightly mushy.
Add sugar; stir to dissolve; continue simmering 10 minutes until kheer thickens but still flows.
Steep saffron in warm milk; stir into kheer along with cardamom powder and nuts.
Cook 2-3 more minutes; remove from heat as kheer will thicken further on cooling.
Add rose water if using; serve warm or chilled garnished with pistachios and saffron strands.

name: Gulab Jamun
description: Soft milk-powder dumplings deep-fried and soaked in a fragrant saffron-cardamom sugar syrup.
instructions: Make syrup: combine sugar, water, and cardamom in a saucepan; heat until sugar dissolves; simmer 5 minutes; add rose water and saffron; keep warm.
Sift milk powder, flour, and baking soda; rub in melted ghee until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add milk a tablespoon at a time; knead gently into a soft smooth dough without cracks; do not over-knead; rest 5 minutes.
Divide dough into 20-22 equal portions; roll each into a smooth crack-free ball.
Heat oil to medium heat and fry gulab jamun in batches on medium-low heat 4-5 minutes gently swirling until deep golden brown.
Drain briefly and immediately transfer to warm sugar syrup; coat on all sides; cover and soak 30 minutes until they have absorbed the syrup and plumped up.
Serve warm or at room temperature garnished with crushed pistachios.

name: Mango Lassi
description: Creamy blended drink of ripe mango pulp, yogurt, and a hint of cardamom.
ingredients: 1 cup ripe mango pulp (fresh or canned Alphonso)
instructions: If using fresh mango peel, cube, and blend to a smooth pulp.
Add mango pulp, yogurt, milk, sugar, and cardamom to a blender.
Blend on high for 60 seconds until completely smooth and frothy.
Taste and adjust sweetness; if too thick add a splash more milk.
Add ice cubes and blend briefly or serve over ice.
Pour into tall glasses.
Garnish with a pinch of saffron, a slice of mango, or a dusting of cardamom and serve immediately.

name: Palak Paneer Dhaba Style
description: Rustic roadside-style spinach and paneer curry with a charred onion base and robust spices.
ingredients: 1 medium onion roughly chopped and charred
instructions: Blanch spinach in boiling salted water 2 minutes; drain and blend with green chilies to a coarse-smooth puree; set aside.
Char onion quarters directly on flame or under broiler until edges are blackened; cool and roughly chop.
Heat ghee in a heavy kadai; crackle cumin seeds; add charred onion and ginger garlic paste; fry 2-3 minutes.
Add tomatoes; cook on medium heat until very soft and oil separates; stir in turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder.
Pour in spinach puree; mix; simmer 5 minutes; season with salt.
Add paneer cubes; fold in gently; simmer 3-4 minutes.
Stir in cream and garam masala; serve hot with roti or paratha.

name: Masala Chai
description: Robust spiced Indian tea simmered with ginger, cardamom, and cinnamon and finished with milk.
instructions: Combine water, grated ginger, crushed cardamom, cinnamon stick, and cloves in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat; reduce and simmer 3-4 minutes to extract spice flavors.
Add black tea leaves; simmer 1-2 minutes.
Pour in milk; stir and bring to a full rolling boil watching carefully to avoid overflow.
Reduce heat and gently simmer 2-3 minutes until tea is a deep golden-brown color.
Add sugar; stir to dissolve; taste and adjust.
Strain through a fine-mesh strainer into cups and serve hot.

name: Saltimbocca alla Romana
description: Tender veal cutlets topped with prosciutto and sage, pan-seared in a buttery white-wine sauce.
instructions: Place a slice of prosciutto and two sage leaves on each veal piece; secure with a toothpick.
Season lightly with pepper and dredge the veal side only in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil and 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add veal prosciutto-side down and cook 2 minutes until prosciutto is crisp; flip and cook 1 minute more. Transfer to a platter.
Pour wine into the skillet, scraping up any browned bits, and reduce by half.
Remove from heat, swirl in remaining butter, and pour sauce over the saltimbocca. Remove toothpicks and serve immediately.

name: Supplì al Telefono
description: Crispy Roman fried rice balls with a molten mozzarella center, named for the cheese strands that stretch like a telephone wire.
ingredients: 4 oz fresh mozzarella cut into cubes
instructions: Sauté onion in olive oil until soft; add ground beef and brown, breaking it up.
Add wine, cook 1 minute, then add passata and simmer 20 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in dry rice and cook with the sauce, adding water as needed, until rice is just cooked. Stir in Parmigiano. Spread on a tray and cool completely in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
With damp hands, form oblong rice balls around a cube of mozzarella.
Dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry in 350°F vegetable oil for 3–4 minutes until golden. Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

name: Coda alla Vaccinara
description: Rich Roman braised oxtail stewed with tomato, celery, pine nuts, and dark chocolate in the traditional butcher-quarter style.
instructions: Season oxtail with salt and pepper. Brown in olive oil in a large Dutch oven over high heat in batches; set aside.
In the same pot, sauté onion, garlic, and half the celery over medium heat until soft. Add tomato paste and cook 3 minutes.
Return oxtail to pot, add wine and cook 2 minutes. Add passata, cinnamon, and enough water to nearly submerge meat.
Cover and braise on lowest heat for 2.5–3 hours until meat is very tender.
Stir in remaining celery, pine nuts, raisins, and grated chocolate; simmer uncovered 20 minutes.
Adjust seasoning and finish with parsley. Serve with crusty bread or polenta.

name: Abbacchio Scottadito
description: Chargrilled Roman lamb chops marinated with garlic, rosemary, and lemon, cooked hot enough to "burn the fingers" at the table.
ingredients: 2 lb small lamb rib chops (about 12 chops)
2 sprigs fresh rosemary leaves stripped and minced
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Pound lamb chops gently to flatten to about 1/2-inch thickness.
Whisk together garlic, rosemary, olive oil, lemon juice, and red pepper. Coat chops and marinate 15 minutes at room temperature.
Heat a grill or cast-iron pan to very high heat.
Season chops with salt and pepper; grill 2–3 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

name: Ribollita
description: Hearty Tuscan bread-and-bean soup thickened with day-old bread and lacinato kale, slow-simmered for deep flavor.
ingredients: 1 bunch Tuscan kale stems removed, chopped
instructions: Cook pancetta in a large heavy pot over medium heat until the fat renders, about 5 minutes.
Add olive oil, onion, celery, and carrot; cook until soft, 10 minutes. Add garlic, cook 2 minutes. Add red pepper flakes and tomato paste; cook 5 minutes.
Add stock, kale, cannellini beans, Parmigiano rind, and rosemary. Bring to a boil, then simmer with lid cracked for 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Place thick slices of day-old bread in individual bowls and ladle soup on top.
Drizzle with extra-virgin olive oil and finish with grated Parmigiano. Serve with additional bread.

name: Bistecca alla Fiorentina
description: Thick-cut Florentine T-bone steak from Chianina beef, grilled over hardwood coals and served rare with just olive oil, salt, and lemon.
ingredients: 1 Florentine T-bone steak 2 to 3 inches thick (about 2.5 lb)
instructions: Remove steak from the fridge 1 hour before cooking; pat very dry.
Heat a charcoal grill or cast-iron grill pan to very high heat.
Season steak generously on both sides with salt and pepper.
Grill 5–7 minutes per side for rare to medium-rare, turning once. Let the bone side also touch the grill for 2 minutes.
Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with olive oil, garnish with rosemary, and serve with lemon wedges. Carve tableside.

name: Panzanella
description: Tuscan summer bread salad with ripe tomatoes, cucumber, red onion, and basil in a tangy red-wine-vinegar dressing.
ingredients: 6 oz stale ciabatta or Tuscan bread torn into chunks
1.5 lb ripe tomatoes cut into chunks
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Soak bread chunks in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes; squeeze out excess water and crumble into large pieces into a salad bowl.
Add tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion to the bowl.
Whisk together vinegar, olive oil, garlic, sugar, salt, and pepper to make dressing.
Pour dressing over the salad and toss well. Let sit 15 minutes for bread to absorb the juices.
Add basil, toss gently, and serve at room temperature.

name: Cinghiale al Cinghiale
description: Ruscan wild-boar ragù slow-braised in Chianti with juniper berries, rosemary, and herbs, served over pappardelle.
ingredients: 2 lb wild boar shoulder cut into 1-inch cubes
1 bottle Chianti or other robust red wine
instructions: Marinate boar in wine with aromatics (onion, carrots, celery, garlic, rosemary, juniper, bay) overnight in the fridge.
Drain meat and vegetables, reserving the wine marinade. Pat meat dry.
Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over high heat; brown meat in batches. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the drained vegetables over medium heat until soft. Add tomato paste and cook 3 minutes.
Return meat to pot, add reserved wine, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to lowest, cover, and braise 2–2.5 hours until meat is very tender.
Shred meat, taste and adjust seasoning. Cook pappardelle to al dente; toss with ragù. Serve with Pecorino.

name: Tortellini in Brodo
description: Emilian pork-and-Parmigiano-stuffed tortellini floating in a rich golden capon broth, the quintessential Christmas dish of Bologna.
