ingredients: For the broth: 1 whole capon or chicken (3 lb)
For the filling: 1/4 lb prosciutto di Parma finely minced
For the pasta: 2 cups all-purpose flour
instructions: For broth: place chicken, brisket, and vegetables in a large pot with cold water, bring to a boil, skim foam, and simmer 2 hours. Strain and season with salt.
For filling: brown pork in a dry skillet. Cool, then combine with prosciutto, Parmigiano, egg, and nutmeg. Season well.
For pasta: mound flour, make a well, add eggs and a pinch of salt. Knead 10 minutes until smooth and silky. Rest 30 minutes wrapped.
Roll dough paper-thin. Cut 1.5-inch squares; place a tiny mound of filling on each. Fold diagonally and wrap around a finger, pressing ends together to form tortellini.
Bring broth to a gentle simmer. Cook tortellini 3–4 minutes until they float.
Ladle into bowls, ensuring plenty of broth, and serve with extra Parmigiano.

name: Lasagne alla Bolognese
description: Classic Emilian lasagne layered with slow-cooked Bolognese ragù, silky béchamel, and ample Parmigiano Reggiano.
ingredients: For assembly: 1 cup grated Parmigiano Reggiano
instructions: Ragù: Sauté vegetables in butter until soft. Add beef and pork; brown well. Add wine, reduce. Add milk, reduce. Add passata and simmer very gently, partially covered, 1.5 hours. Season.
Béchamel: Melt butter, whisk in flour, cook 1 minute. Gradually whisk in warm milk until smooth. Simmer until thick; season with nutmeg and salt.
Blanch lasagna sheets briefly in salted water; lay on damp towels.
Preheat oven to 375°F. Spread thin layer of béchamel on pan bottom. Layer pasta, ragù, béchamel, Parmigiano; repeat 4–5 layers, ending with béchamel and Parmigiano.
Dot top with butter; bake 40–45 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Osso Buco alla Milanese
description: Milanese braised veal shanks in white wine with a bright gremolata of lemon, garlic, and parsley, traditionally served with risotto milanese.
ingredients: 4 cross-cut veal shanks about 1.5 inches thick (about 3 lb total)
For gremolata: 1/4 cup flat-leaf parsley minced
instructions: Pat shanks dry and season with salt and pepper. Dredge in flour.
Brown shanks in butter and oil in a wide Dutch oven over high heat, 4 minutes per side. Remove.
In same pot, sauté onion, carrot, celery, and garlic over medium heat until soft. Add wine, scrape up browned bits, and reduce by half.
Add stock, tomatoes, thyme, and bay leaves. Return shanks. Liquid should reach halfway up the shanks.
Cover and braise over very low heat or in a 325°F oven for 1.5–2 hours until meat is very tender.
Mix gremolata ingredients. Serve osso buco over risotto milanese, topped with gremolata.

name: Risotto alla Milanese
description: Saffron-gilded Milanese risotto made with beef stock, butter, and abundant Parmigiano Reggiano — the classic partner to osso buco.
instructions: Bring stock to a low simmer in a saucepan. Dissolve saffron in 1/2 cup warm stock; set aside.
Melt 3 tbsp butter in a wide heavy pan over medium heat. Sauté shallot until soft, 3 minutes.
Add rice and stir 2 minutes until edges turn translucent. Add wine and cook until absorbed.
Add stock one ladle at a time, stirring frequently; each addition should be absorbed before adding the next. Cook 18–20 minutes total until rice is al dente and creamy.
Stir in saffron stock, remaining butter, and Parmigiano. Remove from heat, stir vigorously to mantecare.
Season with salt and pepper; serve immediately scattered with parsley.

name: Cotoletta alla Milanese
description: Bone-in veal chop breaded in fine breadcrumbs and shallow-fried in clarified butter until golden, the original Milanese cutlet.
ingredients: 2 bone-in veal rib chops about 3/4-inch thick (about 1.5 lb)
instructions: Using a meat mallet, pound veal chops on both sides to about 1/4-inch thickness, keeping bone attached.
Season with salt. Set up a dredging station: flour, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs.
Dredge each chop in flour, dip in egg, then coat evenly in breadcrumbs, pressing firmly.
Heat clarified butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry chops 3–4 minutes per side until deeply golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly on a wire rack, season with sea salt, and serve immediately with lemon wedges and parsley.

name: Vitello Tonnato
description: Elegant Piedmontese cold sliced veal draped in a silky tuna-and-caper sauce, a classic summer centerpiece.
ingredients: 2 lb veal loin or tenderloin tied
1 can tuna in olive oil drained
capers and lemon slices for garnish
instructions: Simmer onion, carrot, celery, wine, bay leaf, and cloves in salted water 10 minutes. Add veal and simmer gently 60–75 minutes until just cooked through. Cool in liquid.
For sauce: blend eggs, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. With blender running, stream in olive oil until a thick mayonnaise forms.
Add tuna, anchovies, capers, and a splash of cooking liquid; blend until smooth and pourable. Adjust seasoning.
Remove veal from liquid, pat dry, and slice paper-thin against the grain.
Arrange slices on a platter, overlapping. Spoon sauce generously over all.
Garnish with capers and lemon slices. Refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight before serving.

name: Bagna Cauda
description: Warm Piedmontese garlic-and-anchovy dipping sauce served hot at the table with raw and lightly cooked seasonal vegetables.
ingredients: 2 oz anchovy fillets in oil drained
assorted vegetables for dipping: fennel, radicchio, bell pepper, carrot, cauliflower
instructions: Mince garlic very finely or crush to a paste.
Combine garlic and olive oil in a small heavy saucepan over the lowest possible heat.
Cook very gently, stirring often, for 15 minutes until garlic is soft and fragrant but not colored.
Add anchovy fillets and mash with a wooden spoon until they dissolve into the oil. Stir 5 minutes more.
Remove from heat and swirl in butter until melted.
Transfer to a fondue pot or ceramic warmer. Serve surrounded by vegetables and crusty bread for dipping.

name: Farinata Genovese
description: Golden Ligurian chickpea-flour pancake baked in a blazing-hot oven until crisp at the edges and custardy in the center.
ingredients: 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the pan
instructions: Whisk chickpea flour into cold water until smooth; whisk in 1/4 cup olive oil and salt. Let batter rest 4 hours or overnight at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 500°F (with a 12-inch cast-iron skillet inside) for at least 30 minutes.
Skim any foam from batter surface.
Carefully add 2 tbsp olive oil to the hot skillet; pour in batter to a depth of about 1/4 inch.
Bake 15–20 minutes until golden and set at center with slightly crisp edges.
Season generously with black pepper; slice into wedges and serve hot.

name: Risi e Bisi
description: Venetian spring rice-and-pea dish — wetter than risotto, thicker than soup — made from fresh peas and pancetta in pea-pod broth.
ingredients: 2 cups Vialone Nano or Arborio rice
salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: For pea broth: Simmer pea pods in 7 cups salted water with a sliced onion and carrot for 30 minutes; strain.
In a wide pot, sauté pancetta and onion in butter and olive oil until onion is translucent. Add parsley and cook 1 minute.
Add peas and a ladle of broth; cover and simmer gently 5 minutes until almost tender.
Add rice and remaining hot broth all at once; stir and cook at a gentle boil for 18–20 minutes until rice is tender. The consistency should be quite soupy.
Remove from heat; stir in remaining butter and Parmigiano.
Season with salt and white pepper; serve immediately in warm bowls.

name: Sarde in Saor
description: Venetian sweet-and-sour marinated sardines layered with agrodolce onions, raisins, and pine nuts — best made two days ahead.
ingredients: 1.5 lb fresh sardines cleaned filleted and butterflied
1/2 cup raisins soaked in warm water
instructions: Dust sardine fillets in flour; shallow-fry in hot vegetable oil until golden, about 2 minutes per side. Season with salt and drain on paper towels.
Sauté onions in olive oil over low heat for 25–30 minutes until very soft but not colored.
Raise heat, add wine vinegar and white wine; cook 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
In a glass dish, layer sardines, onions, drained raisins, and pine nuts. Repeat, ending with the onion mixture.
Pour any remaining sousing liquid over top. Cover and refrigerate at least 24–48 hours.
Serve at room temperature as part of an antipasto.

name: Tiramisù
description: The Treviso-born mascarpone-and-espresso layered dessert with savoiardi, egg zabaglione, and a dusting of cocoa.
ingredients: 1/4 cup Dutch-process cocoa powder for dusting
instructions: Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water until pale and ribbon-like, about 8 minutes. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Fold in mascarpone until smooth.
Whip heavy cream and vanilla to soft peaks. Fold cream into mascarpone mixture in two additions.
Mix espresso with demerara sugar in a shallow bowl.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger in espresso (1 second per side) and arrange in a single layer in an 8×11-inch baking dish.
Spread half the cream over ladyfingers; dust with cocoa. Repeat with a second layer. Dust top generously with cocoa. Refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight before serving.

name: Arancini
description: Saffron-scented Sicilian fried rice balls stuffed with a rich ragù, green peas, and melted caciocavallo cheese.
ingredients: 1/4 lb caciocavallo or mozzarella cut into small cubes
instructions: Bring stock, butter, and saffron to a boil; add rice, cover, reduce to low, cook until liquid evaporates (~20 min). Off heat, stir in Parmigiano, cool 10 min, then mix in eggs. Spread on baking sheet; refrigerate 1 hour.
Brown pancetta; add onion, cook until soft. Add beef and pork; brown. Add tomato paste, cook 3 min. Add wine, reduce. Add peas; season. Cool.
With damp hands, cup 1/2 cup rice, indent center, fill with 1–2 tsp ragù and a cube of cheese. Close and roll into a ball.
Whisk flour, water, eggs, and salt into batter. Dip balls in batter then coat in breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry at 370°F in batches of 3 until golden all over, 4–5 min. Drain on paper towels. Serve immediately.

name: Caponata
description: Sicilian sweet-and-sour eggplant relish with celery, olives, capers, and pine nuts in a rich agrodolce tomato sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 cup pitted green olives chopped and rinsed
instructions: Toss eggplant with salt; drain in colander 20 minutes. Pat dry. Roast at 425°F with 1/4 cup olive oil on a lined baking sheet for 30–35 minutes until browned.
Heat remaining oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté celery, onion, and bell pepper until soft, 8 minutes.
Add tomato paste; cook 5 minutes. Add red pepper flakes.
Add olives, capers, raisins, vinegar, and sugar; cook 5 minutes for flavors to meld.
Fold in roasted eggplant gently. Taste and adjust sweet-sour balance with more vinegar or sugar.
Stir in pine nuts and parsley. Serve at room temperature; better the next day.

name: Pasta con le Sarde
description: Sicilian bucatini with fresh sardines, wild fennel, saffron, raisins, and pine nuts in the sweet-savory Palermitan tradition.
ingredients: 1 large fennel bulb halved, fronds reserved
1/3 cup golden raisins soaked and drained
instructions: Toast breadcrumbs in 3 tbsp olive oil until golden; set aside.
Dissolve saffron in white wine; set aside.
Boil a large pot of salted water. Cook fennel 10 minutes until tender; remove with a slotted spoon, dice, and reserve water for pasta.
Sauté onion in olive oil until translucent; add anchovies and garlic, cook until anchovies dissolve. Add diced fennel; cook 2 minutes.
Add saffron wine; reduce by half. Add raisins, pine nuts, and sardines; gently fold together, leaving some texture. Cook pasta in the fennel water to 1 minute shy of al dente.
Add pasta and 1 cup pasta water to the pan; toss until al dente. Serve with toasted breadcrumbs and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Cannoli Siciliani
description: Crispy Sicilian pastry tubes filled with sweetened sheep's-milk ricotta, chocolate chips, and candied orange peel.
ingredients: 2 tbsp unsalted butter at room temperature
For filling: 2 lb fresh ricotta well-drained overnight
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, cinnamon, and salt. Work in butter until crumbly. Beat egg with Marsala; add to flour and knead until smooth. Rest 30 minutes wrapped.
Roll dough paper-thin. Cut into 4-inch rounds. Wrap around metal cannoli tubes; seal edges with egg white.
Deep-fry at 350°F until golden and bubbled, 2–3 minutes. Drain and cool slightly before sliding off tubes.
Beat ricotta with powdered sugar until smooth. Fold in chocolate chips and orange peel. Transfer to a piping bag.
Fill shells just before serving, piping from both ends.
Dust with powdered sugar and garnish ends with pistachios or extra chocolate chips.

name: Pizza Margherita Napoletana
description: Authentic Neapolitan pizza with a charred, airy cornicione, San Marzano tomato sauce, fresh fior di latte mozzarella, and basil.
ingredients: For dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour (or 00 flour)
For toppings: 1 cup San Marzano tomatoes hand-crushed
6 oz fresh mozzarella or fior di latte sliced
instructions: Combine flour, yeast, and salt. Add water; mix until shaggy, then knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Rest covered at room temperature 8–24 hours.
Divide into 2 balls; rest 1 hour at room temperature.
Place a baking steel or heavy sheet pan on top rack; preheat oven to maximum temperature (500–550°F) for 45 minutes.
Stretch each dough ball to a 10-inch round on floured surface; do not use a rolling pin.
Spread crushed tomatoes lightly, leaving a 3/4-inch border. Top with mozzarella slices. Drizzle olive oil, season with salt.
Bake 6–8 minutes until crust is charred in spots and cheese is bubbling. Top with fresh basil.

name: Parmigiana di Melanzane
description: Campanian layered eggplant Parmesan baked with Neapolitan tomato sauce, mozzarella, hard-boiled eggs, and fried eggplant.
ingredients: 3 cups marinara or Neapolitan tomato sauce
instructions: Salt eggplant slices generously; stack and weigh down 90 minutes. Rinse and pat very dry.
Fry eggplant in olive oil over medium heat until golden, 3–4 min per side; drain on paper towels.
Preheat oven to 325°F. Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce in the bottom of a 9×13 baking dish.
Layer: eggplant, sauce, torn basil, mozzarella, and Parmigiano. Repeat until all ingredients are used, ending with sauce and cheeses.
Bake 50–60 minutes until bubbling and deeply golden.
Rest 20 minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Orecchiette con Cime di Rapa
description: Pugliese ear-shaped pasta tossed with bitter broccoli rabe, anchovy-garlic oil, and chili flakes — a staple of Bari's street cooks.
ingredients: 1 bunch broccoli rabe stems trimmed and chopped
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli rabe 2–3 minutes until bright green; remove with tongs and set aside. Keep water boiling.
Add orecchiette to the same water; cook to 1 minute shy of al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Heat olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add garlic and anchovies; cook until garlic is golden and anchovies dissolve, 3 minutes. Add red pepper flakes, cook 30 seconds.
Add broccoli rabe and toss. Add pasta and half the pasta water; toss vigorously over high heat 1–2 minutes until everything is well-coated.
Adjust with more pasta water if needed; season with salt and pepper.
Finish with parsley and serve with grated Pecorino.

name: Malloreddus alla Campidanese
description: Sardinian saffron-tinged gnocchetti shells in a slow-cooked fennel sausage-and-tomato sauce, finished with aged Pecorino Sardo.
ingredients: 3/4 lb Sardinian fennel sausage casings removed
1 can whole peeled tomatoes crushed by hand
1 pinch saffron dissolved in 2 tbsp warm water
instructions: Brown sausage meat in olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat, breaking it up; remove and set aside, leaving fat in pan.
Sauté garlic in remaining fat until fragrant; discard garlic. Add fennel seeds and red pepper; cook 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, saffron water, salt, and pepper; simmer 20 minutes until sauce thickens. Return sausage to pan.
Cook malloreddus in a large pot of salted water according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water.
Drain pasta and add directly to sauce; toss well, adding a splash of pasta water if needed.
Serve with abundant grated Pecorino Sardo.

name: Canederli in Brodo
description: Tyrolean bread dumplings made with stale bread, speck, and herbs, simmered in a clear golden meat broth.
ingredients: 3 oz speck or bacon finely minced
6 cups rich meat or chicken broth
instructions: Sauté onion in butter until translucent; cool slightly.
Toss together bread cubes, speck, sautéed onion, and parsley in a large bowl.
Beat eggs with milk; pour over bread mixture. Mix well and let rest 20 minutes until bread is moist and clumping.
Add flour, nutmeg, salt, and pepper; mix until the dough holds together when pressed. If too wet, add more flour a tablespoon at a time.
With damp hands, form golf-ball-sized dumplings. Test one in simmering broth — if it falls apart, mix more flour into remaining dough.
Simmer canederli in gently simmering broth 15 minutes until cooked through. Serve in deep bowls with broth.

name: Frico Croccante
description: Crispy Friulian cheese-and-potato wafer made from aged Montasio, pan-fried until molten in the center and lacey at the edges.
ingredients: 1 lb aged Montasio cheese (or a mix of aged and semi-aged) grated
salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Squeeze excess moisture from grated potatoes and onion in a clean kitchen towel.
Mix cheese, potato, and onion together in a bowl; season with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add half the cheese-potato mixture, pressing into an even layer. Cook 8–10 minutes until deep golden on the bottom.
Flip carefully using a plate; add remaining oil and cook the second side 7–8 minutes until crisp and golden.
Slide onto a cutting board; cool 2 minutes (it crisps as it cools) and cut into wedges. Repeat with remaining mixture.

name: Arrosticini Abruzzesi
description: Abruzzese skewers of cubed castrated sheep meat grilled over a narrow charcoal grill and eaten straight off the wooden stick.
ingredients: 2 lb lamb shoulder or mutton cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Thread 4–5 cubes of lamb tightly onto each wooden skewer, alternating lean and fat pieces.
Season skewers generously with salt and pepper.
Brush lightly with olive oil infused with rosemary and garlic.
Grill over very hot charcoal in a narrow grill (the cylindrical fornacella style) or a very hot cast-iron ridged pan, 3–4 minutes per side, turning so all sides are browned.
Serve immediately with crusty bread and lemon wedges.

name: Texas Smoked Brisket
description: A whole packer brisket seasoned with just salt and pepper and slow-smoked over oak for authentic Texas bark and a deep smoke ring.
ingredients: 2 cups beef tallow or unsalted butter for spritzing
instructions: Trim fat cap on brisket to 1/4 inch and remove any hard fat.
Mix salt, pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder; coat brisket generously on all sides.
Preheat smoker to 225°F using post oak or hickory wood.
Place brisket fat-side up on smoker grates; smoke for 8-10 hours until internal temp reaches 165°F.
Wrap tightly in butcher paper; return to smoker.
Continue smoking until internal temp reaches 200-205°F and probe slides in like butter, about 4-6 more hours.
Rest wrapped in a cooler for at least 1 hour before slicing against the grain.

name: Carolina Vinegar Pulled Pork
description: Smoked pork shoulder mopped with tangy vinegar sauce in the tradition of Eastern North Carolina BBQ.
ingredients: 2 cups apple cider vinegar for sauce
instructions: Mix salt, pepper, and paprika; rub all over pork shoulder.
Preheat smoker to 250°F with oak or hickory wood.
Place pork on smoker and smoke for 8-10 hours, mopping with vinegar-beer mop every hour.
Meanwhile combine sauce ingredients in a saucepan; simmer 25 minutes.
Smoke until internal temp reaches 200°F.
Rest wrapped in foil for 1 hour.
Shred pork, discarding bone and excess fat.
Toss shredded pork with vinegar sauce and serve.

name: Baby Back Ribs 3-2-1 Method
description: Tender smoked baby back ribs using the classic 3-2-1 method: smoke, braise, then sauce for fall-off-the-bone results.
instructions: Remove membrane from bone side of ribs using paper towel for grip.
Mix brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, salt, and cayenne; coat ribs generously on both sides.
Preheat smoker to 225°F with apple or cherry wood.
Smoke ribs directly on grates for 3 hours.
Wrap each rack in foil with apple cider, butter, and honey; return to smoker for 2 hours at 225°F.
Unwrap ribs; brush with BBQ sauce; return to smoker uncovered for 1 hour to set sauce.
Rest 10 minutes; slice and serve.

name: St. Louis Style Smoked Ribs
description: Spare ribs trimmed to a rectangular St. Louis cut, smoked low and slow to achieve a beautifully lacquered bark.
ingredients: 2 racks St. Louis style spare ribs
instructions: Trim ribs to even rectangular shape; remove membrane from bone side.
Slather ribs with yellow mustard as binder.
Mix dry rub ingredients; coat ribs liberally on both sides.
Preheat smoker to 275°F with apple or peach wood.
Place ribs bone-side down; smoke for 4.5-5 hours, spritzing with apple juice every 45 minutes after first hour.
In last 30 minutes brush with BBQ sauce; cook until ribs bend easily at 195-200°F.
Rest 15 minutes; slice and serve.

name: Smoked Beef Short Ribs
description: Massive beef short ribs seasoned with a simple salt-and-pepper rub and smoked until deeply tender with a bold bark.
ingredients: 3 lb beef short ribs plate cut 4-5 bones
instructions: Trim excess fat cap and silver skin from top of ribs.
Slather ribs with mustard; season liberally with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Preheat smoker to 250°F with oak or cherry wood.
Place ribs bone-side down; smoke for 3 hours without opening lid.
Mix beef stock and vinegar in spray bottle; spritz ribs every hour.
Continue smoking until internal temp reaches 203-210°F and probe slides in like butter, about 5-6 more hours total.
Wrap in foil; rest 30 minutes before serving.

name: Memphis Dry Rub Ribs
description: Baby back ribs smoked low and slow with a bold paprika-and-spice dry rub and no sauce, in the authentic Memphis style.
instructions: Remove membrane from bone side of ribs.
Mix all dry rub ingredients; generously season ribs on both sides, pressing into meat.
Preheat smoker to 275°F using hickory wood.
Place ribs on smoker; cook for 4.5-5 hours spritzing with apple juice every 30 minutes after first hour.
Ribs are done when meat pulls back from bones 1/4 inch and rack bends easily at 200°F.
Rest 15 minutes; dust with another round of dry rub before slicing and serving.

name: Kansas City Sweet and Saucy Ribs
description: Baby back ribs smoked low and slow and finished with a thick sweet molasses-based Kansas City style BBQ sauce.
instructions: Remove membrane from back of ribs; season both sides with mixed dry rub.
Preheat smoker to 225°F with apple or cherry wood.
Smoke ribs for 3 hours.
Wrap ribs in foil with apple cider and butter; cook 2 hours more.
Stir molasses and Worcestershire into BBQ sauce.
Unwrap ribs; brush generously with KC BBQ sauce; smoke uncovered 45 minutes until sauce is sticky and set.
Rest 10 minutes; slice and serve with extra sauce.

name: Brisket Burnt Ends
description: Smoky cubed brisket point sauced with buttery Kansas City BBQ glaze and returned to the smoker for sticky caramelized bites.
ingredients: 4 tbsp unsalted butter cut in pats
instructions: Season brisket point with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika.
Smoke at 250°F with oak or cherry wood for 6-8 hours until internal temp reaches 200°F.
Remove from smoker; rest 20 minutes then cut into 1-inch cubes.
Place cubed brisket in foil pan; add butter pats, BBQ sauce, brown sugar, vinegar, and honey.
Toss to coat; cover pan with foil.
Return to smoker at 250°F for 1.5-2 hours, tossing every 30 minutes until sauce caramelizes.
Serve immediately.

name: Smoked Turkey
description: A whole turkey brined in apple cider and slow-smoked over apple wood for a juicy, deeply flavored bird perfect for any occasion.
instructions: Combine cider, water, vinegar, salt, brown sugar, Worcestershire, garlic powder, and onion powder in large pot; brine turkey 12-24 hours.
Remove turkey from brine; pat dry thoroughly.
Mix softened butter with paprika and pepper; rub under and over skin.
Preheat smoker to 275°F with apple wood.
Place turkey breast-side up on smoker; cook 4-5 hours until breast reaches 165°F.
Rest tented with foil for 20 minutes before carving.

name: Alabama White Sauce Smoked Chicken
description: Smoky split chicken halves brushed with a tangy mayo-based Alabama white sauce for a classic Southern BBQ experience.
instructions: Rub chicken halves with olive oil; season with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika.
Preheat smoker to 275°F with hickory or pecan wood.
Place chicken halves skin-side up on smoker grates.
Smoke for 2.5-3 hours until breast meat reaches 165°F.
Whisk together mayo, vinegar, brown sugar, mustard, horseradish, and cayenne for white sauce.
Baste chicken with white sauce in final 15 minutes; cook until set.
Serve with additional white sauce on the side.

name: Smoked Sausage Links
description: Classic smoked pork sausage links slow-smoked over hickory until deeply flavored with a satisfying snap in the casing.
ingredients: 3 lb pork sausage links kielbasa or similar
instructions: Mix brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, and cayenne; lightly dust sausages with rub.
Preheat smoker to 225°F with hickory or pecan wood.
Place sausages on smoker grates.
Smoke for 2 hours spritzing with beer every 30 minutes.
Increase temperature to 275°F; smoke 30 more minutes until internal temp reaches 160°F.
Rest 5 minutes; serve with mustard and sauerkraut.

name: Classic Smashburger
description: Thin crispy-edged beef patties smashed on a screaming-hot griddle for maximum Maillard crust with melted American cheese.
ingredients: 1.5 lb ground beef 80/20 divided into 8 balls
kosher salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine mayo, mustard, ketchup, and garlic powder to make burger sauce; set aside.
Heat griddle or cast iron over high heat until smoking; butter and toast buns until golden; set aside.
Add beef balls to griddle 2-4 at a time; immediately smash flat with a burger press or heavy spatula over parchment; season with salt and pepper.
Cook 45-60 seconds until edges are deeply browned; scrape and flip with firm pressure.
Place cheese on half the patties; stack a second patty on each cheesed patty; cook 30 seconds more.
Assemble on toasted buns with sauce, pickles, lettuce, and tomato.

name: Juicy Lucy Burger
description: A Minnesota-style stuffed burger with molten cheese sealed inside the patty for an explosive cheesy surprise.
ingredients: 4 oz American cheese cut in cubes
lettuce tomato and pickles for serving
instructions: Mix Worcestershire, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper into ground beef gently.
Divide beef into 8 equal thin patties.
Place a mound of mixed cheese in center of 4 patties; top with remaining 4 patties; seal edges tightly.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Grill stuffed patties 4-5 minutes per side until internal temp reaches 165°F; do not press.
Toast buttered buns on grill until golden.
Rest burgers 3 minutes before serving; warn guests about hot cheese interior.

name: BBQ Bacon Burger
description: A thick grilled beef burger topped with crispy bacon, cheddar, caramelized onions, and smoky BBQ sauce.
instructions: Form beef into 4 patties; season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder; refrigerate until grilling.
Cook bacon in skillet until crispy; set aside.
Caramelize onions in butter over medium-low heat 20-25 minutes until golden.
Preheat grill to medium-high; cook patties 3-4 minutes per side until 160°F internal temp.
Top each patty with cheddar in last minute of cooking; cover to melt.
Toast buns on grill.
Assemble with BBQ sauce on bun, lettuce, patty with cheese, bacon, and caramelized onions.

name: Grilled Hot Dogs with Toppings
description: Char-grilled beef hot dogs in toasted buns with classic fixings of mustard, relish, onion, and sport peppers.
instructions: Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Score hot dogs with shallow diagonal cuts on each side for better caramelization.
Grill hot dogs 6-8 minutes turning frequently until nicely charred and blistered.
Butter buns and toast cut-side down on grill 1-2 minutes until golden.
Place hot dog in bun; add mustard in zigzag pattern; top with relish, onion, tomato, and sport peppers.
Add pickle spear to side; dust with celery salt; serve immediately.

name: Bacon-Wrapped Grilled Pork Tenderloin
description: Juicy pork tenderloin wrapped in bacon and grilled until caramelized outside and perfectly rosy within.
instructions: Mix mustard, brown sugar, garlic powder, paprika, pepper, salt, and thyme; rub over tenderloin.
Wrap tenderloin tightly with overlapping bacon strips securing with toothpicks.
Preheat grill to medium heat; set up two-zone cooking.
Sear wrapped tenderloin over direct heat 2-3 minutes per side until bacon is browned.
Move to indirect heat; close lid and cook until pork reaches 145°F internal temp, about 20-25 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing.

name: Grilled Flank Steak with Garlic Herb Marinade
description: Marinated flank steak grilled hot and fast over charcoal and sliced thin against the grain for maximum tenderness.
instructions: Whisk together soy sauce, olive oil, Worcestershire, garlic, rosemary, thyme, brown sugar, pepper, lemon juice, and pepper flakes for marinade.
Score flank steak lightly in crosshatch pattern; submerge in marinade; refrigerate 4-8 hours.
Remove steak from marinade; pat dry; bring to room temperature 30 minutes.
Preheat grill to high heat.
Grill steak 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare (130°F internal).
Rest 8 minutes then slice very thin against the grain.

name: Grilled Chicken Thighs with Honey Sriracha Glaze
description: Bone-in chicken thighs grilled over two-zone heat then glazed with a sticky honey sriracha sauce for irresistible caramelization.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika; let sit 30 minutes.
Whisk honey, sriracha, soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic together for glaze.
Preheat grill to medium with two-zone setup; brush grates with oil.
Place thighs skin-side down over indirect heat; cook 25 minutes flipping once.
Move to direct heat skin-side down; brush generously with glaze; grill 5-7 minutes per side until internal temp reaches 165°F and glaze is caramelized.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Grilled Salmon with Brown Butter and Dill
description: Salmon fillets seasoned simply and grilled over high heat then finished with a nutty brown butter and fresh dill sauce.
instructions: Pat salmon dry; brush with olive oil; season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Preheat grill to high heat; clean and oil grates well.
Place salmon skin-side down on grill; cook 4-5 minutes without moving.
Carefully flip; cook 3-4 more minutes until salmon flakes easily at 130-135°F.
Meanwhile melt butter in small skillet over medium heat until golden and nutty; remove from heat.
Stir in dill, capers, lemon juice, and pepper flakes into brown butter.
Plate salmon and spoon brown butter sauce over top.

name: Grilled Lamb Chops with Garlic and Rosemary
description: Rack of lamb chops marinated in garlic and rosemary then grilled hot and fast to medium-rare perfection.
ingredients: 8 lamb rib chops from a rack of lamb
instructions: Combine garlic, rosemary, olive oil, salt, pepper, lemon juice, mustard, and oregano in small bowl.
Coat lamb chops in marinade; let marinate 30 minutes at room temperature.
Preheat grill to high heat; clean and oil grates.
Shake excess marinade from chops; place on grill over direct heat.
Grill 3 minutes per side for medium-rare (135°F internal).
Rest 3 minutes; serve immediately.

name: Grilled Shrimp Skewers with Garlic Butter
description: Jumbo shrimp threaded on skewers and grilled in under 10 minutes with a lemon garlic butter baste.
ingredients: 1.5 lb jumbo shrimp peeled and deveined
instructions: Toss shrimp with olive oil, paprika, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Thread shrimp onto skewers (2-3 per skewer in a C shape).
Mix melted butter, garlic, lemon juice, and parsley for basting sauce.
Preheat grill to high heat.
Grill shrimp 2-3 minutes per side brushing with garlic butter after flipping.
Remove immediately when shrimp are pink and curled; serve with remaining garlic butter.

name: Elote Grilled Corn on the Cob
description: Mexican street corn charred on the grill then slathered with mayo, cotija cheese, chili powder, and lime juice.
instructions: Peel back corn husks without removing; strip silk; soak in cold water 30 minutes.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Pull husks back up around corn; grill for 15 minutes turning occasionally.
Peel back husks; grill directly on grates 2-3 minutes per side until kernels are charred.
Brush each cob with mayo-sour cream mixture.
Roll in cotija cheese; dust with chili powder, paprika, and cayenne.
Squeeze lime juice over top; garnish with cilantro.

name: Grilled Portobello Mushrooms with Balsamic and Herbs
description: Meaty portobello caps marinated in balsamic and herbs then grilled until tender for a satisfying vegetarian BBQ main.
ingredients: 4 large portobello mushroom caps stems removed
1/4 cup goat cheese crumbled for serving
instructions: Whisk balsamic, olive oil, garlic, thyme, rosemary, mustard, salt, and pepper together for marinade.
Place mushroom caps gill-side up in shallow dish; pour marinade over; marinate 30 minutes.
Preheat grill to medium-high heat.
Place mushrooms gill-side down on grill; cook 5-6 minutes until grill marks form.
Flip; brush with remaining marinade; grill 5-6 more minutes until tender and cooked through.
Top with goat cheese and parsley; serve immediately.

name: Korean BBQ Short Ribs (Kalbi)
description: Flanken-cut beef short ribs marinated in soy, Asian pear, sesame oil, and garlic then grilled fast over high heat.
ingredients: steamed rice and kimchi for serving
instructions: Score ribs between bones if not already flanken cut.
Blend soy sauce, brown sugar, mirin, garlic, sesame oil, grated pear, ginger, green onions, and pepper into marinade.
Marinate ribs in marinade 4-8 hours in refrigerator; bring to room temperature before grilling.
Preheat grill to high heat.
Grill ribs 2-3 minutes per side until caramelized and cooked through.
Garnish with sesame seeds and additional green onion; serve with rice and kimchi.

name: Japanese Yakitori Chicken Skewers
description: Classic Japanese grilled chicken thigh and scallion skewers basted repeatedly with homemade tare sauce over charcoal.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs cut in 1.5 inch pieces
4 green onions cut in 1.5 inch pieces
instructions: Combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, water, and brown sugar in small saucepan; bring to boil then reduce to 1/3 volume over low heat about 30 minutes; cool to make tare.
Thread chicken pieces and scallion alternately on skewers (3 chicken and 2 scallion per skewer).
Preheat charcoal grill or broiler to high heat.
Grill skewers 6 minutes total turning every 90 seconds.
Baste with tare on both sides; grill 3-4 more minutes until caramelized.
Baste once more; grill 1 minute; serve with extra tare and shichimi.

name: Thai Grilled Chicken (Gai Yang)
description: Thai-style marinated chicken halves grilled until caramelized and served with a sweet chili dipping sauce.
ingredients: 1 whole chicken 3.5 lb butterflied and halved
1/4 cup sweet chili sauce for serving
instructions: Blend garlic, lemongrass, fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, white pepper, coriander, and coconut milk into marinade.
Coat chicken halves in marinade; refrigerate 4-8 hours.
Bring chicken to room temperature; preheat grill to medium heat.
Grill chicken skin-side down over indirect heat 20 minutes.
Flip; continue grilling 20-25 minutes until breast reaches 165°F.
Move to direct heat to char skin 3-4 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes; serve with sweet chili sauce and lime wedges.

name: Greek Pork Souvlaki Skewers
description: Marinated pork shoulder cubes threaded on skewers and grilled over charcoal for crispy edges and juicy centers.
ingredients: 1.5 lb pork shoulder cut in 1.5 inch cubes
instructions: Whisk olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, oregano, thyme, salt, and pepper together for marinade.
Toss pork cubes in marinade; refrigerate 2-4 hours.
Thread pork onto metal skewers (5-6 pieces per skewer).
Preheat grill to high heat.
Grill skewers 12-15 minutes total turning every 3-4 minutes until pork is caramelized and reaches 145°F.
Warm pita on grill 30 seconds per side.
Serve pork on pita with tzatziki, tomato, onion, and parsley.

name: Lebanese Kafta Kebabs
description: Spiced ground lamb and beef kofta shaped onto flat skewers and grilled over charcoal until juicy and charred.
instructions: Combine ground lamb, ground beef, grated onion, garlic, parsley, mint, and all spices; mix thoroughly.
Refrigerate mixture 30 minutes.
Divide into 8 portions; shape each portion around a flat metal skewer into a 6-inch cylinder.
Preheat grill to high heat.
Grill kafta skewers 3-4 minutes per side turning once or twice until browned and cooked through.
Serve on pita with hummus, tomato, onion, and fresh herbs.

name: Brazilian Picanha Churrasco
description: Rump cap steaks scored through the fat cap, skewered in a C-shape, seasoned with just rock salt, and grilled over charcoal Brazilian-style.
ingredients: 3 lb picanha rump cap with fat cap intact
crusty bread and rice for serving
instructions: Score fat cap in a crosshatch pattern without cutting into meat.
Slice picanha into 1-inch thick steaks keeping fat cap on.
Fold each steak into a C-shape and skewer so fat is on outside.
Season generously with rock salt and pepper on all sides.
Preheat charcoal grill to very high heat with glowing coals.
Grill skewered picanha turning every 3-4 minutes; cook with fat side toward heat first to render.
Cook 18-20 minutes total for medium (135°F internal).
Rest 5 minutes; slice thin at the table; serve with chimichurri.

name: Smoked Mac and Cheese
description: Creamy three-cheese macaroni in a cast iron skillet smoked at low temperature for an hour to develop a signature smoky depth.
ingredients: 1 lb elbow macaroni cooked al dente
instructions: Preheat smoker to 225°F using apple or cherry wood.
Cook macaroni to al dente; drain and set aside.
Melt 1/2 cup butter in 12-inch cast iron over medium heat; whisk in flour to form roux; whisk in mustard powder.
Add half-and-half; bring to boil whisking; reduce heat; whisk in cream cheese until smooth.
Stir in cheddar and gouda until melted; season with salt, pepper.
Fold in cooked macaroni; mix melted butter, panko, and paprika; sprinkle over top.
Place skillet in smoker; smoke 1 hour until topping is golden and mac is infused with smoke.

name: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancake Stack
description: Tall, golden buttermilk pancakes stacked high and served with maple syrup and butter for a classic dinner.
ingredients: butter and maple syrup for serving
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl whisk buttermilk, eggs, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour wet ingredients into dry and stir until just combined; let batter rest 10 minutes.
Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and lightly grease with butter.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake; cook until bubbles form on surface and edges look set, about 2 minutes.
Flip and cook 1-2 minutes more until golden. Repeat with remaining batter.
Serve stacked with butter and warm maple syrup.

name: Banana Pancakes
description: Moist, banana-studded pancakes topped with caramelized banana slices and a drizzle of maple syrup.
instructions: Whisk flour, baking powder, cinnamon, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Mash 2 bananas with sugar in a separate bowl until smooth; whisk in egg yolks, milk, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour wet ingredients into dry and stir until just combined.
Beat egg whites to soft peaks and fold into batter.
Slice remaining banana and set aside; heat a greased griddle over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake; place 2-3 banana slices on each. Cook until bubbles form, about 2 minutes, then flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Serve with maple syrup and extra banana slices.

name: Blueberry Pancakes
description: Fluffy buttermilk pancakes bursting with fresh blueberries, served with warm maple syrup.
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk buttermilk, eggs, melted butter, and vanilla in another bowl.
Fold wet into dry until just combined; gently fold in blueberries.
Let batter rest 5 minutes while heating a greased griddle over medium-low heat.
Pour 1/3 cup batter per pancake and cook until bubbles form on top, about 2-3 minutes.
Flip and cook 2 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with maple syrup and extra blueberries.

name: Savory Dutch Baby with Mushrooms and Gruyere
description: A dramatic oven-puffed German pancake loaded with sauteed mushrooms, Gruyere, and fresh thyme.
instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F and place a 12-inch cast iron skillet inside to heat.
Blend eggs, milk, flour, salt, and pepper in a blender until smooth; rest 10 minutes.
Meanwhile saute mushrooms in 1 tbsp butter over medium-high heat until browned, about 6 minutes; add garlic and thyme, season, and set aside.
Remove skillet from oven; add remaining 2 tbsp butter and swirl to coat. Immediately pour in batter.
Sprinkle Gruyere and mushrooms over top. Bake 20-22 minutes until puffed and deep golden.
Top with chives and flaky salt; serve immediately directly from the pan.

name: Lemon Ricotta Pancakes
description: Light and creamy ricotta pancakes brightened with lemon zest, topped with blueberry syrup.
instructions: Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar in a large bowl.
Whisk ricotta, buttermilk, egg yolks, lemon zest, lemon juice, and melted butter together.
Fold wet ingredients into dry until just combined.
Beat egg whites to stiff peaks; gently fold into batter in two additions.
Heat a lightly buttered griddle over medium-low heat. Cook 1/4-cup portions 2-3 minutes per side.
For blueberry syrup: simmer blueberries and maple syrup in a small pot 5 minutes until jammy.
Serve pancakes topped with warm blueberry syrup.

name: Sheet Pan Pancakes
description: Oven-baked buttermilk pancakes on a sheet pan cut into squares for feeding a crowd effortlessly.
ingredients: 5 tbsp unsalted butter melted plus more for pan
powdered sugar and maple syrup for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F; generously butter a rimmed 13x18-inch sheet pan.
Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk buttermilk, eggs, melted butter, and vanilla; fold into dry ingredients until just combined.
Pour batter onto prepared pan; spread evenly. Scatter berries over top.
Bake 15-18 minutes until set in center and edges are golden.
Cut into squares and serve with maple syrup.

name: Classic Belgian Waffles
description: Light yeast-risen Belgian waffles with deep pockets for holding pools of butter and maple syrup.
ingredients: butter and maple syrup for serving
fresh berries and whipped cream optional
instructions: Combine warm milk, melted butter, maple syrup, salt, and eggs in a large bowl; whisk to combine.
Add flour and yeast; stir until smooth. Cover and rest at room temperature 1 hour until bubbly. (Can refrigerate overnight.)
Preheat waffle iron; spray with nonstick cooking spray.
Stir down batter; pour 2/3 to 3/4 cup per waffle into the iron. Close and cook 5-6 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Serve immediately with butter, maple syrup, and fresh berries if desired.

name: Chicken and Waffles
description: Crispy buttermilk-fried chicken thighs served on fluffy Belgian waffles with hot sauce and maple syrup.
ingredients: maple syrup and hot sauce for serving
instructions: Cut chicken into strips; marinate in buttermilk, 1 egg, and hot sauce at least 1 hour or overnight.
Make waffle batter: whisk 2 cups flour, baking powder, cinnamon, and 1 tsp salt; combine buttermilk, oil, and egg yolks; fold together. Beat egg whites to peaks and fold in.
Whisk 3 cups flour, garlic powder, paprika, cayenne, and salt for dredge.
Dredge chicken in flour, back into buttermilk, then flour again.
Fry in 350°F oil 6-7 minutes per batch until golden and 165°F internal. Drain on a rack.
Cook waffles in preheated iron until golden and crisp.
Serve chicken on waffles with maple syrup and hot sauce.

name: Cornbread Waffles
description: Crispy-edged cornbread waffles with a tender crumb, perfect topped with fried eggs or chili.
instructions: Whisk cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Whisk molasses, melted butter, buttermilk, and 1 egg; pour into dry ingredients and stir until just combined. Let rest 10 minutes.
Preheat waffle iron; brush with melted butter or cooking spray.
Cook waffles in 1/4-cup ladlefuls until lightly browned and crisp, about 4-5 minutes.
Fry eggs in butter until whites are set and yolks are runny.
Serve cornbread waffles topped with a fried egg and hot sauce.

name: Savory Bacon-Cheddar Waffles
description: Crispy waffles loaded with crumbled bacon and sharp cheddar, served with sour cream and chives.
ingredients: sour cream and chives for serving
instructions: Cook bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain on paper towels and crumble. Reserve 1 tbsp drippings.
Whisk flour, baking powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Whisk milk, eggs, and melted butter together; stir into dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in crumbled bacon, cheddar, and green onions.
Preheat waffle iron and brush with reserved bacon drippings or cooking spray.
Cook waffles until deep golden and crisp, about 5 minutes.
Serve topped with sour cream and extra chives.

name: Classic French Toast
description: Thick-cut bread soaked in a vanilla-cinnamon custard and pan-fried to golden perfection.
ingredients: 8 thick slices brioche or challah bread
powdered sugar and maple syrup for serving
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt in a shallow dish.
Heat 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat until foamy.
Dip bread slices one at a time into the custard, letting each soak 20-30 seconds per side.
Cook in batches, 2-3 slices at a time, 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden.
Add more butter between batches.
Serve dusted with powdered sugar and warm maple syrup.

name: Baked French Toast Casserole
description: Overnight cream cheese French toast casserole with a brown sugar crumb topping, baked until golden.
instructions: Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Spread bread cubes in the pan.
Whisk cream cheese, eggs, milk, cream, brown sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt until smooth; pour over bread. Cover and refrigerate 3 hours or overnight.
Make crumb topping: mix flour, brown sugar, and cinnamon; cut in cold butter until pea-sized crumbles form. Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Let casserole sit at room temperature 10 minutes.
Scatter crumb topping over casserole; bake uncovered 20 minutes, then tent with foil and bake 30-35 minutes more until center is set.
Cool 5 minutes; serve with maple syrup.

name: Stuffed French Toast
description: Challah slices stuffed with whipped cream cheese and strawberry jam, baked until puffed and golden.
instructions: Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Whip cream cheese until fluffy. Slice each bread piece almost through horizontally; spread inside with cream cheese and jam. Press closed.
Whisk eggs, milk, melted butter, vanilla, honey, and salt in a bowl.
Dip each stuffed piece in custard, soaking at least 1 minute; arrange in dish. Pour remaining custard over. Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes to overnight.
Preheat oven to 375°F. Cover with foil; bake 25 minutes. Remove foil; bake 20-25 minutes until golden.
Toss strawberries with honey and lemon juice. Serve French toast topped with strawberries.

name: French Toast Sticks
description: Thick-cut bread fingers dipped in vanilla custard and pan-fried, rolled in cinnamon sugar for dipping.
ingredients: 8 slices Texas toast or thick white bread
instructions: Remove crusts from bread; cut each slice into 3 thick sticks.
Whisk eggs, cream, vanilla, sugar, cinnamon, and salt in a shallow dish.
Mix coating sugar and cinnamon on a plate; set aside.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Quickly dip each stick in egg mixture (do not soak); shake off excess and place in pan. Cook in batches 2-3 minutes per side until golden on all sides.
Immediately roll hot sticks in cinnamon sugar. Serve with maple syrup.

name: Brioche French Toast
description: Ultra-rich brioche slices soaked in orange-scented custard and pan-fried to a lacquered, golden finish.
ingredients: powdered sugar and maple syrup for serving
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, cream, sugar, vanilla, orange zest, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a shallow bowl.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat until foamy.
Soak brioche slices in custard 30 seconds per side.
Cook 2-3 slices at a time, 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden brown.
Add more butter as needed between batches.
Dust with powdered sugar; serve with maple syrup and fresh berries.

name: Tunisian Shakshuka
description: Bold North African eggs poached in a spiced harissa tomato sauce with olives, capers, and feta.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion and peppers; cook 8 minutes until softened and beginning to char at edges.
Add garlic, harissa, caraway seeds, and cumin; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes; simmer 15 minutes until thickened. Stir in olives and capers; season with salt.
Make 6 wells in the sauce; crack an egg into each. Spoon sauce over egg whites.
Cover and cook on lowest heat 5-8 minutes until whites are just set and yolks are still runny.
Crumble feta on top; scatter parsley. Serve directly from pan with crusty bread.

name: Fancy Huevos Rancheros
description: Elevated huevos rancheros with homemade ranchero sauce, crispy tortillas, refried beans, and cotija cheese.
instructions: Make ranchero sauce: sauté onion in 1 tbsp oil 5 minutes; add garlic, cumin, paprika, chipotle, and tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes; blend until smooth.
Warm tortillas one at a time in a brush-oiled skillet 15 seconds per side until puffed and fragrant.
Fry eggs in remaining oil to desired doneness; season with salt.
Spread refried beans on each tortilla; top with ranchero sauce and a fried egg.
Garnish with avocado, cotija, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime. Serve with hot sauce.

name: Eggs Benedict
description: Classic poached eggs on English muffins with Canadian bacon and blender hollandaise sauce.
instructions: Make hollandaise: blend egg yolks, lemon juice, water, cayenne, and salt. With blender running, slowly stream in hot melted butter until thick and emulsified. Keep warm.
Warm Canadian bacon in a skillet 1-2 minutes per side.
Toast English muffins; keep warm in a 200°F oven.
Fill a large pot with 3 inches of water; add vinegar and bring to a bare simmer.
Crack eggs into individual cups; gently slide into water. Poach 2-3 minutes until whites are set and yolks are runny. Remove with slotted spoon.
Assemble: muffin half, Canadian bacon, poached egg, hollandaise. Garnish with chives.

name: Eggs Florentine
description: Poached eggs over wilted garlic spinach on toasted English muffins with silky hollandaise sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter melted for hollandaise
instructions: Make hollandaise: blend egg yolks with lemon juice and salt; with blender running slowly pour in hot butter until thick. Season with hot sauce; set aside.
Wilt spinach in 1 tbsp butter with shallot over medium heat 2 minutes until just wilted; press out liquid and season.
Toast English muffins in remaining butter until golden.
Poach eggs: simmer water with vinegar; slide eggs in and cook 3-4 minutes. Remove with slotted spoon.
Assemble: muffin half, spinach, poached egg, hollandaise. Garnish with chives.

name: Chorizo and Potato Hash
description: Crispy smashed potatoes tossed with spicy Spanish chorizo and fried eggs in a one-pan dinner.
ingredients: 8 oz Spanish or Mexican chorizo sliced
instructions: Boil potatoes in salted water 12-15 minutes until fork-tender; drain.
Heat a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat; cook chorizo until browned, 3-4 minutes. Remove to a plate.
Add olive oil to pan; add potatoes and smash each with a spatula. Cook undisturbed 4-5 minutes until crisp; flip and crisp the other side.
Add bell pepper, onion, and garlic; toss and cook 4 minutes until softened. Add chorizo back and toss with paprika.
Make 4 wells; crack eggs in each. Cover and cook 3-4 minutes until whites are set.
Scatter parsley; serve with hot sauce.

name: Sausage Gravy and Biscuits
description: Fluffy homemade buttermilk biscuits smothered in rich, creamy pork sausage gravy for the ultimate comfort dinner.
instructions: Make biscuits: whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar, and salt. Cut in cold butter until pea-sized. Add buttermilk and stir until just combined.
Pat dough 3/4-inch thick on floured surface; cut into rounds. Bake at 450°F 12-14 minutes until golden.
Brown sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking into crumbles. Blot excess grease but leave 2 tbsp.
Sprinkle flour over sausage; stir and cook 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk and half-and-half.
Simmer 5-7 minutes until thickened; season with black pepper, red pepper flakes, and salt.
Split warm biscuits and smother generously with gravy.

name: Breakfast Strata
description: Savory make-ahead bread casserole layered with bacon, spinach, and Parmesan baked until puffed and golden.
instructions: Arrange bread cubes in a greased 9x13-inch casserole dish.
Cook bacon until crisp; crumble over bread. Leave 1 tbsp drippings in pan.
Sauté onion in drippings 4 minutes; add garlic and spinach; cook until wilted. Spoon over bread and bacon. Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt, mustard, and pepper; pour evenly over casserole.
Cover and refrigerate 1 hour to overnight.
Preheat oven to 375°F; bake uncovered 20 minutes, then tent with foil and bake 30-35 minutes until puffed and set. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Croque Madame
description: Classic French bistro sandwich of ham and Gruyere in bechamel sauce topped with a fried egg.
ingredients: salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Make bechamel: melt butter over medium heat; whisk in flour and cook 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk; cook stirring until thick, 4 minutes. Stir in nutmeg and mustard; season with salt.

Preheat broiler. Spread bechamel on all bread slices. Place 4 slices béchamel-side up on a baking sheet; top with ham and half the Gruyere. Cover with remaining bread bechamel-side up; top with more bechamel and remaining Gruyere.
Broil 4-5 minutes until cheese is bubbling and golden.
Fry eggs in olive oil to desired doneness.
Top each sandwich with a fried egg; garnish with parsley.

name: Italian Sausage and Pepper Frittata
description: Hearty oven-finished frittata packed with Italian sausage, roasted peppers, onions, and provolone.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Whisk eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a bowl; stir in 3/4 cup provolone.
Cook sausage in an oven-safe 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, breaking into crumbles, until browned, 5-6 minutes. Remove; pour off excess fat, leaving 1 tbsp.
Sauté peppers and onion in the same pan 5 minutes; add garlic and cook 1 minute. Return sausage to pan.
Pour egg mixture over sausage and vegetables; cook without stirring until edges start to set, 4-5 minutes. Sprinkle remaining provolone.
Transfer to oven; bake 18-22 minutes until puffed and set. Rest 5 minutes; slice into wedges.

name: Corned Beef Hash
description: Crispy-edged cast iron hash of corned beef and Yukon gold potatoes topped with jammy eggs.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Boil diced potatoes in salted water 6-8 minutes until just tender; drain well.
Heat butter and oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion; cook 4 minutes until softened.
Add potatoes in a single layer; cook undisturbed 5-6 minutes until a crispy crust forms on the bottom.
Add corned beef, garlic, Worcestershire, and paprika; stir and press down. Cook another 8-10 minutes, flipping occasionally, until deeply browned and crispy. Season with salt and pepper.
Make 4 wells; crack eggs in each. Cover and cook 3-4 minutes to desired doneness.
Top with chives and serve from the skillet.

name: Sweet Potato Hash with Eggs
description: Smoky sweet potato and red onion hash with crispy edges, finished with baked eggs and avocado.
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes peeled and diced small
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Toss sweet potatoes, red onion, bell pepper, and garlic with olive oil, paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a large cast iron skillet or sheet pan.
Roast 20-22 minutes until tender and edges are caramelized, stirring once halfway.
Make 4 wells in the hash; crack an egg into each. Return to oven 5-7 minutes until egg whites are set.
Top with sliced avocado, fresh cilantro, and hot sauce. Serve immediately.

name: Migas
description: Scrambled eggs folded with crispy fried tortilla strips, peppers, and Monterey Jack for a Tex-Mex dinner.
ingredients: salsa and hot sauce for serving
instructions: Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat; add tortilla strips and fry 4-5 minutes until crisp, turning occasionally. Remove to paper towels and season with salt.
In the same pan over medium heat, cook jalapeno, bell pepper, and onion 4 minutes until softened. Add tomato and cook 1 minute.
Season eggs with salt and pepper; reduce heat to medium-low. Add crispy tortillas back to pan; pour eggs over. Cook, gently folding, 2-3 minutes until just set. Remove from heat; fold in cheese.
Serve immediately topped with avocado, salsa, cilantro, and hot sauce.

name: Savory Crepes with Ham and Gruyere
description: Delicate French crepes folded around sliced ham and melted Gruyere with a light Dijon bechamel.
ingredients: 2 tbsp unsalted butter melted plus more for pan
instructions: Make crepe batter: blend flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, and salt until smooth. Rest 30 minutes.
Cook crepes in a lightly buttered 8-inch skillet over medium heat, 1-2 minutes per side until just golden. Stack on a plate.
Make bechamel: melt butter, whisk in flour, cook 1 minute; gradually add milk whisking constantly until smooth and thick. Stir in mustard and nutmeg; season.
Lay a crepe flat; spread with a thin layer of bechamel, add a slice of ham, and sprinkle Gruyere. Fold into quarters.
Arrange filled crepes in a buttered baking dish; top with remaining bechamel and Gruyere. Broil 4-5 minutes until golden.
Garnish with chives and serve.

name: Cheese Blintzes
description: Pan-fried crepe rolls stuffed with sweetened ricotta and cream cheese, served with sour cream and jam.
ingredients: sour cream and fruit jam for serving
instructions: Blend milk, flour, eggs, 2 tbsp melted butter, sugar, and salt until smooth; rest 30 minutes or refrigerate overnight.
Cook thin crepes in a buttered 8-inch pan over medium-high heat, one side only, 1 minute each. Stack cooked-side up.
Make filling: beat ricotta, cream cheese, sugar, egg yolk, vanilla, and lemon zest until smooth.
Place 3 tbsp filling near bottom edge of each crepe (cooked-side up); fold bottom up, fold sides in, and roll up.
Heat remaining butter over medium heat; fry blintzes seam-side down in batches 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Serve hot with sour cream and fruit jam.

name: Huevos Divorciados
description: Two fried eggs on crispy tortillas each sauced with a different salsa — red chile and green tomatillo.
ingredients: 3 dried guajillo chiles stemmed and seeded
2 tbsp vegetable oil plus more for tortillas
instructions: Make red salsa: toast guajillo chiles in dry pan 30 seconds; soak in hot water 15 minutes. Blend with tomatoes, half the onion, and 2 garlic cloves; simmer in 1 tsp oil 8 minutes. Season.
Make green salsa: broil tomatillos, serranos, remaining onion, and garlic 8-10 minutes until charred. Blend with cilantro and lime juice; season.
Heat 1/4-inch oil in a skillet; fry tortillas 30 seconds per side until crispy. Drain.
Fry eggs in oil to desired doneness.
Spread each tortilla with refried beans; place one egg on each. Pour red salsa over 4 eggs and green salsa over the other 4.
Top with cotija; serve immediately.

name: Classic Roast Turkey
description: A perfectly golden whole roasted turkey with herb butter under the skin and pan drippings for gravy.
instructions: Remove turkey from refrigerator 1 hour before roasting and pat dry.
Preheat oven to 325°F. Mix butter with garlic, thyme, rosemary, sage, salt and pepper.
Loosen skin over breast and thighs; rub herb butter underneath and all over outside.
Stuff cavity with onion and lemon. Truss legs with kitchen twine.
Place breast-side up on a rack in a roasting pan. Pour stock into pan bottom.
Roast 13-15 minutes per pound, basting every 45 minutes, until thigh registers 165°F, about 3 hours.
Tent loosely with foil and rest 30 minutes before carving.

name: Spatchcocked Thanksgiving Turkey
description: Butterflied turkey roasted at high heat for ultra-crispy skin and juicy meat in just 80 minutes.
instructions: Using kitchen shears, cut along both sides of backbone and remove. Flip turkey breast-side up and press firmly on breastbone to flatten.
Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil; scatter two-thirds of onions, carrots, celery and thyme on bottom. Place a wire rack on top.
Rub turkey all over and under skin with oil; season liberally with salt and pepper. Tuck wing tips underneath. Place turkey on rack.
Roast until breast registers 150°F and thighs 165°F, about 80 minutes.
While turkey roasts, make gravy: simmer backbone with remaining vegetables and stock 45 minutes; strain. Make roux with butter and flour, whisk in strained stock; simmer until thickened.
Rest turkey 20 minutes, then carve and serve with gravy.

name: Turkey Gravy from Drippings
description: Rich and silky turkey gravy made from pan drippings and a fortified broth with neck and giblets.
ingredients: kosher salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Chop turkey neck and giblets into 1-inch pieces. Heat oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat and brown turkey parts, 5-7 minutes.
Add onion, carrots and celery; cook 5 minutes until softened. Add stock, soy sauce, thyme and bay leaves; bring to a boil then simmer 45 minutes.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh strainer; discard solids. Skim off fat.
In a separate saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Add flour and whisk constantly until golden brown, about 3 minutes.
Slowly whisk in strained broth in a thin stream until fully incorporated. Bring to a boil then simmer until thickened, about 15 minutes.
Stir in any pan drippings from roasted turkey; season with salt and pepper and keep warm until serving.

name: Classic Herb Stuffing
description: Traditional bread stuffing with celery, onion and fresh sage for the ultimate Thanksgiving side dish.
ingredients: 1 lb day-old white bread cut into 1-inch cubes
instructions: Preheat oven to 275°F. Spread bread cubes on two rimmed baking sheets; bake until dried, about 50 minutes. Let cool. Increase oven to 350°F.
Melt butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add onion, celery and garlic; cook until softened, about 10 minutes. Add sage and thyme; cook 1 minute more.
Whisk together stock, eggs and parsley. Combine with bread cubes and sautéed vegetables; toss until evenly mixed.
Transfer to a buttered 9x13-inch baking dish. Cover tightly with foil and bake until internal temperature reaches 150°F, about 45 minutes.
Remove foil and continue baking until top is golden and crisp, 15-20 minutes. Let cool 5 minutes and serve.

name: Cranberry Orange Sauce
description: Bright and tangy homemade cranberry sauce with fresh orange juice and zest.
instructions: Combine sugars, orange juice and water in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Add cranberries and cinnamon stick. Bring to a boil then reduce heat to a simmer.
Cook stirring occasionally until berries burst and sauce thickens, about 12-15 minutes. Mash any remaining whole berries against side of pan.
Remove cinnamon stick. Stir in orange zest and vanilla extract.
Transfer to a bowl and let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving; sauce thickens as it chills.

name: Sweet Potato Casserole with Marshmallows
description: Creamy mashed sweet potatoes topped with toasted marshmallows and a buttery pecan streusel.
ingredients: 3 lb sweet potatoes peeled and cubed
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Boil sweet potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Drain.
Mash sweet potatoes; stir in brown sugar, melted butter, milk, eggs, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until smooth. Spread into a greased 9x13-inch baking dish.
Combine chopped pecans, flour and cold butter; work together with fingers until crumbly. Sprinkle pecan streusel over sweet potatoes.
Bake 25 minutes until set and topping is lightly golden.
Remove from oven; top with mini marshmallows. Return to oven and bake 5-8 minutes more until marshmallows are puffed and golden.
Let cool 5 minutes before serving.

name: Fancy Green Bean Casserole
description: Elevated homemade green bean casserole with fresh mushroom cream sauce and crispy fried shallots.
ingredients: kosher salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Fry sliced shallots in oil over medium heat, stirring, until deep golden brown. Remove with slotted spoon to paper towels; season with salt. Reserve 2 tbsp shallot oil.
Blanch green beans in boiling salted water 3-4 minutes; transfer immediately to ice water. Drain and set aside.
Heat shallot oil and 2 tbsp butter in a large oven-safe skillet over high heat. Add mushrooms; cook until dry and caramelized, about 10 minutes. Reduce heat; add garlic and flour; cook 2 minutes.
Whisk in stock, cream, soy sauce and lemon juice. Simmer until thickened, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Preheat oven to 375°F. Fold blanched green beans and half the fried shallots into mushroom sauce. Bake 20-25 minutes until bubbling.
Top with remaining fried shallots and serve immediately.

name: Pecan Pie
description: A classic Southern pecan pie with a gooey brown sugar filling and buttery pastry crust.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F with rack in lowest position.
Whisk together eggs, corn syrup, brown sugar, melted butter, vanilla, salt and rye whiskey if using in a large bowl until smooth.
Stir in pecan halves. Pour filling into unbaked pie shell.
Bake on lowest rack until filling is set around edges but center barely jiggles, 40-45 minutes; tent with foil if crust browns too quickly.
Transfer to a wire rack and cool completely, at least 2 hours, before slicing. Serve at room temperature or slightly warmed with whipped cream.

name: Classic Pumpkin Pie
description: Silky spiced pumpkin pie in a flaky crust — the definitive Thanksgiving dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Beat eggs and pumpkin puree together in a large bowl. Combine sugar, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, nutmeg and salt; stir into pumpkin mixture.
Gradually stir in evaporated milk until smooth. Pour into unbaked pie shell; fill only 3/4 full.
Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350°F and bake until center is nearly set and a knife inserted near center comes out mostly clean, 40-50 minutes more.
Cool completely on a wire rack at least 2 hours. Refrigerate until serving. Serve with whipped cream.

name: Prime Rib Roast
description: A majestic slow-roasted standing rib roast with a golden herb crust — the Christmas dinner centerpiece.
instructions: Season roast generously all over with salt; refrigerate uncovered on a rack overnight.
Remove from refrigerator 2 hours before cooking. Preheat oven to 250°F. Mix pepper, garlic powder, rosemary, thyme and olive oil; rub all over roast.
Place roast bone-side down on a rack in a roasting pan with halved garlic head and thyme. Roast until center registers 120°F for rare to medium-rare, 3-4 hours.
Remove from oven; tent loosely with foil. Rest at least 30 minutes (up to 1.5 hours).
Increase oven to 500°F. Uncover roast and sear 5-10 minutes until deeply browned and crusted.
Carve along ribs and slice; serve immediately with horseradish cream.

name: Beef Wellington
description: Tender beef tenderloin wrapped in mushroom duxelles and prosciutto in golden puff pastry.
instructions: Season tenderloin with salt and pepper; sear in an oiled hot skillet on all sides until browned, 2 minutes per side. Brush all over with Dijon mustard; chill 20 minutes.
Cook mushrooms, shallots and garlic in butter over medium heat adding sherry gradually until completely dry and caramelized, 30-40 minutes. Stir in thyme; cool completely.
Lay overlapping slices of prosciutto on plastic wrap; spread mushroom duxelles evenly. Place tenderloin at edge and roll tightly into a log; refrigerate 30 minutes.
Roll out puff pastry; unwrap tenderloin roll and place on pastry. Wrap tightly sealing seam with egg wash; refrigerate 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 425°F. Brush pastry with egg wash; score decoratively. Bake until pastry is deep golden and internal temperature is 125°F, 25-30 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing into 1-inch portions and serving immediately.

name: Honey-Glazed Spiral Ham
description: A showstopping holiday ham lacquered with a sticky honey, brown sugar and mustard glaze.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F. Line a roasting pan with foil; place ham cut-side down in pan.
Make glaze: melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat; whisk in honey, brown sugar, mustard, pineapple juice, garlic powder and paprika. Simmer 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened.
Brush one-third of glaze over ham. Cover pan tightly with foil and bake for 1.5 hours.
Uncover; increase oven to 425°F. Brush with half the remaining glaze; bake 15 minutes. Brush with remaining glaze; bake 10-15 minutes more until caramelized and sticky.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing and serving with pan juices.

name: Yorkshire Pudding
description: Dramatic sky-high popovers made from a rested egg batter cooked in sizzling hot beef drippings.
instructions: Combine eggs, flour, milk, water and salt in a bowl; whisk until completely smooth. Transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate overnight or up to 3 days.
Remove batter from refrigerator while preheating oven to 450°F.
Divide beef dripping evenly among a 12-cup muffin tin or six individual popover molds. Place in oven until fat is smoking hot, about 10 minutes.
Working quickly, divide batter evenly among cups filling each about half full. Immediately return to oven.
Bake without opening the oven until puddings have risen, turned deep brown all over and sound hollow when tapped, about 15-18 minutes.
Serve immediately alongside prime rib roast.

name: Sugar Cookies with Royal Icing
description: Classic buttery sugar cookies decorated with smooth royal icing in festive holiday designs.
instructions: Whisk flour, baking powder and salt. Beat butter and sugar until fluffy; add egg, vanilla and milk. Stir in flour mixture until just combined.
Divide dough in half; flatten into discs. Wrap and refrigerate 1-2 hours until firm.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Roll dough to 1/4-inch thickness; cut into desired shapes. Chill cut shapes on baking sheets for 15 minutes.
Bake until edges are set and bottom is just barely golden, 10-12 minutes. Cool completely on a wire rack.

Make royal icing: beat egg whites and cream of tartar to soft peaks; gradually add powdered sugar until thick and glossy. Thin with water 1 tsp at a time for flooding consistency. Divide and color as desired.
Pipe outlines, flood with thinned icing and let set 1-2 hours before stacking.

name: Mulled Wine
description: A warming pot of red wine mulled with citrus, cinnamon, cloves and star anise for Christmas parties.
instructions: Combine wine, orange slices, cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise, cardamom and brandy in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer stirring occasionally (do not boil or you will burn off the alcohol).
Reduce heat to medium-low; cook 10 minutes until fragrant and flavors have melded.
Stir in honey to taste; add more for a sweeter wine.
Ladle into mugs through a fine-mesh strainer to catch spices. Garnish with fresh orange slices and a cinnamon stick.

name: Easter Roast Leg of Lamb
description: Garlic and rosemary studded leg of lamb roasted to a blushing pink medium-rare for Easter Sunday.
instructions: Using a sharp knife, make small incisions all over the lamb. Insert a slice of garlic and a small sprig of rosemary into each slit.
Mix mustard, olive oil, thyme, salt and pepper. Rub all over the lamb. Let marinate at room temperature 1 hour or refrigerate overnight.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Place baby potatoes in a large roasting pan; drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Set lamb on top of potatoes.
Squeeze lemon over lamb. Roast until thickest part registers 135°F for medium about 1.5 hours.
Rest lamb on a carving board 20 minutes. Carve and serve over potatoes with pan juices.

name: Easter Deviled Eggs
description: Classic deviled eggs with a creamy mustard filling piped high and dusted with smoked paprika.
ingredients: kosher salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Place eggs in a steamer basket over 1 inch of boiling water. Cover and steam 12 minutes. Transfer immediately to an ice bath; cool 15 minutes then peel.
Halve eggs lengthwise; pop yolks into a food processor. Set aside 24 of the best-looking white halves.
Add mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar and hot sauce to yolks; process until smooth. With machine running, drizzle in olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Transfer filling to a zip-lock bag; snip corner. Pipe filling generously into egg white halves.
Garnish with a dusting of smoked paprika, a crack of black pepper and fresh chives. Refrigerate until serving.

name: Hot Cross Buns
description: Lightly spiced enriched yeast buns studded with raisins and currants and marked with iced crosses.
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, yeast, cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg and salt. Add warm milk, 2 whole eggs plus 1 yolk (reserve the white) and butter; knead with a mixer 8-10 minutes until dough is soft and elastic.
Mix in raisins and currants. Cover and let rise 1 hour until puffy.
Grease a 9x13 pan. Divide dough into 14 equal pieces; roll into balls and arrange in pan touching. Cover and rise 1 hour until puffed together. Preheat oven to 375°F.
Whisk reserved egg white with 1 tbsp milk; brush over buns. Bake 20 minutes until golden brown. Cool completely on a rack.
Mix powdered sugar with 2 tbsp milk until thick. Pipe or drizzle a cross on each bun.

name: Easter Carrot Cake
description: A moist spiced carrot cake with toasted walnuts and a tangy cream cheese frosting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour two 9-inch round cake pans. Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, spices and salt in a bowl.
Whisk eggs and sugar vigorously until pale; whisk in oil and vanilla. Fold in flour mixture until just combined. Fold in grated carrots and walnuts.
Divide batter evenly between prepared pans. Bake 30-35 minutes until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool in pans 10 minutes; turn out and cool completely.
Make frosting: beat cream cheese and butter together until smooth. Gradually add powdered sugar; beat until fluffy and smooth.
Place one cake layer on a plate; spread with one-third of frosting. Top with second layer; frost top and sides. Refrigerate 30 minutes to set before slicing.

name: Hoppin John Black-Eyed Peas
description: Southern New Year's black-eyed peas braised with a ham hock over white rice for good luck.
ingredients: 1 lb dried black-eyed peas soaked overnight and rinsed
kosher salt and black pepper to taste
white or brown rice for serving
instructions: Heat butter in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add onion, bell pepper, celery and garlic; cook 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add drained black-eyed peas, ham hock, chicken broth, cayenne, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil then reduce heat to a simmer.
Cover and cook 45-60 minutes until peas are creamy and tender, adding more broth if too thick.
Stir in apple cider vinegar; taste and adjust seasoning. Remove ham hock; pull off any meat and return to pot.
Serve over cooked white rice ladling plenty of cooking liquid over the top. Garnish with sliced green onions.

name: Champagne Risotto
description: Elegant creamy risotto made with Champagne and finished with Parmesan for New Year's Eve.
ingredients: 2 cups Champagne or dry sparkling wine
4 cups warm chicken or vegetable broth
kosher salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Warm broth in a small saucepan; keep at a bare simmer. Melt 2 tbsp butter in a wide heavy saucepan over medium heat. Sauté shallots until softened, 2-3 minutes; do not brown.
Add rice; stir to coat and toast for 2 minutes until edges turn translucent.
Add 1 cup Champagne; let bubble and evaporate stirring constantly. Add remaining Champagne; let evaporate again.
Add broth one ladleful at a time stirring and allowing each addition to absorb before adding more, about 18-20 minutes total until rice is al dente.
Remove from heat; stir in remaining 2 tbsp butter, heavy cream and Parmesan vigorously until creamy and saucy. Season with salt and white pepper.
Serve immediately in warm bowls; garnish with chives.

name: 4th of July Baby Back Ribs
description: Slow-cooked picnic-style baby back ribs with a smoky dry rub and sticky BBQ glaze.
ingredients: 2 racks baby back ribs (about 4 lb total)
instructions: Mix brown sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper and cayenne. Remove membrane from back of ribs by peeling with paper towel. Rub generously all over ribs; let sit 1 hour at room temperature or refrigerate overnight.
Preheat oven to 275°F. Wrap each rack tightly in foil; place on baking sheets. Bake low and slow for 3-3.5 hours until meat begins to pull away from bones.
Remove from oven; unwrap carefully. Transfer ribs to a foil-lined baking sheet.
Mix BBQ sauce with apple cider vinegar. Brush ribs generously with sauce.
Increase oven to 400°F or fire up a grill; cook ribs uncovered 20-30 minutes basting every 10 minutes until sauce is sticky and caramelized.
Rest 10 minutes; cut between bones to serve.

name: Watermelon Feta Salad
description: Refreshing summer salad of sweet watermelon, salty feta, cucumber and fresh mint with a honey-lime dressing.
instructions: Cut watermelon into 1-inch cubes and place in a large shallow serving bowl or platter. Add cucumber cubes and scatter mint and basil leaves over.
Whisk together honey, lime juice, olive oil and a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Drizzle dressing over salad; toss gently to combine.
Scatter crumbled feta all over the top. Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 1 hour.
